prs.title: Fix state_group enum usage in FPG parameter indexing
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a bug where three variables were using `state_group` (EnumArray) instead of `state_group_str` (string array) when indexing Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG) parameters. This caused errors in the production simulation API.

### The Error

Users encountered the following error when running simulations:
```
Error computing household_net_income_including_health_benefits for your household: 
Invalid value(s) ['CA'] for enum StateGroup. Valid values are: ['CONTIGUOUS_US', 'AK', 'HI', 'GU', 'PR', 'VI']
```

### Root Cause

The issue stems from a recent change in `policyengine-core` (around 2025-12-03) that made enum validation stricter:

> "Invalid enum values now raise ValueError instead of logging a warning and returning index 0. This prevents silent data corruption when incorrect enum strings are passed to simulations."

Previously, policyengine-core would silently coerce invalid enum values by returning index 0 (the first enum value). This masked bugs where the wrong variable type was being used for parameter indexing. With the stricter validation, these latent bugs are now surfacing as errors.

### The Fix

Changed three locations to use `state_group_str` instead of `state_group`:

| File | Line |
|------|------|
| `ky_family_size_tax_credit_rate.py` | 19 |
| `wv_low_income_family_tax_credit_fpg.py` | 19 |
| `repeal_state_dependent_exemptions.py` | 423 |

### Why This Matters

- `state_group` returns an `EnumArray` with enum objects like `StateGroup.CONTIGUOUS_US`
- `state_group_str` returns a string array like `['CONTIGUOUS_US']`
- FPG parameters are indexed by string keys (`CONTIGUOUS_US`, `AK`, `HI`, etc.)
- When passing an `EnumArray` to parameter indexing, the new stricter validation in policyengine-core can reject it

### Test Updates

Updated tests to derive `state_group` from `state_code` rather than explicitly setting it, ensuring the full code path is exercised and similar bugs don't go undetected.

## Request for Review

**I'm not 100% sure if this is a complete fix.** I would appreciate insight from those who worked on the recent enum validation changes in `policyengine-core` to confirm:

1. Is using `state_group_str` (string array) the correct approach for parameter indexing?
2. Are there other places in the codebase that might have similar issues?
3. Should `EnumArray` types work with parameter indexing, or is converting to strings the expected pattern?

## Test Plan

- [x] Run `policyengine-core test` on `ky_family_size_tax_credit_rate.yaml` - 4 passed
- [x] Run `policyengine-core test` on `wv_low_income_family_tax_credit_fpg.yaml` - 4 passed  
- [x] Run `policyengine-core test` on `repeal_state_dependent_exemptions.yaml` - 5 passed
- [ ] Verify fix resolves production API errors

reviews.title: Add monorepo structure with design system and app split
reviews.body:
## Summary

This PR implements a monorepo architecture that splits the PolicyEngine app into two separate deployable applications:

- **Website** (`policyengine.org`) - Homepage, blog/research, team, donate pages
- **Calculator** (`app.policyengine.org`) - Interactive policy simulator, household builder, reports

### Key Changes

#### Architecture
- **Separate entry points**: `main.website.tsx` and `main.calculator.tsx`
- **Separate routers**: `WebsiteRouter.tsx` and `CalculatorRouter.tsx`
- **Separate HTML files**: `website.html` and `calculator.html`
- **Build-time app selection**: `VITE_APP_MODE` env var controls which app is built

#### Cross-App Navigation
- Added `WEBSITE_URL` and `CALCULATOR_URL` constants in `src/constants/index.ts`
- Environment-aware URLs (relative in dev, absolute in prod)
- Updated `HeaderLogo` to navigate from calculator → website homepage

#### Vercel Configuration
- Root `vercel.json` for website (`VITE_APP_MODE=website`)
- `calculator/vercel.json` for calculator app (`VITE_APP_MODE=calculator`)
- Proper rewrites to serve SPA from correct HTML entry point

### Files Changed

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `calculator/vercel.json` | Vercel config for calculator project |
| `vercel.json` | Vercel config for website project |
| `app/vite.config.mjs` | Build config with app mode selection |
| `app/src/main.website.tsx` | Website entry point |
| `app/src/main.calculator.tsx` | Calculator entry point |
| `app/src/WebsiteApp.tsx` | Website app component |
| `app/src/CalculatorApp.tsx` | Calculator app component |
| `app/src/WebsiteRouter.tsx` | Website routes |
| `app/src/CalculatorRouter.tsx` | Calculator routes |
| `app/src/constants/index.ts` | Cross-app URL constants |
| `app/src/components/homeHeader/HeaderLogo.tsx` | Fixed to use anchor for cross-app nav |

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Preview deployments tested for both apps
- [x] Cross-app navigation works (website → calculator, calculator → website)
- [x] HeaderLogo tests updated and passing
- [x] `policyengine-calculator` Vercel project Root Directory set to `calculator`

## Post-Merge Steps

1. Verify both Vercel projects trigger production deployments
2. Test production URLs:
   - `https://policyengine.org/us` loads website homepage
   - `https://app.policyengine.org/us` loads calculator dashboard
3. Test cross-app navigation in production

## Expected Outcome

After merge:
- `policyengine.org` serves the Website app (homepage, research, team, etc.)
- `app.policyengine.org` serves the Calculator app (dashboard, reports, simulations, etc.)
- Logo click in calculator navigates to website homepage
- "Calculate my taxes" buttons in website navigate to calculator

## Architecture Diagram

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Monorepo Root                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    │                           │
        ┌───────────┴───────────┐   ┌───────────┴───────────┐
        ▼                       │   ▼                       │
┌───────────────────┐           │   ┌───────────────────┐   │
│  policyengine.org │           │   │app.policyengine.org│  │
│  (Website)        │           │   │  (Calculator)      │  │
├───────────────────┤           │   ├───────────────────┤   │
│ vercel.json       │           │   │ calculator/       │   │
│ VITE_APP_MODE=    │           │   │   vercel.json     │   │
│   website         │           │   │ VITE_APP_MODE=    │   │
└───────────────────┘           │   │   calculator      │   │
        │                       │   └───────────────────┘   │
        ▼                       │           │               │
┌───────────────────┐           │           ▼               │
│ website.html      │           │   ┌───────────────────┐   │
│ main.website.tsx  │           │   │ calculator.html   │   │
│ WebsiteApp        │           │   │ main.calculator   │   │
│ WebsiteRouter     │           │   │ CalculatorApp     │   │
└───────────────────┘           │   │ CalculatorRouter  │   │
                                │   └───────────────────┘   │

reviews.title: test: add vercel.json config validation tests
reviews.body:
## Summary
Add tests that validate `app/vercel.json` is correctly configured for SPA routing.

## What broke and why

When implementing social preview support (OG tags), I added a root `vercel.json` to configure API functions. This broke the entire site with 404 errors on all routes because:

1. **Root vercel.json overrides app/vercel.json** - Vercel uses the config file closest to the project root, so my new root config took precedence over the working `app/vercel.json`

2. **Wrong routing config** - I tried various approaches (`rewrites`, `routes` with `handle: filesystem`) but none worked correctly because:
   - The original working config used `{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/" }` in `app/vercel.json`
   - My root config used different patterns and paths that didn't match the outputDirectory setup

3. **SPA routing requires specific config** - For React Router to handle client-side routes, all requests must be rewritten to serve `index.html`. Without this, direct URL access (e.g., refreshing `/uk/research/some-article`) returns 404 because Vercel looks for a literal file at that path.

## Timeline of the incident

| Commit/PR | Description | Impact |
|-----------|-------------|--------|
| [1113ee30](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-app-v2/commit/1113ee30) | Added root `vercel.json` to enable API functions | 🔴 Broke all routes with 404 |
| [0db14439](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-app-v2/commit/0db14439) | Attempted fix: changed rewrite to serve index.html | 🔴 Still broken |
| [#437](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-app-v2/pull/437) | Attempted fix: switched to `routes` with filesystem handler | 🔴 Still broken |
| [#438](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-app-v2/pull/438) | **Fix**: Removed root vercel.json, restored app/vercel.json | ✅ Site working |

## What these tests catch

These tests would have **immediately failed** when the root `vercel.json` was added:

```
✗ given root vercel.json then does NOT exist (app/vercel.json is canonical)
```

And would have caught incorrect rewrite configurations:

```
✗ given vercel.json rewrites then has SPA fallback rule
  Expected: { source: "/(.*)", destination: "/" }
```

## Tests added
1. Verifies `app/vercel.json` exists
2. Verifies it contains valid JSON
3. Verifies it has `rewrites` array
4. Verifies it has the SPA fallback rule `{ source: "/(.*)", destination: "/" }`
5. Verifies no `routes` array (which breaks SPA routing when combined with rewrites)
6. Verifies no root `vercel.json` exists (which caused 404 errors)

## Test plan
- [x] Tests pass locally
- [x] CI passes

reviews.title: Crash in policy creation
reviews.body:
Fixes #383 

Thorough verification required.

RCA (Root Cause Analysis)

  Crash: TypeError: (char || "").match is not a function

  Location: ValueSetter.tsx - in the ValueInputBox component when rendering NumberInput (which uses react-number-format's NumericFormat component internally)

  Root Cause:
  Some parameters (specifically HMRC IncomeTax parameters) have non-numeric values (likely objects, arrays, or other complex types) in their metadata. When a user clicks on
  these parameters in the policy parameter selector, the ValueInputBox component tries to pass these non-numeric values directly to Mantine's NumberInput component.

  The NumberInput uses react-number-format's NumericFormat internally, which expects string or number values. When it receives a non-numeric value, it attempts to call
  .match() on it (for parsing/formatting), which fails because .match() only exists on strings.

  Trigger:
  Clicking on specific parameter leaves in the policy parameter selector tree (HMRC IncomeTax and a few other params) during isolated policy creation flow.

  Fix:
  Added type guard in ValueSetter.tsx line 536-538 to ensure the value passed to NumberInput is always a number:
  const numericValue = typeof value === 'number' ? value : 0;
  const displayValue = isPercentage ? numericValue * 100 : numericValue;

  This prevents non-numeric values from reaching the NumberInput/NumericFormat component.

prs.title: Fix ACA required contribution percentage to be flat below 133% FPL
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #7066

The ACA statute (26 USC 36B) specifies that the contribution percentage for household income "up to 133%" should be **flat** (initial=final=2.1% for 2026), not linearly interpolated. The previous implementation used `np.interp` which incorrectly interpolated from 0% to 133% FPL.

**Before:** At 100% FPL, the rate was incorrectly interpolated  
**After:** At 100% FPL, the rate is 2.1% (flat as statute requires)

## Solution

Refactored the parameter structure to separate thresholds and rates:

- `threshold.yaml` - FPL bracket boundaries
- `initial.yaml` - starting rate for each bracket  
- `final.yaml` - ending rate for each bracket

The formula now finds which bracket income falls into and interpolates between initial and final rates **within that bracket**. For flat brackets (like 0-133%), initial=final so no interpolation occurs.

This is cleaner than the previous "hack" approach and properly matches the IRS table structure with "Initial Premium" and "Final Premium" columns.

## Test plan

- [x] All 22 ACA PTC tests pass
- [x] Verified flat rate at 100% and 120% FPL (2.1%)
- [x] Verified jump to 3.14% at 133% FPL
- [x] Verified ARPA/IRA years (2021-2025) work correctly

prs.title: Add Emergency Medicaid for undocumented immigrants
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements Emergency Medicaid eligibility for individuals who are ineligible for regular Medicaid due to immigration status but meet all other Medicaid eligibility requirements and have an emergency medical condition.

Closes #7003

## Regulatory Authority

This implementation is based on:

- **42 USC 1396b(v)(2)** - Exception for emergency services for aliens
  - (v)(2)(A): Person is not otherwise eligible due to immigration status
  - (v)(2)(B): Person meets all applicable Medicaid eligibility requirements except immigration status
  - (v)(2)(C): Organ transplant procedures are excluded
- **42 USC 1396b(v)(3)** - Definition of emergency medical condition
- **8 USC 1611(b)(1)(A)** - Exception for emergency medical care from public benefits restrictions
- **42 CFR 440.255** - Federal regulations on emergency services
- **42 CFR 435.406** - Citizenship and noncitizen eligibility

## Eligibility Requirements

Per the statute, Emergency Medicaid eligibility requires **all three** conditions:

1. **Immigration Status**: Person is NOT eligible for regular Medicaid due to immigration status (uses existing `is_medicaid_immigration_status_eligible` variable)
2. **Medicaid Requirements**: Person meets all other Medicaid eligibility requirements including income and categorical eligibility (uses existing `medicaid_category` variable)
3. **Emergency Condition**: Person has an emergency medical condition as defined in 42 USC 1396b(v)(3)

## Files Added

### Parameters (5 files)
```
policyengine_us/parameters/gov/hhs/medicaid/emergency_medicaid/
├── index.yaml                        # Metadata (economy: false, household: false)
├── enabled.yaml                      # Program enabled from 1987
├── emergency_condition_definition.yaml  # Statutory definition criteria
├── organ_transplant_exclusion.yaml   # Organ transplant exclusion per (v)(2)(C)
└── uses_medicaid_income_thresholds.yaml  # Income threshold requirement
```

### Variables (2 files)
```
policyengine_us/variables/gov/hhs/medicaid/emergency_medicaid/
├── has_emergency_medical_condition.py   # Input variable (boolean)
└── is_emergency_medicaid_eligible.py    # Eligibility calculation
```

### Tests (3 files, 57 test cases)
```
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/hhs/medicaid/emergency_medicaid/
├── has_emergency_medical_condition.yaml  # 3 unit tests
├── is_emergency_medicaid_eligible.yaml   # 34 unit tests
└── integration.yaml                      # 20 integration tests
```

## Test Coverage (57 tests)

| Test Category | Count | Description |
|--------------|-------|-------------|
| Unit tests - eligible cases | 12 | All immigration statuses and Medicaid categories |
| Unit tests - ineligible (regular Medicaid) | 8 | Citizens, LPRs, refugees, asylees |
| Unit tests - no emergency | 2 | Missing emergency condition |
| Unit tests - no Medicaid category | 3 | Income too high |
| Unit tests - edge cases | 9 | Pre-1987, condition combinations |
| Integration tests | 20 | Full pipeline with household structures |
| Input variable tests | 3 | has_emergency_medical_condition |

## Example Calculation

**Scenario**: Undocumented adult (age 35) with emergency medical condition and $18,000 income

1. `is_medicaid_immigration_status_eligible`: false (undocumented)
2. `medicaid_category`: ADULT (income < 138% FPL in expansion state)
3. `has_emergency_medical_condition`: true

**Result**: `is_emergency_medicaid_eligible` = true

Formula: `enabled & has_emergency & (medicaid_category != NONE) & ~immigration_eligible`

## Implementation Notes

- Uses existing `medicaid_category` variable which handles all income/categorical eligibility checks
- Uses existing `is_medicaid_immigration_status_eligible` variable for immigration status
- `has_emergency_medical_condition` is an input variable (boolean) since emergency conditions are determined by medical providers, not calculated
- Program enabled starting 1987 (OBRA '86 created Emergency Medicaid)
- Parameters marked with `economy: false` and `household: false` since this is person-level eligibility

## References

- [42 USC 1396b(v)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396b#v) - Emergency services exception
- [8 USC 1611(b)(1)(A)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/8/1611#b_1_A) - Emergency medical care exception
- [42 CFR 440.255](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/440.255) - Emergency services regulations
- [42 CFR 435.406](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/435.406) - Noncitizen eligibility

prs.title: Medicare savings program
prs.body:
Fixes #6893

## Summary

This PR corrects the Medicare Savings Program (MSP) implementation to align with federal statutory requirements. Key fixes:

1. **FPL Unit Size**: Uses individual/couple FPL instead of SPM unit size
2. **Income Methodology**: Applies SSI income exclusions per statutory requirement
3. **Parameter Updates**: Adds historical values and proper legal citations

---

## FPL Unit Size Fix

**Legal References**:
- [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - Income "determined under section 1382a" (SSI methodology)
- [SSA POMS SI 01715.010](https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501715010) - Specifies "individual" and "couple" resource limits

**Rationale**: MSP follows SSI methodology, which uses individual or eligible couple as the unit. SSI does not include children or other household members in the income/resource unit. Medicare.gov also publishes limits only for "Individual" and "Married couple" categories.

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `spm_unit_fpg` which calculated FPL based on the full SPM unit size (could be 3, 4, 5+ people).

**Fix**: Created `msp_fpg` variable that returns:
- Individual FPL (1 person) if unmarried
- Couple FPL (2 persons) if married

---

## Income Methodology Fix

**Legal Reference**: [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - "income (determined under section 1382a of this title)"

Section 1382a is the SSI income determination methodology ([42 U.S.C. § 1382a](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1382a)), which requires:
1. $20 general income exclusion (from unearned first)
2. $65 earned income exclusion
3. 50% of remaining earned income excluded

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `adjusted_gross_income_person` without any exclusions.

**Fix**: Updated `msp_countable_income` to use SSI income variables and apply the `_apply_ssi_exclusions()` function.

---

## Published Limits vs Our Approach

Medicare.gov publishes income limits that are approximately $20/month higher than raw FPL thresholds. This is because they include the $20 general exclusion in the threshold.

Our implementation applies the $20 exclusion to income instead:
- **Our approach**: `(income - $20) <= FPL`
- **Published approach**: `income <= (FPL + $20)`

These are mathematically equivalent.

---

## Income Limit Legal Citations

| Category | FPL % | Legal Reference |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| QMB | 100% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(i)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_i), [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)-(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) |
| SLMB | 120% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iii)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iii) |
| QI | 135% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iv)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iv) |

---

## Test Plan

- [x] All 19 MSP tests pass
- [x] Unit tests for `msp_fpg`, `msp_category`, `msp_eligible`, `msp_benefit_value`
- [x] Integration tests for complete eligibility pipeline
- [x] Tests document calculation methodology with inline comments

## Summary

Implements Illinois Medicaid Presumptive Eligibility (MPE) for pregnant women per [89 Ill. Admin. Code § 120.66](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/Ill-Admin-Code-tit-89-SS-120.66).

MPE provides temporary ambulatory prenatal care coverage to pregnant women while their full Medicaid application is processed. The program's purpose is to "encourage early and continuous prenatal care of low income pregnant women who otherwise may postpone or do without that care."

- Income limit: 200% FPL (using MAGI methodology per § 120.64)
- Available regardless of citizenship/immigration status
- Household size includes unborn children (via `current_pregnancies`)

### Not Modeled
- "No prior MPE this pregnancy" rule (administrative data, not observable from survey)

Fixes #6786

prs.title: Fix unrealistic SDLT charges causing 224% tax rates in first income decile
prs.body:
**Summary**                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                             
This PR fixes a critical data quality issue where property_purchased defaulted to True for all households, causing every household to be charged Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) as if they had just purchased their property. This resulted in:
  - 224% effective tax rates in the first income decile                                                                                      
  - Negative net incomes for low-income households (e.g., -£40,543 in England)                                                               
  - £370bn total SDLT vs the official £13.9bn (26x too high)                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                             
**Root Cause**                                                                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                             
The property_purchased variable in PolicyEngine UK defaults to True (designed for the web calculator where users model specific purchase scenarios). In microsimulation, this caused all 32.5 million households to be charged SDLT on their full property value annually.
                                                                                                                                             
**Fix**                                                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                             
  Set property_purchased stochastically based on actual UK housing transaction rates:                                                        
  - Rate: 3.85% (1.1m transactions / 28.6m households)                                                                                       
  - Sources:                                                                                                                                 
    - https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/monthly-property-transactions-completed-in-the-uk-with-value-40000-or-above                   
    - https://www.ons.gov.uk/peoplepopulationandcommunity/birthsdeathsandmarriages/families/bulletins/familiesandhouseholds/2024             
                                                                                                                                             
  **Verification**                                                                                                                               
                                                                                                                                             
  | Metric        | Before Fix | After Fix | Official |                                                                                      
  |---------------|------------|-----------|----------|                                                                                      
  | Total SDLT    | £370.3bn   | £15.7bn   | £13.9bn  |                                                                                      
  | D1 Tax Rate   | 224%       | <100%     | -        |                                                                                      
  | D1 Net Income | -£40,543   | Positive  | -        |                                                                                      
                                                                                                                                             
  Source: https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/uk-stamp-tax-statistics                                                                   
                                                                                                                                             
  **Changes**                                                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                                             
  Modified:                                                                                                                                  
  - policyengine_uk_data/datasets/frs.py - Added stochastic property_purchased generation with documented sources                            
                                                                                                                                             
  Added:                                                                                                                                     
  - policyengine_uk_data/tests/test_property_purchased.py - Tests for:                                                                       
    - Property purchase rate ~3.85%                                                                                                          
    - SDLT total within £5-50bn range (official is £13.9bn)                                                                                  
    - Not all households have property_purchased=True                                                                                        
  - policyengine_uk_data/tests/test_low_income_deciles.py - Tests for:                                                                       
    - First decile tax rate < 100%                                                                                                           
    - First decile average tax < £50k                                                                                                        
    - First decile net income > -£10k                                                                                                        
    - Tax ordering (D1 < D10)                                                                                                                
    - No excessive negative incomes                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                             
  **Test Plan**                                                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                             
  - Verify property_purchased rate is approximately 3.85%                                                                                    
  - Verify total SDLT is in realistic range (£5-50bn)                                                                                        
  - Verify first decile tax rates are below 100%                                                                                             
  - Verify first decile net incomes are not severely negative                                                                                
  - Regenerate enhanced FRS dataset with fix applied

prs.title: Fix OBR fiscal year alignment for tax reforms
prs.body:
**Summary**

  - Align PolicyEngine calculations with OBR fiscal year timing for income source tax reforms
  - Fix student loan threshold parameter format

  **Changes**

  - Student loan thresholds: Use year-only format ("2027") instead of date format ("2027-01-01") to fix parameter parsing
  - Dividend tax: Start baseline modifier from 2027 (not 2026) since OBR fiscal year 2026-27 shows minimal impact for April 2026 start
  - Savings/Property tax: Remove 2027 from baseline, start from 2028 - policies start April 2027 but OBR fiscal year 2027-28 shows £0 static impact

  **Why**

  OBR reports fiscal years (April-March). A policy starting April 2027 falls in fiscal year 2027-28, but our annual calculations query calendar years. The first full calendar year impact is 2028, matching OBR's £0 static estimate for 2027-28 on savings/property tax increases.

prs.title: Fix student loans policy reform
Edit salary sacrifice implementation
prs.body:
**Description**

This PR implements the £2,000 salary sacrifice pension cap from the Autumn Budget 2025, which takes effect from April 2029.

  **Summary**

  - Adds parameter salary_sacrifice_pension_cap (£2,000 from 2029-04-06, infinity before)
  - Excess above cap is redirected to regular employee pension contributions
  - Applies 13% employer haircut on excess (employers spread NI costs across workers)
  - Revenue impact: ~£3.6 billion (NI: £2.0bn, Income Tax: £1.1bn due to pension relief caps)

  **Key changes**

  - New parameter: gov.hmrc.national_insurance.salary_sacrifice_pension_cap
  - New variables: salary_sacrifice_returned_to_income, employee_pension_contributions_reported
  - Modified variables: employment_income (adds excess for NI), employee_pension_contributions (adds excess for
  income tax relief)
  - Simulation: Added input aliasing for employee_pension_contributions →
  employee_pension_contributions_reported

  **Usage**

```
  # Reform (with cap - current law)
  reform = Microsimulation()
```

```
  # Baseline (no cap)
  baseline = Microsimulation(reform={
      "gov.hmrc.national_insurance.salary_sacrifice_pension_cap": {
          "2029": float("inf"),
          "2030": float("inf"),
      }
  })


  revenue = reform.calculate("gov_balance", 2030).sum() - baseline.calculate("gov_balance", 2030).sum()

```

  **Test plan**

  - Revenue impact test (~£3.3bn ± £1.5bn)
  - NI increases with reform (>£1bn)
  - Income tax impact test
  - Excess redirected to pension contributions
  - Employer haircut (13%) applied correctly
  - Affected population (~3.3 million workers)

prs.title: Add owns vehicle variable
prs.body:
Summary

Adds a new owns_vehicle input variable to support calibration of vehicle ownership rates in policyengine-uk-data.

  This addresses https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-uk-data/issues/236, which identified that the  microdata shows 54.1% of households with zero fuel spending, while NTS 2024 data shows only 22% of UK households lack a car - a 32 percentage point gap.

  Changes

  - Added owns_vehicle boolean input variable at household level

  How it works

This is an input variable (no formula). The value will be imputed in policyengine-uk-data based on LCFS fuel spending data (households with petrol/diesel spending are assumed to own a vehicle), then calibrated to NTS 2024 targets (~78% vehicle ownership).

  This approach:
  - Keeps the relationship between vehicle ownership and fuel spending in the data layer, not the tax-benefit system
  - Allows proper calibration/reweighting
  - Handles EVs correctly (they can be assigned owns_vehicle=True without fuel spending)

  References

  - https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/national-travel-survey-2024/nts-2024-household-car-availability-and-trends-in-car-trips
  - https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6781339100e3d719f19217f1/dft-car-ownership-evidence-review.pdf

reviews.title: Add UK microsim guidance
Add the 65+ age heterogeneity to US LSRs
reviews.body:
### Overview

This PR adds empirically grounded **age heterogeneity (65+)** to the US labor supply response (LSR) parameters used in behavioral microsimulation. The implementation follows the **multiplier approach** consistent with CBO (2012) and French (2005), applying an age-based scaling factor to both **substitution** and **income** elasticities for individuals aged 65 and over.

### Implementation

* Introduces `age_multiplier_65_and_over` parameter for both substitution and income elasticities
* Keeps the existing structure (`by_position_and_decile` for substitution; `base` for income)
* Default values remain **0** for base elasticities (no behavioral response) and **2.0** for the 65+ multiplier
* Applies multiplier only when `age >= 65`

### Why a Multiplier Approach (vs. Full Age Breakdown)

1. **Evidence-based**: Literature shows older workers (especially 62–70) have higher labor supply elasticities, mainly on the *extensive* margin. However, no studies provide age-by-income-decile or age-by-earner breakdowns.

2. **Parsimony**: A single multiplier avoids an unnecessary 44-parameter expansion and is easier to calibrate.

3. **Transparency**: Multiplier interpretation is straightforward: "65+ workers are X times more responsive."

4. **Flexibility**: Users can tune the multiplier (e.g., 1.5–3.0 range) or revert to 1.0 for no age effect.

---

### Empirical Basis

#### Substitution Elasticity (after-tax wage responsiveness)

| Study | Population | Age Group | Elasticity | Implied 65+/<65 Multiplier | Margin | Notes |
|-------|------------|-----------|------------|----------------------------|---------|-------|
| **CBO WP 2012-13** (Reichling & Whalen) | US working-age | 25–64 | 0.27–0.53 (central 0.40) | — | Frisch | Baseline for CBO fiscal analysis |
| **French (2005)** *REStud* | Male heads | 40 → 60 | 0.2–0.4 → 1.0–1.3 | **≈ 3.0–3.25×** | Structural | Strong age elasticity increase |
| **Blau & Shvydko (2011)** *JLE* | Mixed | 62–69 | 0.5–0.8 (extensive) / 0.05–0.2 (intensive) | **≈ 2–3×** | Reduced form | Driven by retirement decisions |
| **Coile & Gruber (2007)** *RESTAT* | Mixed | 62–64 | 0.4–0.7 | **≈ 2×** | Extensive | SS incentives near retirement |
| **Gustman & Steinmeier (2009)** *JLE* | Mixed | 65–69 | 0.45–0.8 | **≈ 2–2.5×** | Extensive | Pension/SS interactions |

**Recommended parameters:**

| Type | Base (under 65) | 65+ Multiplier (default) | Range for sensitivity | Source rationale |
|------|-----------------|--------------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| Substitution | 0.3–0.4 | **2.0 ×** | 1.5–3.0 × | CBO (2012), French (2005), Blau & Shvydko (2011) |

---

#### Income Elasticity (disposable income responsiveness)

| Study | Population | Age Group | Elasticity | Implied 65+/<65 Multiplier | Notes |
|-------|------------|-----------|------------|----------------------------|-------|
| **CBO WP 2012-12** (McClelland & Mok) | US working-age | 25–64 | −0.02 to −0.05 (central −0.04) | — | Baseline CBO value |
| **French (2005)** | Male heads | 60+ | −0.06 to −0.08 | **≈ 1.5–2×** | Life-cycle model |
| **Gustman & Steinmeier (2009)** | Mixed | 65+ | −0.07 to −0.10 | **≈ 2×** | Structural retirement |
| **Rogerson & Wallenius (2009)** | Model | — | — | **≈ 1.3–1.5×** | Calibration support |

**Recommended parameters:**

| Type | Base (under 65) | 65+ Multiplier (default) | Range for sensitivity | Source rationale |
|------|-----------------|--------------------------|----------------------|------------------|
| Income | −0.04 | **2.0 ×** | 1.3–2.0 × | CBO (2012), French (2005), Gustman & Steinmeier (2009) |

---

### References

* **CBO (2012-12):** *A Review of Recent Research on Labor Supply Elasticities.* Working Paper by Robert McClelland and Shannon Mok. [Link](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/43675)

* **CBO (2012-13):** *Review of Estimates of the Frisch Elasticity of Labor Supply.* Working Paper by Felix Reichling and Charles Whalen. [Link](https://www.cbo.gov/publication/43676)

* **French (2005):** *The Effects of Health, Wealth, and Wages on Labour Supply and Retirement Behaviour.* Review of Economic Studies 72(2): 395–427. [Link](https://academic.oup.com/restud/article-abstract/72/2/395/1558553)

* **Blau & Shvydko (2011):** *Labor Market Rigidities and the Employment Behavior of Older Workers.* ILR Review 64(3): 464–484. [Link](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/001979391106400303)

* **Coile & Gruber (2007):** *Future Social Security Entitlements and the Retirement Decision.* Review of Economics and Statistics 89(2): 234–246.

* **Gustman & Steinmeier (2009):** *How Changes in Social Security Affect Recent Retirement Trends.* Journal of Labor Economics 27(2): 213–252.

* **Rogerson & Wallenius (2009):** *Micro and Macro Elasticities in a Life Cycle Model with Taxes.* Journal of Economic Theory 144(6): 2277–2292. [Link](https://ideas.repec.org/a/eee/jetheo/v144y2009i6p2277-2292.html)

* **Keane (2011):** *Labor Supply and Taxes: A Survey.* Journal of Economic Literature 49(4): 961–1075. [Link](https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/jel.49.4.961)

reviews.title: Enhance SSN undocumented type imputation
reviews.body:
Fixes #246

# Implement ASEC Undocumented Algorithm ([paper](https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=4662801))

## Algorithm Logic: Process of Elimination

1. **Start**: Assume all foreign-born non-citizens *might* be undocumented (code 0)
2. **Remove**: People with evidence of legal status → move to code 3 ("OTHER_NON_CITIZEN") 
3. **Result**: Those remaining in code 0 have no clear indicators of legal status → likely undocumented

## Target Implementation
Modify the existing `add_ssn_card_type()` function to apply these conditions before the random refinement step, ensuring that people meeting any of these conditions are assigned to code 3 ("OTHER_NON_CITIZEN") rather than potentially remaining as code 0 ("NONE"/undocumented).

## The 14 Conditions

### **Condition 1: Pre-1982 Arrivals**
- **Logic**: Remove those who arrived before 1982 (eligible for IRCA amnesty)
- **Variable**: `PEINUSYR` codes 1-7 (Before 1950 through 1980-1981)

### **Condition 2: Eligible Naturalized Citizens**
- **Logic**: Remove naturalized citizens who meet time/age requirements
- **Variables**: `PRCITSHP == 4`, `A_AGE >= 18`, `PEINUSYR` (for years in US), `A_MARITL`, `A_SPOUSE`

### **Condition 3: Medicare Recipients**
- **Logic**: Remove those with Medicare coverage
- **Variable**: `MCARE == 1`

### **Condition 4: Federal Retirement Benefits**
- **Logic**: Remove those receiving federal government pensions
- **Variables**: `PEN_SC1 == 3` OR `PEN_SC2 == 3` (Federal government pension)

### **Condition 5: Social Security Disability**
- **Logic**: Remove those receiving SS disability benefits
- **Variables**: `RESNSS1 == 2` OR `RESNSS2 == 2` (disabled adult or child)

### **Condition 6: Indian Health Service Coverage**
- **Logic**: Remove those with IHS coverage
- **Variable**: `IHSFLG == 1`

### **Condition 7: Medicaid Recipients** (State-specific adjustments needed)
- **Logic**: Remove Medicaid recipients (with state policy exceptions)
- **Variables**: `CAID == 1`, `GESTFIPS` (for state-specific rules)

### **Condition 8: CHAMPVA Recipients**
- **Logic**: Remove those with CHAMPVA coverage
- **Variable**: `CHAMPVA == 1`

### **Condition 9: Military Health Insurance**
- **Logic**: Remove those with TRICARE/military coverage
- **Variable**: `MIL == 1`

### **Condition 10: Government Employees**
- **Logic**: Remove government workers and military personnel
- **Variables**: `PEIO1COW` codes 1-3 (federal/state/local gov) OR `A_MJOCC == 11` (military)

### **Condition 11: Social Security Recipients**
- **Logic**: Remove those receiving Social Security payments
- **Variable**: `SS_YN == 1`

### **Condition 12: Housing Assistance** (State-specific adjustments needed)
- **Logic**: Remove housing assistance recipients (with mixed-status family exceptions)
- **Variables**: Household-level `HPUBLIC == 1` OR `HLORENT == 1`, `GESTFIPS`

### **Condition 13: Veterans/Military Personnel**
- **Logic**: Remove veterans and active military
- **Variables**: `PEAFEVER == 1` OR `A_MJOCC == 11`

### **Condition 14: SSI Recipients**
- **Logic**: Remove those receiving SSI for themselves (not on behalf of children)
- **Variables**: `SSI_YN == 1`, `RESNSSI1`/`RESNSSI2` (to verify recipient)

issues.title: Calibrate vehicle ownership rates
issues.body:
**Summary**

The PolicyEngine UK microdata shows 54.1% of households with zero fuel spending, but according to NTS 2024 data, only 22% of UK households lack a car. This 32 percentage point gap suggests vehicle ownership is under-represented in the microdata.

**Evidence**

  | Metric                                    | Value  |
  |-------------------------------------------|--------|
  | PolicyEngine: HHs with zero fuel spending | 54.1%  |
  | NTS 2024: HHs with no car                 | 22%    |
  | Gap                                       | ~32 pp |

  EVs don't explain this gap - they represent only ~4% of vehicles (NTS 2024).

  **Impact**

This affects any analysis involving fuel duty, including the Autumn Budget 2025 fuel duty freeze analysis. The "no change" category in winners/losers charts is inflated because vehicle ownership is under-represented.

  **Proposed fix**

Add calibration target for vehicle ownership aligned with NTS data (~78% of households own a car). This would indirectly improve fuel consumption estimates.

**Sources**

  - https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/national-travel-survey-2024/nts-2024-household-car-availability-and-trends-in-car-trips
  - https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6781339100e3d719f19217f1/dft-car-ownership-evidence-review.pdf

**Analysis script**

- https://gist.github.com/vahid-ahmadi/66f5b237735df1e36e043db9573b1548

issues.title: Update the UK lsr functionality
issues.body:
**Problem:**
The UK behavioral response toggle in the PolicyEngine app was not working because the API wasn't calling ```apply_dynamics()``` when behavioral response parameters were present in reforms. This meant that labor supply adjustments were being ignored, and users weren't seeing the intended behavioral effects of policy changes.

**Solution:**
Added automatic detection of behavioral response parameters (```gov.simulation.labor_supply_responses.income_elasticity``` and ```substitution_elasticity```) in the API. When these parameters are present in a UK household calculation request, the API now automatically calls ```simulation.apply_dynamics(year)``` to enable behavioral adjustments before calculating results.

prs.title: Add Alaska TANF program
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements Alaska Temporary Assistance Program (ATAP), Alaska's TANF program, covering income eligibility, deductions, and benefit calculations for **adult-included units** and **pregnant women**.

Closes #7075

---

## Alaska ATAP Income Rules

### Regulatory Authority

- **Alaska Statutes**: [AS 47.27](https://www.akleg.gov/basis/statutes.asp#47.27) - Temporary Assistance
- **Alaska Administrative Code**: [7 AAC 45](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/title-7/part-3/chapter-45) - Public Assistance
- **Program Standards**: [TA-Standards.pdf](http://dpaweb.hss.state.ak.us/POLICY/PDF/TA-Standards.pdf)

---

### 1. INCOME ELIGIBILITY TESTS

#### Gross Income Test (185% Standard)

Total nonexempt gross monthly income must not exceed 185% of the need standard.

Source: [7 AAC 45.520](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.520)

#### Net Income Test (Need Standard)

Countable income (after deductions) must not exceed the need standard.

Source: [7 AAC 45.520](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.520)

#### Resource Test

| Unit Type | Resource Limit |
|-----------|----------------|
| Standard  | $2,000         |
| Elderly (60+) | $3,000     |

Source: [7 AAC 45.280](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.280)

---

### 2. INCOME DEDUCTIONS & EXEMPTIONS

#### A. Work Incentive Deduction

**New Applicants** (not received ATAP in previous 4 months):
- $90 flat deduction only

**Continuing Recipients** (received ATAP within previous 4 months):
- $150 flat deduction + 33% of remaining earnings

**Implementation Note**: Uses `is_tanf_enrolled` to distinguish new applicants ($90) from continuing recipients ($150 + 33%). Tier 1 rate is applied for continuing recipients as PolicyEngine cannot track tier progression across months.

Source: [7 AAC 45.480](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.480)

#### B. Childcare Deduction

| Child Age | Maximum Monthly Disregard |
|-----------|---------------------------|
| Under 2   | $200 per child            |
| 2 and older | $175 per child          |

Source: [7 AAC 45.485](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.485)

#### C. Child Support Passthrough

Recipients may retain up to **$50** of monthly child support payments.

Source: [7 AAC 45.400](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.400)

---

### 3. INCOME STANDARDS BY FAMILY SIZE (2026)

#### Adult-Included Units (One Caretaker + Children)

| Family Size | 185% Standard | Need Standard | Max Payment |
|-------------|---------------|---------------|-------------|
| 2           | $3,529        | $1,908        | $821        |
| 3           | $3,975        | $2,149        | $923        |
| 4           | $4,417        | $2,388        | $1,025      |
| 5           | $4,863        | $2,629        | $1,127      |
| 6           | $5,309        | $2,870        | $1,229      |
| 7           | $5,749        | $3,108        | $1,331      |
| 8           | $6,199        | $3,351        | $1,433      |
| 9+          | +$447         | +$242         | +$102       |

Source: [TA-Standards.pdf](http://dpaweb.hss.state.ak.us/POLICY/PDF/TA-Standards.pdf#page=1)

#### Pregnant Woman (Size 1)

| Year | 185% Standard | Need Standard | Max Payment |
|------|---------------|---------------|-------------|
| 2026 | $2,205        | $1,192        | $514        |

Source: [7 AAC 45.523(a)(3)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.523), [TA-Standards.pdf](http://dpaweb.hss.state.ak.us/POLICY/PDF/TA-Standards.pdf#page=5)

---

### 4. BENEFIT CALCULATION

#### Formula:
```
Benefit = (Need Standard − Countable Income) × (Max Payment ÷ Need Standard)
```

The ratio (Max Payment / Need Standard) is the "ratable reduction" percentage, approximately 43% for 2026.

Source: [7 AAC 45.525](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/alaska/7-AAC-45.525)

---

## Test Coverage

**100 test cases** across 13 test files covering:

| Category | Tests | Key Scenarios |
|----------|-------|---------------|
| Benefit Calculation | 8 | Adult-included and pregnant woman |
| Eligibility | 8 | Combined eligibility checks |
| Gross Income Test | 7 | 185% threshold, exact boundary |
| Net Income Test | 7 | Need standard comparison |
| Resource Test | 9 | Standard ($2,000) and elderly ($3,000) limits |
| Earned Income | 13 | New vs continuing recipients, two earners |
| Unearned Income | 7 | Child support passthrough |
| Childcare Deduction | 10 | Age brackets (under 2, exactly 2, 2+) |
| Need Standard | 8 | Family sizes 1-10, pregnant woman |
| Maximum Payment | 8 | Family sizes 1-11, pregnant woman |
| Integration | 9 | Full pipeline with edge cases |

**Edge cases tested:**
- Income at exact 185% gross threshold
- Gross income passes but net income fails
- Two-parent household with both earners
- Child age exactly 2 (childcare deduction boundary)
- Family size 9 (first beyond table)
- Pregnant woman alone (size 1)

---

## Known Limitations (Not Modeled)

### Unit Types Not Modeled
1. **Child-only units** - Only adult-included and pregnant woman are implemented
2. **Two-parent incapacitated** - Both parents treated as able to work

### Features Not Modeled
3. **Minimum payment threshold ($10)** - Payments below $10 should not be issued per regulation
4. **Shelter/utility reduction** - Regional heating utility standards, non-heating utility standards, and shelter allowances that reduce benefits for families with low shelter costs
5. **Summer reduction for two-parent families** - Reduced payment during summer months
6. **Income deeming** - Personal allowance deductions for stepparent, alien sponsor, or parent of minor parent
7. **Work incentive tiers** - Uses Tier 1 (33% disregard) for all continuing recipients; cannot track months receiving ATAP
8. **60-month lifetime limit** - Cannot simulate due to single-period architecture

### Historical Values
9. **2017-2022 values** - Need standard and pregnant woman values estimated via SSI COLA backwards calculation from 2023 authoritative values; not verified from official sources

---

prs.title: Implement North Dakota TANF program
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements North Dakota's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program.

Closes #7073

---

## Regulatory Authority

| Source | Citation |
|--------|----------|
| State Statute | [N.D. Century Code Chapter 50-09](https://ndlegis.gov/cencode/t50.html) |
| State Administrative Code | [N.D.A.C. Chapter 75-02-01.2](https://ndlegis.gov/information/acdata/pdf/75-02-01.2.pdf) |
| Policy Manual | [Service Chapter 400-19](https://nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/) |

---

## Income Eligibility Tests

### Net Income Test

Countable income must be **less than** the Standard of Need.

**Source:** [Policy Manual 400-19-110-15](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_110_15.htm)

---

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

### 1. Standard Employment Expense Allowance

**Formula:** Greater of **27%** of gross earned income OR **$180**

Applied first to gross earned income before other deductions.

**Source:** [Policy Manual 400-19-105-25](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_105_25.htm)

### 2. Time Limited Percentage (TLP) Disregard

**Declining Rate by Calendar Month:**

| Months | TLP Rate |
|:------:|:--------:|
| 1-6 (Jan-Jun) | 50% |
| 7-9 (Jul-Sep) | 35% |
| 10-12 (Oct-Dec) | 25% |

Applied to earnings after the Standard Employment Expense deduction.

> **Note:** Uses calendar month as proxy for participation months. The disregard cycle resets each January. In actual ND TANF policy, TLP tracks cumulative participation months and ends after 12 months (0% disregard for month 13+).

**Source:** [Policy Manual 400-19-105-25](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_105_25.htm)

---

## Income Standards

### Standard of Need (Effective 2025-10-01)

North Dakota uses a 2D lookup table based on the number of caretakers (0, 1, or 2) and children (0-10) in the household.

| Caretakers | 0 children | 1 child | 2 children | 3 children | 4 children | 5 children |
|:----------:|:----------:|:-------:|:----------:|:----------:|:----------:|:----------:|
| 0 | $0 | $366 | $536 | $697 | $866 | $1,028 |
| 1 | $523 | $739 | $962 | $1,175 | $1,393 | $1,612 |
| 2 | $739 | $962 | $1,175 | $1,393 | $1,612 | $1,830 |

**Historical Values:** Parameters include values effective 2015-10-01, 2023-08-01, 2024-10-01, and 2025-10-01.

**Sources:**
- [Policy Manual 400-19-110-05 Standard of Need Chart](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_110_05.htm)
- [Archive 2024-10-01 (Release 25.1)](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/Archive%20Documents/2025/Release%2025.1/400_19_110_05.htm)
- [Archive 2023-08-01 (ML 3869)](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/Archive%20Documents/2024%20-%20ML%203869/400_19_110_05.htm)
- [Archive 2015-10-01 (ML 3740)](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/Archive%20Documents/2023%20-%20ML%203740/400_19_110_05.htm)

---

## Resource Limits

| Household Size | Resource Limit |
|:--------------:|:--------------:|
| 1 person | $3,000 |
| 2 persons | $6,000 |
| Each additional | +$25 |

**Source:** [Policy Manual 400-19-55-05-05 Asset Limits](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_55_05_05.htm)

---

## Benefit Calculation

### Formula

```
Standard Employment Expense = max(0.27 × Gross Earned, $180)
TLP Disregard = TLP_Rate(month) × (Gross Earned - Standard Employment Expense)
Countable Earned Income = Gross Earned - Standard Employment Expense - TLP Disregard
Countable Income = Countable Earned Income + Unearned Income
Benefit = max(Standard of Need - Countable Income, 0)
```

Where `TLP_Rate(month)` = 50% for months 1-6, 35% for months 7-9, 25% for months 10-12.

**Source:** [Policy Manual 400-19-110-20 Benefit Calculation](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_110_20.htm)

### Example Calculation

**Family of 3 (1 caretaker, 2 children) with $1,500/month earned income in January:**
1. Gross earned income: $1,500
2. Standard Employment Expense: max($1,500 × 0.27, $180) = $405
3. After SEE: $1,500 - $405 = $1,095
4. TLP disregard (50% for January): $1,095 × 0.50 = $547.50
5. Countable earned income: $1,095 - $547.50 = $547.50
6. Standard of Need (1 caretaker, 2 children): $962
7. **Benefit: $962 - $547.50 = $414.50**

---

## Out of Scope

The following are not modeled in this implementation:

### Benefit Rules
- **$10 Minimum Benefit** – Benefits below $10 are not issued ([N.D.A.C. 75-02-01.2-43](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/north-dakota/N-D-A-C-75-02-1.2-43))

### Income Deductions
- **Dependent Care Deduction** – Maximum deduction amounts vary by child age, tied to Child Care Assistance Program rates ([N.D.A.C. 75-02-01.2-53](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/north-dakota/N-D-A-C-75-02-1.2-53))

### Special Allowances
- **$45 Out of Home Allowance** – Additional allowance for individuals placed outside the home ([Policy Manual 400-19-110-20](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_110_20.htm))
- **Kinship Care Maintenance Payment** – Additional payment for relative caregivers ([Policy Manual 400-19-110-20](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_110_20.htm))

### Time Limits
- **60-Month Lifetime Limit** – Federal lifetime limit on TANF benefits ([42 U.S.C. § 608(a)(7)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/608))
- **TLP Month 13+ (0% disregard)** – Calendar month proxy only covers months 1-12; cumulative participation tracking not modeled ([Policy Manual 400-19-105-25](https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/40019/400_19_105_25.htm))

---

## Files Added

### Parameters (7 files)

```
policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/nd/dhs/tanf/
├── benefit/
│   ├── max_children.yaml
│   └── standard_of_need.yaml
├── income/
│   └── deductions/
│       ├── standard_employment_expense/
│       │   ├── minimum.yaml
│       │   └── rate.yaml
│       └── time_limited_percentage/
│           └── rate.yaml
└── resources/
    └── limit/
        ├── base.yaml
        └── increment.yaml
```

### Variables (9 files)

```
policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/nd/dhs/tanf/
├── nd_tanf.py
├── nd_tanf_standard_of_need.py
├── eligibility/
│   ├── nd_tanf_eligible.py
│   ├── nd_tanf_income_eligible.py
│   └── nd_tanf_resources_eligible.py
└── income/
    ├── nd_tanf_countable_earned_income.py
    ├── nd_tanf_countable_earned_income_person.py
    ├── nd_tanf_countable_income.py
    └── nd_tanf_countable_unearned_income.py
```

### Tests (8 files, 82 tests)

```
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/nd/dhs/tanf/
├── integration.yaml (26 tests)
├── nd_tanf.yaml (6 tests)
├── nd_tanf_countable_earned_income_person.yaml (10 tests)

```

---

## Test Coverage

| Category | Count |
|----------|:-----:|
| Integration tests | 26 |
| Unit tests | 56 |
| **Total** | **82** |

prs.title: Implement South Dakota TANF
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes #7070

Implements the South Dakota Department of Social Services Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program with a simplified approach using federal baseline variables.

## Regulatory Authority

- **Primary Source:** [ARSD Article 67:10 - Temporary Assistance for Needy Families](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10)
- **Payment Standards:** [ARSD 67:10:05:03](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:05:03)
- **Income Standards:** [ARSD 67:10:03](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:03)
- **Resource Limits:** [ARSD 67:10:04:03](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:04:03)
- **Program Overview:** [SD DSS TANF Page](https://dss.sd.gov/economicassistance/tanf.aspx)
- **State Plan:** [SD TANF State Plan](https://dss.sd.gov/docs/economicassistance/tanf/TANFStatePlan.pdf)

## Income Eligibility Tests

### Net Income Test (100%)
South Dakota uses a single net income test - countable income must not exceed the payment standard for the family size.

**Formula:**
```
Countable Earned Income = max(0, Gross Earned - $90) × 0.80
Countable Income = Countable Earned + Unearned Income
Eligible if: Countable Income ≤ Payment Standard
```

**Source:** [ARSD 67:10:03:05 - Standard earned income deduction](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:03:05)

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

| Deduction | Amount | Source |
|-----------|--------|--------|
| Flat earned income deduction | $90/month per earner | [ARSD 67:10:03:05](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:03:05) |
| Percentage disregard on remainder | 20% | [ARSD 67:10:03:05](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:03:05) |
| Child support received | 100% excluded | [ARSD 67:10:03:04](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:03:04) |
| Unearned income disregard | None | [ARSD 67:10:03:02](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:03:02) |

## Resource Limits

| Resource Limit | Amount | Source |
|---------------|--------|--------|
| Maximum countable resources | $2,000 | [ARSD 67:10:04:03](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:04:03) |

## Income Standards (Payment Standards)

Per [ARSD 67:10:05:03](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:05:03), effective 07/01/2023:

| Family Size | Independent Living | Shared Living |
|-------------|-------------------|---------------|
| 1 | $512 | $317 |
| 2 | $627 | $432 |
| 3 | $701 | $507 |
| 4 | $775 | $581 |
| 5 | $848 | $654 |
| 6 | $922 | $728 |
| 7 | $996 | $800 |
| 8 | $1,070 | $875 |
| 9 | $1,141 | $949 |
| 10 | $1,213 | $1,020 |
| 11 | $1,287 | $1,093 |
| 12 | $1,361 | $1,167 |
| 13+ | +$53 per person | +$53 per person |

**Note:** Starting August 2025, payment standards will be reduced by 10%. The state plans gradual annual reductions until reaching 35% total. [Source](https://southdakotasearchlight.com/2025/07/15/south-dakota-legislative-committee-finalizes-benefit-cuts-tanf-needy-families/)

## Benefit Calculation

```
Benefit = Payment Standard - Countable Income
Final Benefit = max(0, Benefit)
```

**Source:** [ARSD 67:10:05:02](https://sdlegislature.gov/Rules/Administrative/67:10:05:02)

**Example:** Family of 3 with $400/month gross earnings (independent living)
1. Countable earned = max(0, $400 - $90) × 0.80 = $248
2. Countable income = $248
3. Payment standard = $701
4. Benefit = $701 - $248 = **$453/month**

## Files Added

prs.title: Implement Delaware TANF
prs.body:
## Summary
Closes #7068

Implements Delaware's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program with full eligibility determination and benefit calculation. This implementation distinguishes between **applicants** and **recipients**, who have different income tests per Delaware regulations.

## Regulatory Authority
- [16 Del. Admin. Code §4000-4008](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4008)
- [Delaware TANF State Plan 2017-2020](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/dss/pdf/detanfstateplan2017.pdf)

---

## Eligibility Determination

Delaware TANF uses a **three-step process** that differs for applicants vs recipients:

### Step 1: Gross Income Test (Same for Both)
| Test | Threshold |
|------|-----------|
| Gross income | ≤ 185% of Standard of Need |

Source: [16 Del. Admin. Code §4008.1.1, §4008.1.2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4008)

### Step 2: Net Income Test (Different Rules)

| Status | Deductions Applied | Compare To |
|--------|-------------------|------------|
| **Applicant** | $90 + childcare | Payment Standard |
| **Recipient** | $90 + childcare + **$30 + 1/3** | Standard of Need |

**Key Difference**: Recipients get more favorable treatment:
- Additional $30 flat + 1/3 disregard on earned income
- Higher threshold (Standard of Need > Payment Standard)

Source: [Delaware TANF State Plan, Exhibits 1 & 2 (page 5)](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/dss/pdf/detanfstateplan2017.pdf#page=5)

### Step 3: Benefit Calculation (Same for Both)
Full deductions applied ($90 + $30 + 1/3 + childcare), then deficit formula.

---

## Income Deductions & Disregards

**Order of deductions matters** - applied in this sequence:

### Earned Income Deductions (Per Earner)
| Order | Deduction | Amount | Description |
|-------|-----------|--------|-------------|
| 1 | Work expense | $90/month | Standard work deduction |
| 2 | $30 disregard | $30/month | Flat earned income disregard |
| 3 | 1/3 disregard | 33.3% of remainder | Applied after $30 |
| 4 | Dependent care | Up to $200 (under 2) / $175 (2+) | Per child, capped at actual expenses |

Sources:
- [16 Del. Admin. Code §4008.1.1 Step 2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4008) - "$90.00 earned income deduction"
- [Delaware TANF State Plan 2017 - Exhibit 1 (page 7)](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/dss/pdf/detanfstateplan2017.pdf#page=7)

**Note**: $30 + 1/3 disregard only applies to:
- Recipient eligibility test (Step 2)
- Benefit calculation (Step 3)
- NOT to applicant eligibility test

> ⚠️ **Implementation Note**: The $30+1/3 disregard is actually **time-limited**:
> - $30 + 1/3: First 4 consecutive months only
> - $30 only: Next 8 months
> - Neither: Until 12 months without TANF benefits
>
> We **always apply the full $30+1/3 disregard**.
>
> Source: [WorkWorld - DE Earned Income Disregards](https://help.workworldapp.com/wwwebhelp/de_earned_income_disregards_tanf_and_ga.htm)

### Unearned Income Disregards
| Disregard | Amount |
|-----------|--------|
| Child support | First $50/month |

Source: [16 Del. Admin. Code §4008.2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4008) - "First $50 of child support disregard"

---

## Income Standards

### Standard of Need
Calculated as **75% of Federal Poverty Level** (monthly).

Sources:
- [16 Del. Admin. Code §4007.2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4007) - *"The standard of need used is 75% of the Federal Poverty Level"*
- [Delaware TANF State Plan 2017 (page 8)](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/dss/pdf/detanfstateplan2017.pdf#page=8)

### Payment Standard (Frozen since 2002)
| Family Size | Payment Standard |
|-------------|------------------|
| 1 | $201 |
| 2 | $270 |
| 3 | $338 |
| 4 | $407 |
| 5 | $475 |
| 6 | $544 |
| 7 | $612 |
| 8 | $681 |
| 9+ | $681 + $69 per additional person |

Sources:
- [Delaware TANF State Plan 2017 - Payment Standard Table (page 8)](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/dss/pdf/detanfstateplan2017.pdf#page=8)
- [16 Del. Admin. Code §4008](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4008)

### Gross Income Limit
**185% of Standard of Need** (calculated dynamically from FPL)

Source: [16 Del. Admin. Code §4008.1](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4008)

---

## Benefit Calculation Formula

```
Net Earned Income = Gross Earned - $90 - $30 - (1/3 of remainder) - Childcare
Net Unearned Income = Gross Unearned - $50 child support disregard
Countable Income = Net Earned + Net Unearned

Deficit = Standard of Need - Countable Income
Remainder = Deficit × 50%
Grant = min(Remainder, Payment Standard)
```

Sources:
- [16 Del. Admin. Code §4008.1.1 Step 3 - TANF Grant Computation](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4008)
- [Delaware TANF State Plan 2017 - Exhibit 1 and Exhibit 2 (page 7)](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/dss/pdf/detanfstateplan2017.pdf#page=7)

---

## Resource Limit
- **$10,000** for all households

Sources:
- [16 Del. Admin. Code §4000-4002.2](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/delaware/16-Del-Admin-Code-SS-4000-4002) - "Resource limit of $10,000.00"
- [Delaware TANF State Plan 2017 (page 5)](https://dhss.delaware.gov/wp-content/uploads/sites/11/dss/pdf/detanfstateplan2017.pdf#page=5)

---

## Implementation Structure

### Parameters (`/parameters/gov/states/de/dhss/tanf/`)
```
tanf/
├── benefit/
│   └── deficit_rate.yaml              # 50%
├── income/
│   ├── standard_of_need.yaml          # 75% of FPL
│   ├── gross_limit.yaml               # 185% of Standard of Need
│   └── deductions/
│       ├── work_expense.yaml          # $90
│       ├── thirty_disregard.yaml      # $30
│       ├── one_third_disregard.yaml   # 33.3%
│       ├── dependent_care.yaml        # $200/$175 by age
│       └── child_support.yaml         # $50
├── payment_standard/
│   ├── amount.yaml                    # By family size
│   ├── max_unit_size.yaml             # 8
│   └── additional_person.yaml         # $69
└── resource_limit.yaml                # $10,000
```

### Variables (`/variables/gov/states/de/dhss/tanf/`)
```
tanf/
├── de_tanf.py                         # Benefit calculation
├── de_tanf_standard_of_need.py        # 75% FPL
├── de_tanf_payment_standard.py        # By family size
├── eligibility/
│   ├── de_tanf_eligible.py            # Combined eligibility
│   ├── de_tanf_gross_income_eligible.py
│   ├── de_tanf_net_income_eligible.py # Applicant/recipient logic
│   └── de_tanf_resources_eligible.py
└── income/
    ├── de_tanf_gross_income.py        # Total gross (earned + unearned)
    ├── de_tanf_countable_income.py    # Recipient total
    ├── de_tanf_net_income.py          # Applicant total
    ├── earned/
    │   ├── de_tanf_countable_earned_income_person.py  # $90+$30+1/3
    │   ├── de_tanf_countable_earned_income.py         # SPMUnit total
    │   ├── de_tanf_net_earned_income.py               # Applicant earned
    │   ├── de_tanf_earned_income_deduction.py         # $90
    │   └── de_tanf_dependent_care_deduction.py        # Childcare
    └── unearned/
        └── de_tanf_countable_unearned_income.py       # Gross - $50
```

### Key Implementation Detail: `is_tanf_enrolled`
The variable `de_tanf_net_income_eligible` uses `is_tanf_enrolled` to apply the correct rules:
- `False` (applicant): Uses `de_tanf_net_income`, compares to Payment Standard
- `True` (recipient): Uses `de_tanf_countable_income`, compares to Standard of Need

---

## Test Coverage
- Eligibility tests for both applicants and recipients
- Income calculation chain verification
- Benefit calculation with deficit formula
- Edge cases (zero income, high income, resource limits)
- Applicant vs recipient pathway tests

prs.title: Implement Rhode Island TANF program
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements Rhode Island Works (RI Works), Rhode Island's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) cash assistance program.

Closes #7062

---

## Rhode Island Works Income Rules

### Regulatory Authority
- **Rhode Island General Laws Chapter 40-5.2** - The Rhode Island Works Program
- **218-RICR-20-00-2** - Rhode Island Works Program Rules and Regulations

---

### 1. INCOME ELIGIBILITY TESTS

#### Net Income Test
Countable income (after disregards/exemptions) must be less than the Payment Standard.

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2.15 - Income Calculations](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/rhode-island/218-RICR-20-00-2.15)

#### Resource Test
Countable resources must not exceed **$5,000**.

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2.14.1 - Resource Limits](https://rules.sos.ri.gov/Regulations/part/218-20-00-2)

---

### 2. INCOME DEDUCTIONS & EXEMPTIONS

#### A. Earned Income Disregard (Per Earner)

Each employed individual receives:
1. **$525 flat deduction** from gross earned income (effective July 2024)
2. **50% disregard** of remaining earned income after flat deduction

Formula per earner: `Countable Earned = max(Gross Earned - $525, 0) × 0.5`

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2.15.5(B)(1) - Earned Income Disregard](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/rhode-island/218-RICR-20-00-2.15); [FY2025 SFO Budget as Enacted, p. 13](https://www.rilegislature.gov/sfiscal/Budget%20Analyses/FY2025%20SFO%20Budget%20as%20Enacted.pdf#page=13)

#### B. Dependent Care Deduction

| Dependent Age | Maximum Deduction |
|---------------|-------------------|
| Under age 2 | $200/month |
| Age 2+ | $175/month |

Deduction is the lesser of actual childcare expenses or maximum allowed.

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2.15.5(B)(2) - Dependent Care Deduction](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/rhode-island/218-RICR-20-00-2.15)

#### C. Child Support Exclusion

First **$50/month** of child support received is excluded from countable income.

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2.15.3(D) - Child Support Pass-Through](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/rhode-island/218-RICR-20-00-2.15)

---

### 3. INCOME STANDARDS BY FAMILY SIZE (effective September 2024)

| Family Size | Payment Standard | Subsidized Housing |
|-------------|------------------|-------------------|
| 1 | $510 | $445 |
| 2 | $701 | $636 |
| 3 | $865 | $800 |
| 4 | $990 | $925 |
| 5 | $1,115 | $1,050 |
| 6 | $1,240 | $1,175 |
| 7 | $1,364 | $1,299 |
| 8 | $1,489 | $1,424 |
| Each Additional | +$125 | +$125 |

**Subsidized Housing Reduction:** $65 flat reduction to payment standard for recipients in subsidized housing.

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2.18.1 - Payment Standards](https://rules.sos.ri.gov/Regulations/part/218-20-00-2); [DHS Press Release - RI Works Benefits Increase FY 2025](https://dhs.ri.gov/press-releases/rhode-island-works-families-see-increase-benefits-fy-2025-state-budget)

---

### 4. BENEFIT CALCULATION

#### Formula:
```
Benefit = Payment Standard − Countable Income
```

Where **Countable Income** =
```
Countable Earned Income + Countable Unearned Income
```

#### Calculation Steps:
1. For each earner: `Per-Earner Countable = max(Gross Earned - $525, 0) × 0.5`
2. Sum per-earner amounts: `Total Earned After Disregard = Σ(Per-Earner Countable)`
3. Subtract dependent care: `Countable Earned = max(Total Earned After Disregard - Dependent Care, 0)`
4. Calculate unearned: `Countable Unearned = Gross Unearned - min(Child Support, $50)`
5. Sum: `Countable Income = Countable Earned + Countable Unearned`
6. Final: `Benefit = Payment Standard - Countable Income`

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2 - Rhode Island Works Program](https://rules.sos.ri.gov/Regulations/part/218-20-00-2)

---

## Not Modeled

- **Earned Income Set Aside**: Adults who gain new employment while on RI Works may exclude their earned income for up to 6 months or until household gross income reaches 185% FPL, whichever comes first. The household chooses whether to use this provision.
- **$100 clothing allowance**: Annual one-time payment per eligible child (issued in August)
- **$10 minimum benefit threshold**: Benefits below $10 are not issued
- **Incapacitated adult care deduction**: $175/month for care of incapacitated adults

Source: [218-RICR-20-00-2.15.3(E) - Earned Income Set Aside](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/rhode-island/218-RICR-20-00-2.15); [RI DHS Public Information Notice](https://dhs.ri.gov/press-releases/rhode-island-works-families-see-increase-benefits-fy-2025-state-budget)

---

## Historical Policy Changes

| Effective Date | Changes |
|----------------|---------|
| 2008-07-01 | RI Works program established (replaced Family Independence Program); $170 earned income disregard |
| 2019-01-01 | Dependent care deduction added ($200 under 2, $175 age 2+) |
| 2021-07-01 | 30% benefit increase; $300 earned income disregard (was $170); $5,000 resource limit (was $1,000) |
| 2024-07-01 | Earned income disregard increased from $300 to $525 (FY 2025 budget) |
| 2024-09-01 | 20% benefit increase (FY 2025 budget) |

Sources: [Senate Fiscal Office Issue Brief 2011](https://www.rilegislature.gov/sfiscal/Other%20Documents/Rhode%20Island%20Works.pdf#page=1); [RI Works 2021 Reform Package](https://dhs.ri.gov/press-releases/ri-works-benefit-increase-almost-here); [FY2025 SFO Budget as Enacted](https://www.rilegislature.gov/sfiscal/Budget%20Analyses/FY2025%20SFO%20Budget%20as%20Enacted.pdf#page=13); [RI Works FY 2025 Increase](https://dhs.ri.gov/press-releases/rhode-island-works-families-see-increase-benefits-fy-2025-state-budget)

---

## Files Added

### Parameters (9 files)
```
gov/states/ri/dhs/works/
├── income/
│   ├── earned_income_disregard/
│   │   ├── amount.yaml           # $170 (2008) → $300 (2021) → $525 (2024)
│   │   └── rate.yaml             # 50% disregard rate
│   ├── child_support_disregard.yaml  # $50/month exclusion
│   └── dependent_care/
│       └── amount.yaml           # By age brackets
├── payment_standard/
│   ├── amount.yaml               # By family size (1-8)
│   ├── additional_person.yaml    # $125 per person beyond 8
│   └── max_unit_size.yaml        # 8
├── subsidized_housing_reduction.yaml  # $65
└── resource_limit.yaml           # $5,000
```

### Variables (10 files)
```
gov/states/ri/dhs/works/
├── ri_works.py                           # Final benefit
├── ri_works_payment_standard.py          # Payment standard by family size
├── eligibility/
│   ├── ri_works_eligible.py              # Final eligibility
│   ├── ri_works_income_eligible.py       # Income eligibility
│   └── ri_works_resource_eligible.py     # Resource eligibility
└── income/
    ├── ri_works_countable_income.py      # Total countable income
    ├── earned/
    │   ├── ri_works_countable_earned_income.py          # Earned after all disregards
    │   └── ri_works_earned_income_after_disregard_person.py  # Per-person disregard
    ├── unearned/
    │   └── ri_works_countable_unearned_income.py        # Unearned with child support exclusion
    └── deductions/
        └── ri_works_dependent_care_deduction.py         # Dependent care deduction
```

### Tests (10 files, 70 test cases)
```
tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ri/dhs/works/

├── ri_works.yaml                              # 4 benefit calculation tests

├── ri_works_countable_unearned_income.yaml    # 8 unearned income tests

```
