prs.title: Add Maine TANF Program
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes #7052

Implements Maine's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program.

## Regulatory Authority

- [22 M.R.S. Section 3762](https://www.mainelegislature.org/legis/statutes/22/title22sec3762.html) - Maine TANF statute
- [10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 331](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/maine/10-144-C-M-R-ch-331) - Maine TANF regulations
- [10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 331, Appendix Charts](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/maine/10-144-C-M-R-ch-331-app-Charts) - Benefit tables
- [TANF 121A Rule Pages (2024)](https://www.maine.gov/dhhs/sites/maine.gov.dhhs/files/rule-2024-09/TANF%20121A%20Rule%20Pages%20%28Clean%29.pdf#page=2) - Current payment standards

## Income Eligibility Tests

### Net Income Test
Countable income must not exceed the Standard of Need for the household size.

**Source:** [22 M.R.S. Section 3762(3)(B)(7-F)](https://www.mainelegislature.org/legis/statutes/22/title22sec3762.html)

### Resource Test
Countable resources must not exceed **$10,000** per family (one vehicle per licensed driver exempted).

**Source:** [22 M.R.S. Section 3762(3)(A)](https://www.mainelegislature.org/legis/statutes/22/title22sec3762.html); [C.M.R. 10, 144, ch. 331, III A (1)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/maine/C-M-R-10-144-ch-331-III)

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

### Earned Income Disregard (Per Employed Person)
Each employed individual in the filing unit receives:
1. **$108 flat deduction** from gross earned income
2. **50% disregard** of remaining earned income after flat deduction

**Note:** First 6 months of employment have higher disregards (100% months 1-3, 75% months 4-6) that cannot be tracked in PolicyEngine's single-period architecture.

**Source:** [22 M.R.S. Section 3762(3)(B)(7-D)(c)](https://www.mainelegislature.org/legis/statutes/22/title22sec3762.html)

### Child Care Deduction
- **$175/month** per child age 2+
- **$200/month** per child under age 2 or with special needs

**Source:** [22 M.R.S. Section 3762(3)(B)(7-D)(d)](https://www.mainelegislature.org/legis/statutes/22/title22sec3762.html)

### Child Support Deduction
First **$50/month** of current child support collections excluded from countable unearned income.

**Source:** [22 M.R.S. Section 3762(3)(B)(1)](https://www.mainelegislature.org/legis/statutes/22/title22sec3762.html); [C.M.R. 10, 144, ch. 331, III B (2)(a)(ii)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/maine/C-M-R-10-144-ch-331-III)

## Income Standards (effective October 2024)

| Household Size | Standard of Need | Maximum Benefit |
|----------------|------------------|-----------------| 
| 1 | $489 | $425 |
| 2 | $769 | $669 |
| 3 | $1,030 | $895 |
| 4 | $1,296 | $1,127 |
| 5 | $1,557 | $1,352 |
| 6 | $1,820 | $1,580 |
| 7 | $2,085 | $1,811 |
| 8 | $2,349 | $2,040 |
| Each Additional | +$263 | +$228 |

**Source:** [10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 331, Appendix Charts (Table 2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/maine/10-144-C-M-R-ch-331-app-Charts); [TANF 121A Rule Pages](https://www.maine.gov/dhhs/sites/maine.gov.dhhs/files/rule-2024-09/TANF%20121A%20Rule%20Pages%20%28Clean%29.pdf#page=2)

## Benefit Calculation

\`\`\`
Monthly TANF Benefit = min(Maximum Benefit, Standard of Need - Countable Income)
\`\`\`

Where:
- \`Countable Income = Countable Earned Income + Countable Unearned Income\`
- \`Countable Earned Income = Sum of (max(Person Gross Earned - $108, 0) × 0.5) - Child Care Deduction\`
- \`Countable Unearned Income = Gross Unearned - min(Child Support, $50)\`

**Source:** [22 M.R.S. Section 3762(3)(B)(8)](https://www.mainelegislature.org/legis/statutes/22/title22sec3762.html); [10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 331, Section G(1)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/maine/C-M-R-10-144-ch-331-III)

### Not Modeled
- **Child-only households**: Maine provides different (lower) payment standards for child-only households where no adult is in the assistance unit. This implementation uses adult-included standards only.
- **Special Need Housing Allowance (SNHA)**: Up to $300/month for households with housing costs ≥ 50% of countable income.

**Source:** [10-144 C.M.R. Chapter 331, Section G(4)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/maine/C-M-R-10-144-ch-331-III)

## Files Added

### Parameters (10 files)
\`\`\`
policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/me/dhhs/tanf/
├── child_care/
│   └── amount.yaml                  # Age-based bracket ($200 under 2, $175 age 2+)
├── child_support_deduction.yaml     # $50/month exclusion
├── earned_income/
│   ├── flat_deduction.yaml          # $108 per employed person
│   └── percentage_disregard.yaml    # 50% disregard
├── max_unit_size.yaml               # Cap at 8 for table lookup
├── maximum_benefit/
│   ├── amount.yaml                  # By household size 1-8
│   └── each_additional.yaml         # +$228 per additional member
├── resource_limit.yaml              # $10,000
└── standard_of_need/
    ├── amount.yaml                  # By household size 1-8
    └── each_additional.yaml         # +$263 per additional member
\`\`\`

### Variables (13 files)
\`\`\`
policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/me/dhhs/tanf/
├── eligibility/
│   ├── me_tanf_eligible.py
│   ├── me_tanf_income_eligible.py
│   └── me_tanf_resources_eligible.py
├── income/
│   ├── deductions/
│   │   └── me_tanf_child_care_deduction.py
│   ├── earned/
│   │   ├── me_tanf_countable_earned_income.py
│   │   └── me_tanf_earned_income_after_disregard_person.py
│   ├── me_tanf_countable_income.py
│   └── unearned/
│       └── me_tanf_countable_unearned_income.py
├── me_tanf.py
├── me_tanf_maximum_benefit.py
└── me_tanf_standard_of_need.py
\`\`\`

### Tests (11 files, 74 test cases)
\`\`\`
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/me/dhhs/tanf/
├── integration.yaml                           # 23 integration cases
├── me_tanf.yaml                               # 5 boundary cases
├── me_tanf_child_care_deduction.yaml          # 5 cases
├── me_tanf_countable_earned_income.yaml       # 4 cases
├── me_tanf_countable_unearned_income.yaml     # 14 cases
├── me_tanf_earned_income_after_disregard_person.yaml  # 1 case (5 people)
├── me_tanf_eligible.yaml                      # 4 cases
├── me_tanf_income_eligible.yaml               # 5 cases
├── me_tanf_maximum_benefit.yaml               # 5 cases
├── me_tanf_resources_eligible.yaml            # 3 cases
└── me_tanf_standard_of_need.yaml              # 5 cases
\`\`\`

## Example Calculations

### Example 1: Single earner with child care
- **Household**: 1 adult (age 30), 2 children (ages 8 and 5)
- **Monthly earned income**: $1,000
- **Child care expenses**: $350/month

**Calculation**:
1. Standard of Need (size 3): $1,030
2. Maximum Benefit: $895
3. Earned income disregard: ($1,000 - $108) × 0.5 = $446
4. Child care deduction: 2 × $175 = $350
5. Countable earned: $446 - $350 = $96
6. Benefit: min($895, $1,030 - $96) = **$895**

### Example 2: Multi-earner household
- **Household**: 2 adults, 2 children (ages 4 and 1)
- **Person 1 earnings**: $600/month
- **Person 2 earnings**: $400/month
- **Child care expenses**: $500/month

**Calculation**:
1. Standard of Need (size 4): $1,296
2. Maximum Benefit: $1,127
3. Person 1 earned disregard: ($600 - $108) × 0.5 = $246
4. Person 2 earned disregard: ($400 - $108) × 0.5 = $146
5. Sum after disregard: $392
6. Child care: $175 (age 4) + $200 (age 1) = $375
7. Countable earned: $392 - $375 = $17
8. Benefit: min($1,127, $1,296 - $17) = **$1,127**

prs.title: Add New Hampshire TANF program
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes #1480

Implements New Hampshire's Financial Assistance to Needy Families (FANF) program, including the Cliff Effect Initiative changes from September 2022.

## Regulatory Authority

- [RSA 167:77-g](https://www.gencourt.state.nh.us/rsa/html/xii/167/167-77-g.htm) - Adjustment of TANF Financial Assistance
- [RSA 167:79](https://www.gencourt.state.nh.us/rsa/html/xii/167/167-79.htm) - Employment Program; Eligibility
- [NH TANF State Plan](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sites/g/files/ehbemt476/files/documents2/tanf-state-plan.pdf) - Program overview
- [FAM 603](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/famar_htm/html/603_01_earned_income_disregards_eid_sr_97-03_02_97_fam_a.htm) - Deductions and Disregards
- [SR 97-03](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/sr_97-03_dated_02_97.htm) - TANF Implementation
- [BFA SR 22-17](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/bfa_sr_22-17_dated_07_22.htm) - Resource limit increase
- [BFA SR 22-18](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/bfa_sr_22-18_dated_07_22.htm) - Child care age threshold change
- [BFA SR 22-28](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/bfa_sr_22-28_dated_09_22.htm) - Cliff Effect Initiative (75% disregard)

## Income Eligibility Tests

### Single Income Test
Net countable income must be at or below the payment standard (60% FPG).

**Source**: [RSA 167:77-g](https://www.gencourt.state.nh.us/rsa/html/xii/167/167-77-g.htm)

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

| Deduction | Applicant | Recipient | Source |
|-----------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Earned Income Disregard | 20% | 75% | [SR 97-03](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/sr_97-03_dated_02_97.htm); [BFA SR 22-28](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/bfa_sr_22-28_dated_09_22.htm) |

| Child Care (under 6, PT) | $100/mo | $100/mo | [FAM 603.05](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/famar_htm/html/603_05_special_situation_deductions_fam_a.htm) |
| Child Care (6+, FT) | $175/mo | $175/mo | [FAM 603.05](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/famar_htm/html/603_05_special_situation_deductions_fam_a.htm) |
| Child Care (6+, PT) | $87.50/mo | $87.50/mo | [FAM 603.05](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/famar_htm/html/603_05_special_situation_deductions_fam_a.htm) |
| SSI | Excluded | Excluded | Federal TANF baseline (42 U.S.C. § 602) |

**Notes**:
- Full-time threshold: $377/month earned income
- A 100% disregard exists for high-demand jobs with medical benefits, but is not implemented due to lack of job classification data

## Resource Limits

| Status | Limit | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Applicant | $1,000 | [SR 97-03](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/sr_97-03_dated_02_97.htm); FAM 403 |
| Recipient | $5,000 | [BFA SR 22-17](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/bfa_sr_22-17_dated_07_22.htm) (eff. 07/01/2022) |

## Income Standards (2024 - 60% FPG Monthly)

| Household Size | Payment Standard |
|----------------|------------------|
| 1 | $753 |
| 2 | $1,022 |
| 3 | $1,291 |
| 4 | $1,560 |
| 5 | $1,829 |
| 6 | $2,098 |
| 7 | $2,367 |
| 8 | $2,636 |

**Source**: [RSA 167:77-g](https://www.gencourt.state.nh.us/rsa/html/xii/167/167-77-g.htm) (60% of 2024 FPG)

## Benefit Calculation

**Formula**: `Benefit = max(Payment Standard - Net Countable Income, 0)`

Where:
- Payment Standard = 60% of monthly FPG for household size
- Net Countable Income = Countable Earned Income + Gross Unearned Income
- Countable Earned Income = max((Gross Earned × (1 - disregard_rate)) - Child Care Deduction, 0)
- Disregard rate: 20% for applicants, 75% for recipients

**Source**: [RSA 167:77-g](https://www.gencourt.state.nh.us/rsa/html/xii/167/167-77-g.htm); [SR 97-03](https://www.dhhs.nh.gov/sr_htm/html/sr_97-03_dated_02_97.htm)

## Example Calculations

### Example 1: Applicant with $1,000/month earnings
- Gross Earned Income: $1,000/month
- After 20% disregard: $1,000 × 0.80 = $800
- Payment Standard (2 persons): $1,022
- **Benefit: $1,022 - $800 = $222**

### Example 2: Recipient with same $1,000/month earnings
- Gross Earned Income: $1,000/month
- After 75% disregard: $1,000 × 0.25 = $250
- Payment Standard (2 persons): $1,022
- **Benefit: $1,022 - $250 = $772** (vs $222 for applicant - $550 more!)

### Example 3: Recipient with child care
- Gross Earned Income: $2,000/month (full-time)
- After 75% disregard: $2,000 × 0.25 = $500
- Child care deduction (child under 6, FT): $200
- Countable earned: $500 - $200 = $300
- Payment Standard (2 persons): $1,022
- **Benefit: $1,022 - $300 = $722**

## Summary

Implements Hawaii's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program.

Closes #7047

## Regulatory Authority

- [Hawaii TANF State Plan (Effective October 1, 2023)](https://humanservices.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Hawaii_TANF_State_Plan_Signed_Certified-Eff_20231001.pdf)

## Income Eligibility Tests

### Gross Income Test
- Threshold: 185% of Standard of Need (SON)
- SON = 100% of 2006 Hawaii Federal Poverty Level (frozen since July 2007)

| Household Size | SON (Monthly) | Gross Limit (185%) |
|----------------|---------------|-------------------|
| 1 | $939 | $1,737 |
| 2 | $1,265 | $2,340 |
| 3 | $1,590 | $2,941 |
| 4 | $1,916 | $3,544 |
| 5 | $2,242 | $4,147 |

**Source:** [Hawaii TANF State Plan Section 10.1 (page 19)](https://humanservices.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Hawaii_TANF_State_Plan_Signed_Certified-Eff_20231001.pdf#page=19)

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

Applied to earned income only, in this order:
1. **20% Standard Deduction**
2. **$200 Flat Rate Deduction**
3. **55% Earned Income Disregard** (months 1-24)

**Source:** [Hawaii TANF State Plan Section 10.2.1 (page 19)](https://humanservices.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Hawaii_TANF_State_Plan_Signed_Certified-Eff_20231001.pdf#page=19)

### Dependent Care Deduction
- Full-time (32+ hrs/week): $175 per child
- Part-time (<32 hrs/week): $165 per child

**Source:** [Hawaii TANF State Plan Section 10.2.2 (page 20)](https://humanservices.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Hawaii_TANF_State_Plan_Signed_Certified-Eff_20231001.pdf#page=20)

## Income Standards

Standard of Assistance (SOA) = 48% of Standard of Need

| Household Size | SON | SOA (48%) |
|----------------|-----|-----------|
| 1 | $939 | $450.72 |
| 2 | $1,265 | $607.20 |
| 3 | $1,590 | $763.20 |
| 4 | $1,916 | $919.68 |
| 5 | $2,242 | $1,076.16 |

**Source:** [Hawaii TANF State Plan Section 11.1 (page 22)](https://humanservices.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Hawaii_TANF_State_Plan_Signed_Certified-Eff_20231001.pdf#page=22)

## Benefit Calculation

```
Benefit = Standard of Assistance - Countable Income
```

- Benefit floored at $0
- NOTE: SOA is reduced by 20% after the family receives their initial two full months of benefits for mandatory work-required households. This reduction cannot be modeled as PolicyEngine cannot track cumulative months of benefit receipt.

**Source:** [Hawaii TANF State Plan Section 11.1 (page 22)](https://humanservices.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/Hawaii_TANF_State_Plan_Signed_Certified-Eff_20231001.pdf#page=22)

## Implementation Notes

- **Simplified approach**: Uses federal baseline for demographic eligibility and gross income sources
- **Asset test**: Disregarded since April 2013
- **Non-simulatable rules**: 60-month lifetime limit, EIDR tier based on months (55% for months 1-24, 36% after), 20% SOA reduction after 2 months

## Test Coverage

- **73 tests** covering eligibility, income calculations, and benefit amounts
- Integration tests validate complete benefit calculation pipeline

## Example Calculation

**Family of 2 with $1,500 monthly earned income:**

| Step | Calculation | Amount |
|------|-------------|--------|
| Gross Earned Income | | $1,500 |
| 20% Standard Deduction | $1,500 × 0.20 | -$300 |
| After Standard | | $1,200 |
| Flat Rate Deduction | | -$200 |
| After Flat | | $1,000 |
| 55% EIDR | $1,000 × 0.55 | -$550 |
| Countable Earned | | $450 |
| SOA (size 2) | | $607.20 |
| **Benefit** | $607.20 - $450 | **$157.20** |

prs.title: Implement Idaho TANF
prs.body:
## Summary
Implements Idaho Temporary Assistance for Families in Idaho (TAFI) program.

Closes #7043

## Regulatory Authority
IDAPA 16.03.08 - Temporary Assistance for Families in Idaho (TAFI)

- Primary Legal Authority: [IDAPA 16.03.08](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/title-IDAPA-16/rule-16.03.08)
- Administering Agency: Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
- Effective Date: April 1, 2016

## Income Eligibility Tests

Idaho TAFI uses a **benefit-based eligibility determination**. Eligibility is determined through the benefit calculation - if the calculated grant standard is positive, the family is income eligible.

Source: [IDAPA 16.03.08.248-252](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/IDAPA-16.03.08.248)

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

### Earned Income (60% Counted)
For families with earned income, 60% of gross earned income is subtracted from the work incentive table amount.

> "For eligible families with earned income, an amount is calculated by subtracting sixty percent (60%) of gross earned income..."

Source: [IDAPA 16.03.08.252](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/IDAPA-16.03.08.252)

### Unearned Income (100% Counted)
100% of unearned income is counted against benefits.

Source: [IDAPA 16.03.08.250](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/IDAPA-16.03.08.250)

## Income Standards (Work Incentive Table)

| Household Size | Monthly Amount |
|----------------|----------------|
| 1 | $309 |
| 2 | $309 |
| 3 | $389 |
| 4 | $469 |
| 5 | $547 |
| 6 | $628 |
| 7 | $708 |
| 8 | $787 |
| 9 | $867 |
| 10 | $947 |
| 11+ | $947 + $80 per additional person |

Source: [IDAPA 16.03.08.251](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/IDAPA-16.03.08.251)

## Benefit Calculation

```python
# With earned income: use work incentive table
# Without earned income: use maximum grant ($309)
base = where(countable_earned > 0, work_incentive - countable_earned, maximum_grant)
grant_standard = max(base - countable_unearned, 0)
benefit = min(grant_standard, maximum_grant)
```

Source: [IDAPA 16.03.08.248-252](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/IDAPA-16.03.08.248)

## Resource Limit

$5,000 maximum countable resources.

Source: [IDAPA 16.03.08.200](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/IDAPA-16.03.08.200)

## Files Added

### Parameters (6 files)
```
policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/id/tafi/
├── income/
│   └── earned/
│       └── countable_rate.yaml      # 60% counted
├── resources/
│   └── limit.yaml                   # $5,000
├── work_incentive_table/
│   ├── additional_person.yaml       # $80 per person over 10
│   ├── amount.yaml                  # Table by size 1-10
│   └── max_size.yaml                # 10
└── maximum_grant.yaml               # $309
```

### Variables (7 files)
```
policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/id/tafi/
├── id_tafi.py                           # Final benefit
├── eligibility/
│   ├── id_tafi_eligible.py              # Combined eligibility
│   └── id_tafi_resources_eligible.py    # Resource test
└── income/
    ├── id_tafi_countable_earned_income.py   # 60% of gross earned
    ├── id_tafi_countable_unearned_income.py # 100% of unearned
    ├── id_tafi_grant_standard.py            # Grant calculation
    └── id_tafi_work_incentive_amount.py     # Table lookup
```

### Tests (8 files, 42 test cases)
```
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/id/tafi/
├── id_tafi.yaml (4 cases)
├── id_tafi_countable_earned_income.yaml (6 cases)
├── id_tafi_countable_unearned_income.yaml (5 cases)
├── id_tafi_eligible.yaml (9 cases)
├── id_tafi_grant_standard.yaml (2 cases)
├── id_tafi_resources_eligible.yaml (5 cases)
├── id_tafi_work_incentive_amount.yaml (4 cases)
└── integration.yaml (7 cases)
```

## Example Calculations

### Example 1: Family of 3, No Income
- No earned income → use Maximum Grant path
- Grant = $309

### Example 2: Family of 3, $500 Earned Income
- Work Incentive Table: $389
- Countable earned: $500 × 0.60 = $300
- Grant = min($389 - $300, $309) = **$89**

### Example 3: Family of 4, $400 Earned + $100 Unearned
- Work Incentive Table: $469
- Countable earned: $400 × 0.60 = $240
- Grant = min($469 - $240 - $100, $309) = **$129**

## Implementation Notes

### Not Implemented (by design)

| Rule | Section | Reason |
|------|---------|--------|
| $10 minimum threshold | 254 | Grants < $10 not paid - intentionally omitted |
| Rounding to next lowest dollar | 252 | Minor impact - intentionally omitted |
| Self-employment 50% expense deduction | 231 | Future enhancement - currently uses gross self-employment income |
| $50 school attendance penalty | 142 | Requires additional input variable |
| $50 work activity penalty | 169 | Requires additional input variable |
| 24-month time limit | 101 | Cannot simulate (single-period limitation) |
| Paternity establishment penalty | 151 | Cannot simulate (time-based) |

## Key Implementation Decisions

1. **Folder named `tafi`** - Uses Idaho's official program name
2. **Simplified implementation** - Uses federal baseline for demographic and immigration eligibility
3. **Benefit-based eligibility** - Income eligibility determined via grant_standard > 0
4. **Flat maximum grant** - Idaho's $309 max applies regardless of family size
5. **Historical values unchanged** - $309 benefit level has been frozen since late 1990s

## References

- [IDAPA 16.03.08 - Full Rule](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/idaho/title-IDAPA-16/rule-16.03.08)
- [Idaho Department of Health and Welfare - About TAFI](https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/services-programs/financial-assistance/about-tafi)

prs.title: Add Nebraska TANF Program
prs.body:
## Summary

Closes #7040

Implements Nebraska Aid to Dependent Children (ADC), the state's TANF program.

## Regulatory Authority

### Primary Legal Sources

1. **Nebraska Revised Statutes**
   - [Section 43-504](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=43-504): Definition of dependent child (age requirements)
   - [Section 43-512](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=43-512): ADC application, payment level (55% of Standard of Need)
   - [Section 43-513](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=43-513): Standard of Need, CPI adjustment methodology
   - [Section 68-1713](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=68-1713): Gap budgeting methodology
   - [Section 68-1726](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=68-1726): Earned income disregard rates, resource limits

2. **Nebraska Administrative Code Title 468**
   - [Title 468 Overview](https://dhhs.ne.gov/Pages/Title-468.aspx): ADC program regulations
   - [Title 468 NAC Chapter 3 (PDF)](https://dhhs.ne.gov/Guidance%20Docs/Title%20468%20-%20Aid%20to%20Dependent%20Children.pdf#page=9): Income standards table

## Income Eligibility Tests

### Standard of Need Test

Countable income (net earned + unearned) must be strictly less than the Standard of Need for the unit size.

### Earned Income Disregard

| Recipient Status | Disregard Rate | Countable Income |
|-----------------|----------------|------------------|
| Initial applicants | 20% | 80% of gross earned |
| Ongoing recipients | 50% | 50% of gross earned |

- Source: [Neb. Rev. Stat. 68-1726(3)(a)](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=68-1726)

**Note**: Tests use `is_tanf_enrolled` to distinguish between initial applicants (false) and ongoing recipients (true).

## Income Standards

| Unit Size | Need Standard | Payment Standard (55%) |
|-----------|---------------|------------------------|
| 1 | $601 | $331 |
| 2 | $741 | $408 |
| 3 | $881 | $485 |
| 4 | $1,021 | $562 |
| 5 | $1,161 | $639 |
| 6 | $1,301 | $716 |
| 7 | $1,441 | $793 |
| 8 | $1,581 | $870 |
| 9 | $1,721 | $947 |
| 10 | $1,861 | $1,024 |
| Each additional | +$140 | +$77 |

**Formula**: Base (1 person) = $601; each additional person = +$140
**Source**: [Title 468 NAC Chapter 3 (PDF)](https://dhhs.ne.gov/Guidance%20Docs/Title%20468%20-%20Aid%20to%20Dependent%20Children.pdf#page=9)

## Resource Limits

| Unit Size | Resource Limit |
|-----------|----------------|
| 1 person | $4,000 |
| 2+ persons | $6,000 |

**Source**: [Neb. Rev. Stat. 68-1726](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=68-1726)

## Benefit Calculation

### Gap Budgeting Formula

Nebraska uses "Budget the Gap" methodology:

1. **Calculate Net Earned Income**: `Gross Earned Income * (1 - disregard_rate)`
   - Initial applicants: 20% disregard → 80% countable
   - Ongoing recipients: 50% disregard → 50% countable
2. **Calculate Gap**: `Need Standard - Net Earned Income`
3. **Determine Benefit Before Unearned**: `min(Gap, Payment Standard)`
4. **Subtract Unearned Income**: `max(Benefit - Unearned Income, 0)`

**Source**: [Neb. Rev. Stat. 68-1713(1)(p)](https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=68-1713)

## Example Calculation

**Family of 3 with $1,000/month gross earned income (ongoing recipient):**
1. Need Standard (size 3): $881
2. Net Earned Income: $1,000 * 0.50 = $500
3. Gap: $881 - $500 = $381
4. Payment Standard: $881 * 0.55 = $485
5. Benefit: min($381, $485) = $381
6. Final (no unearned): $381

## Files Added

### Parameters (7 files)
```
policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/ne/dhhs/adc/
├── benefit/
│   ├── payment_standard_rate.yaml     # 55% of need standard
│   └── standard_of_need/
│       ├── amount.yaml                # Need standard by unit size
│       └── additional_person.yaml     # +$140 per additional person
├── income/
│   └── earned_income_disregard/
│       ├── initial.yaml               # 20% for applicants
│       └── ongoing.yaml               # 50% for recipients
├── resources/
│   └── limit.yaml                     # $4,000/$6,000 bracket limits
└── max_unit_size.yaml                 # Max table size (10)
```

### Variables (9 files)
```
policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ne/dhhs/adc/
├── ne_adc.py                          # Final benefit amount
├── eligibility/
│   ├── ne_adc_eligible.py             # Overall eligibility
│   ├── ne_adc_income_eligible.py      # Income test
│   └── ne_adc_resources_eligible.py   # Resource test
├── income/
│   ├── ne_adc_countable_income.py     # Total countable income
│   └── ne_adc_countable_earned_income.py # After disregard
└── benefit/
    ├── ne_adc_need_standard.py        # Need standard lookup
    ├── ne_adc_payment_standard.py     # 55% of need standard
    └── ne_adc_maximum_benefit.py      # Gap budgeting result
```

### Tests (9 files, 46 test cases)
```
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ne/dhhs/adc/
├── integration.yaml                   # 7 end-to-end scenarios
├── ne_adc.yaml                        # 5 benefit edge cases
├── ne_adc_eligible.yaml               # 6 combined eligibility tests
├── ne_adc_income_eligible.yaml        # 5 income threshold tests
├── ne_adc_resources_eligible.yaml     # 4 resource limit tests
├── ne_adc_maximum_benefit.yaml        # 4 gap budgeting tests
├── ne_adc_need_standard.yaml          # 6 need standard tests
├── ne_adc_payment_standard.yaml       # 4 payment standard tests
└── ne_adc_countable_earned_income.yaml # 5 disregard tests
```

## Test Coverage

| Test Category | Count | Description |
|---------------|-------|-------------|
| Integration tests | 7 | Full calculation pipeline scenarios |
| Benefit calculations | 5 | Gap budgeting edge cases |
| Combined eligibility | 6 | Income, resource, demographic tests |
| Income eligibility | 5 | Countable income vs need standard |
| Resource eligibility | 4 | Asset limit boundary tests |
| Maximum benefit | 4 | Gap budgeting formula tests |
| Need standard | 6 | Lookup by unit size |
| Payment standard | 4 | 55% calculation |
| Countable earned income | 5 | Initial/ongoing disregard |
| **Total** | **46** | |

## Implementation Notes

1. **Initial vs Ongoing Recipients**: Uses `is_tanf_enrolled` to distinguish between initial applicants (20% earned income disregard) and ongoing recipients (50% disregard). Most integration tests model ongoing recipients.

2. **Resource Limits**: Implemented as bracket-style parameter with different limits for 1 person ($4,000) vs 2+ persons ($6,000).

3. **Non-Simulatable Rules**: Time limits (60-month lifetime limit), work requirements, and transitional benefits cannot be enforced due to PolicyEngine's single-period architecture.

prs.title: Add New Mexico TANF program
prs.body:
## Summary
Closes #7038

Implements the New Mexico TANF program (officially called "New Mexico Works"), administered by the New Mexico Health Care Authority (HCA).

## Regulatory Authority
- [NM TANF State Plan (2024-2026)](https://www.hca.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/TANF-Final-State-Plan-2024-to-2026.pdf)
- [8.102 NMAC - Cash Assistance Programs](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0001.html)
- [8.102.500 NMAC - Eligibility Policy](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0500.html)
- [8.102.520 NMAC - Income](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0520.html)

## Income Eligibility Tests

### Gross Income Test
Gross income must be at or below 85% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines for the benefit group size.
> Source: [8.102.500.8(B) NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0500.html), [State Plan Section 9.8, p.20](https://www.hca.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/TANF-Final-State-Plan-2024-to-2026.pdf#page=20)

### Net Income Test
Countable net income must be at or below the payment standard (standard of need) for the benefit group size.
> Source: [8.102.520.11 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0520.html)

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

### Work Incentive Deduction (Earned Income)
| Family Type | Flat Deduction | Plus Percentage |
|-------------|----------------|-----------------|
| Single-parent families | $125 | + 50% of remainder |
| Two-parent families | $225 per parent | + 50% of remainder |
> Source: [8.102.520.12(C) NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0520.html), [State Plan Section 9.8, p.21](https://www.hca.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/TANF-Final-State-Plan-2024-to-2026.pdf#page=21)

### Child Care Deduction
| Child Age | Maximum Monthly Deduction |
|-----------|---------------------------|
| Under age 2 | $200 per child |
| Age 2 and older | $175 per child |
> Source: [8.102.520.12(D) NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0520.html), [State Plan Section 9.8, p.21](https://www.hca.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/TANF-Final-State-Plan-2024-to-2026.pdf#page=21)

### Child Support Deduction
| Component | Amount |
|-----------|--------|
| Disregard | $50 |
| Passthrough (1 child) | $100 |
| Passthrough (2+ children) | $200 |
> Source: [8.102.520.10 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0520.html)

## Resource Limits

| Resource Type | Limit |
|---------------|-------|
| Liquid resources | $1,500 |
| Non-liquid resources | $2,000 |

> Source: [8.102.510.8 NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0510.html), [State Plan Section 9.7, p.20](https://www.hca.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/TANF-Final-State-Plan-2024-to-2026.pdf#page=20)

## Payment Standards (Historical)

| Benefit Group Size | Aug 2015 (7.5% adj) | Nov 2018 (adj removed) | Aug 2023 (23% increase) |
|-------------------|---------------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| 1 | $244 | $266 | $327 |
| 2 | $327 | $357 | $439 |
| 3 | $409 | $447 | $549 |
| 4 | $493 | $539 | $663 |
| 5 | $576 | $630 | $775 |
| 6 | $659 | $721 | $887 |
| 7 | $743 | $812 | $999 |
| 8 | $843 | $922 | $1,134 |
| Each additional | +$83 | +$91 | +$111 |

> Source: [8.102.500.8(D) NMAC](https://www.srca.nm.gov/parts/title08/08.102.0500.html), [State Plan p.19](https://www.hca.nm.gov/wp-content/uploads/TANF-Final-State-Plan-2024-to-2026.pdf#page=19)

## Benefit Calculation
```
Benefit = Payment Standard - Countable Income

Where:
  Countable Income = Countable Earned + Countable Unearned
  Countable Earned = max(Gross Earned - Work Incentive - Child Care, 0)
  Countable Unearned = max(Gross Unearned - Child Support Deduction, 0)
```

## File Structure

### Variables
```
nm_works/
├── eligibility/
│   ├── nm_works_eligible.py
│   ├── nm_works_gross_income_eligible.py
│   ├── nm_works_net_income_eligible.py
│   └── nm_works_resources_eligible.py
├── income/
│   ├── nm_works_gross_income.py
│   ├── nm_works_countable_income.py
│   ├── earned/
│   │   ├── nm_works_countable_earned_income.py
│   │   └── nm_works_earned_income_deduction_person.py
│   ├── unearned/
│   │   └── nm_works_countable_unearned_income.py
│   └── deductions/
│       ├── nm_works_childcare_deduction.py
│       └── nm_works_child_support_deduction.py
├── nm_works.py
└── nm_works_maximum_benefit.py
```

### Parameters
```
nm_works/
├── income/
│   ├── gross_limit/rate.yaml (85% FPL)
│   └── deductions/
│       ├── work_incentive/ (single_parent, two_parent, rate)
│       ├── childcare/amount.yaml (bracket by age)
│       └── child_support/ (disregard, passthrough)
├── payment_standard/
│   ├── amount.yaml (by size, with history)
│   ├── additional_person.yaml
│   └── max_table_size.yaml
└── resources/limit/ (liquid, non_liquid)
```

## Not Implemented

- Extended age eligibility for special education (18-21)
- Extended age eligibility for high school students (18-19)
- Transition Bonus Program
- Diversion Payment
- Sanctions
- Support Services
- School Clothing Allowance

prs.body:
## Summary

Implements Mississippi's Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program.

Closes #7012

## Regulatory Authority

- [MDHS TANF Eligibility Flyer (2018)](https://www.mdhs.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/MDHS_TANF-Eligibility-Flyer.pdf) - Need standards, payment standards, income limits
- [SB 2759 (2021)](https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2021/html/SB/2700-2799/SB2759SG.htm) - Payment standard increase ($110 → $200 first person)
- [Miss. Code. tit. 18, pt. 19](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/mississippi/Miss-Code-tit-18-pt-19) - TANF State Plan (185% rule, earned income disregards)
- [Mississippi Department of Human Services - Applying for TANF](https://www.mdhs.ms.gov/help/tanf/applying-for-tanf/) - Current gross income limits

## Parameter Time Periods

Parameters include historical values with proper effective dates:

### Need Standard (100% Requirements)

| Family Size | 2018-07-01 | 2025-07-01 |
|-------------|------------|------------|
| 1 | $218 | $339 |
| 2 | $293 | $460 |
| 3 | $368 | $581 |
| 4 | $443 | $702 |
| 5 | $518 | $823 |
| 6 | $593 | $944 |
| 7 | $668 | $1,065 |
| 8 | $743 | $1,186 |
| 9 | $818 | $1,307 |
| 10 | $893 | $1,428 |

- **2018-07-01 values**: Direct from [MDHS TANF Eligibility Flyer (2018)](https://www.mdhs.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/MDHS_TANF-Eligibility-Flyer.pdf) - "100% Requirements" column
- **2025-07-01 values**: Derived from [current MDHS website](https://www.mdhs.ms.gov/help/tanf/applying-for-tanf/) gross income limits ÷ 1.85

### Gross Income Limit (185% of Need Standard)

| Family Size | 2018-07-01 | 2025-07-01 |
|-------------|------------|------------|
| 1 | $403 | $627 |
| 2 | $542 | $851 |
| 3 | $680 | $1,074 |
| 4 | $819 | $1,298 |
| 5 | $958 | $1,522 |
| 6 | $1,097 | $1,746 |
| 7 | $1,235 | $1,970 |
| 8 | $1,374 | $2,194 |
| 9 | $1,513 | $2,417 |
| 10 | $1,652 | $2,641 |

**Source**: [Miss. Code. tit. 18, pt. 19](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/mississippi/Miss-Code-tit-18-pt-19) - "income at or below 185 percent of the need standard"

### Payment Standards (Maximum Monthly Benefit)

| Component | 2018-07-01 | 2021-05-01 |
|-----------|------------|------------|
| First person | $110 | $200 |
| Second person | $36 | $36 |
| Each additional | $24 | $24 |

- **2018-07-01 values**: From [MDHS TANF Eligibility Flyer (2018)](https://www.mdhs.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/MDHS_TANF-Eligibility-Flyer.pdf) - "Maximum TANF Grant" row
- **2021-05-01 increase**: [SB 2759 (2021)](https://billstatus.ls.state.ms.us/documents/2021/html/SB/2700-2799/SB2759SG.htm) increased first person from $110 to $200 (first increase since 1999)

| Family Size | 2018 Amount | 2021+ Amount |
|-------------|-------------|--------------|
| 1 | $110 | $200 |
| 2 | $146 | $236 |
| 3 | $170 | $260 |
| 4 | $194 | $284 |
| 5 | $218 | $308 |

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

- **Simplified Implementation**: Uses federal TANF gross income baseline
- **Time-limited disregards not implemented**: 
  - 6-month total earned income disregard (35+ hrs/week employment within 30 days of approval)
  - 3-month total earned income disregard (case closing due to increased earnings)
  - These cannot be tracked in PolicyEngine's single-period simulation architecture
  - **Source**: [Miss. Code. tit. 18, pt. 19](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/mississippi/Miss-Code-tit-18-pt-19)

## Benefit Calculation

```
Benefit = Maximum Payment Standard - Countable Income
If Benefit < 0, Benefit = $0
```

## Resource Limit

- **Limit**: $2,000 for all households
- **Effective**: 2018-07-01
- **Exclusions**: Primary residence, personal vehicle

**Source**: [MDHS TANF Eligibility Flyer (2018)](https://www.mdhs.ms.gov/wp-content/uploads/2018/02/MDHS_TANF-Eligibility-Flyer.pdf)

## Files

### Parameters (7 files)

```
policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/ms/dhs/tanf/
├── income/
│   └── gross_income_limit_rate.yaml

```

### Variables (6 files)

```
policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ms/dhs/tanf/
├── eligibility/
│   ├── ms_tanf_eligible.py
│   ├── ms_tanf_income_eligible.py
│   └── ms_tanf_resources_eligible.py
├── ms_tanf.py
├── ms_tanf_countable_income.py
└── ms_tanf_maximum_benefit.py
```

### Tests (6 files, 58 tests)

```
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ms/dhs/tanf/
├── integration.yaml (7 tests)
├── ms_tanf.yaml (11 tests)
├── ms_tanf_eligible.yaml (8 tests)
├── ms_tanf_income_eligible.yaml (13 tests)
├── ms_tanf_maximum_benefit.yaml (12 tests)
└── ms_tanf_resources_eligible.yaml (7 tests)
```

## Test Coverage

| Component | Tests | Coverage |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| Benefit calculation | 11 | Zero income, reduced benefits, edge cases |
| Income eligibility | 13 | Family sizes 1-4 + size 11 (cap test), boundary conditions |
| Resources eligibility | 7 | Zero to over limit, boundary at $2,000 |
| Maximum benefit | 12 | Family sizes 1-11 |
| Overall eligibility | 8 | All eligibility combinations |
| Integration | 7 | End-to-end realistic scenarios |

## Example Calculations (using 2025-07-01 values)

### Example 1: Single Parent with One Child, No Income
- Household size: 2
- Gross income: $0
- Need standard (size 2): $460
- Income limit (185%): $851
- Income eligible: $0 ≤ $851 ✓
- Resources: $500 ≤ $2,000 ✓
- Payment standard: $200 + $36 = $236
- **Benefit: $236 - $0 = $236/month**

### Example 2: Family of 3 at Income Threshold
- Household size: 3
- Monthly gross income: $1,074
- Need standard (size 3): $581
- Income limit (185%): $1,074.85
- Income eligible: $1,074 ≤ $1,074.85 ✓
- Payment standard: $200 + $36 + $24 = $260
- **Benefit: $260 - $1,074 = $0** (income exceeds payment standard)

prs.title: Implement Kansas TANF
prs.body:
## Summary
Implements Kansas Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program.

Closes #6935

## Regulatory Authority
- **[K.S.A. 39-709](https://ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch39/039_007_0009.html)**: Cash Assistance Program Statute
- **Kansas Administrative Regulations (K.A.R.) Article 30-4**
  - [K.A.R. 30-4-100](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-100): Payment Standards
  - [K.A.R. 30-4-101](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-101): Basic Standards (by county group)
  - [K.A.R. 30-4-110](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-110): Income
  - [K.A.R. 30-4-111](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-111): Earned Income Disregards
- **[Kansas Economic and Employment Support Manual (KEESM)](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/home.htm)**
  - [KEESM 5000](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm5000.htm): Resources
  - [KEESM 7110](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7110.htm): Income Budgeting
  - [KEESM 7200](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7200.htm): Income Deductions
  - [KEESM 7224](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7224.htm): Dependent Care Deduction
  - [KEESM 7400](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7400.htm): Standards for Budgetary Requirements
- **[KEESM Implementation Memo 2008-0326](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/implem_memo/2008_0326_TAF_ei_disregard.htm)**: 60% Earned Income Disregard
- **[Kansas TANF State Plan FFY 2024-2026](https://www.dcf.ks.gov/services/ees/Documents/Reports/TANF%20State%20Plan%20FFY%202024%20-%202026.pdf)**

## Income Eligibility Tests

| Test | Threshold | Source |
|------|-----------|--------|
| Gross Income | < 30% FPL | [K.S.A. 39-709](https://ksrevisor.gov/statutes/chapters/ch39/039_007_0009.html) |
| Countable Income | < Payment Standard | [KEESM 7110](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7110.htm) |
| Resource Limit | ≤ $3,000 | [KEESM 5000](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm5000.htm) |

## Income Deductions & Exemptions

Per [KEESM 7200](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7200.htm), deductions are applied in order:

| Order | Deduction | Amount | Source |
|-------|-----------|--------|--------|
| 1 | Work Expense | $90/employed person | [KEESM 7200](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7200.htm) |
| 2 | Earned Income Disregard | 60% of remainder | [K.A.R. 30-4-111](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-111), [KEESM Memo 2008-0326](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/implem_memo/2008_0326_TAF_ei_disregard.htm) |
| 3 | Dependent Care | Actual, unreimbursed (NO CAP) | [KEESM 7224](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7224.htm) |

**Note on 60% Disregard:** Per K.A.R. 30-4-111(b)(2), this disregard does NOT apply when initially establishing TANF eligibility unless the person received TANF in one of the four preceding months. PolicyEngine applies this disregard to all applicants since benefit history cannot be tracked.

## Income Standards (Payment Standard - High Population Counties, Group III)

| Family Size | Payment Standard |
|-------------|------------------|
| 1 | $241 |
| 2 | $326 |
| 3 | $403 |
| 4 | $471 |
| 5+ | $471 + $61/person |

*Source: [K.A.R. 30-4-101](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-101), [Kansas TANF State Plan p.29](https://www.dcf.ks.gov/services/ees/Documents/Reports/TANF%20State%20Plan%20FFY%202024%20-%202026.pdf#page=29)*

**County Groups:** Payment standard = Basic allowance + Shelter allowance by county group:
- Group I (Rural): $92 shelter
- Group II: $97 shelter  
- Group III (High Population): $109 shelter - *Used in this implementation*
- Group IV (Urban): $135 shelter

High Population Counties (Group III): Butler, Jefferson, Leavenworth, McPherson, Miami, Osage, Reno, Rice, Riley, Sedgwick, Shawnee, Wyandotte

## Benefit Calculation

```
Countable Earned = max(Gross Earned - $90 - 60% of remainder, 0) - Dependent Care
Countable Income = Countable Earned + Unearned Income
Benefit = max(Payment Standard - Countable Income, 0)
```

*Source: [KEESM 7110](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7110.htm), [KEESM 7200](https://content.dcf.ks.gov/ees/keesm/current/keesm7200.htm)*

## Files

### Variables (9 files)
```
tanf/
├── eligibility/
│   ├── ks_tanf_eligible.py
│   ├── ks_tanf_gross_income_eligible.py
│   ├── ks_tanf_income_eligible.py
│   └── ks_tanf_resources_eligible.py
├── income/
│   ├── ks_tanf_countable_earned_income.py
│   ├── ks_tanf_countable_income.py
│   └── ks_tanf_earned_income_after_deductions.py
├── ks_tanf.py
└── ks_tanf_maximum_benefit.py
```

### Parameters (6 files)
- `resource_limit/amount.yaml` - $3,000 limit
- `income/gross_income_limit.yaml` - 30% FPL
- `income/earned_income_disregard/flat.yaml` - $90
- `income/earned_income_disregard/rate.yaml` - 60%
- `payment_standard/amount.yaml` - By family size
- `payment_standard/additional_person_amount.yaml` - $61

### Tests (9 files, 58 test cases)
- Unit tests for each variable with formula
- Integration tests with 9 end-to-end scenarios

## Known Limitations
- Uses High Population Counties (Group III) payment standards as default
- County-specific payment plans not yet implemented as variable
- Time limits (24/48-month) cannot be enforced (requires benefit history tracking)
- Shared living arrangements not implemented

prs.title: Improve agents and skills with better patterns and rules
prs.body:
## Summary

Version 3.2.4 - Enhances agents, skills, and workflow with clearer rules, better patterns, and streamlined encode-policy phases.

## Version Bump

- **3.1.4 → 3.2.4**

## Workflow Changes (encode-policy)

### Phase Restructuring
- **Phase 4**: Split into 4A (parameter-architect) then 4B (test-creator + rules-engineer in parallel)
- **Phase 5**: Simplified to just changelog, `make format`, push (testing moved to Phase 6)
- **Phase 6**: Step 6A (implementation-validator) → Step 6B (ci-fixer runs tests locally)

### Agent Behavior Changes
- **ci-fixer**: Runs tests LOCALLY using `policyengine-core test` instead of waiting for GitHub CI (30+ min)
- **implementation-validator**: Checks Parameters → Variables → Tests (foundation first)
- **issue-manager**: Hybrid approach - stops and asks if existing issue/PR found; proceeds autonomously if none
- **document-collector**: Notes PDFs in sources.md for future reference, doesn't block workflow

## Agent Renames

- **tanf-program-reviewer → program-reviewer**: Generalized for any government program, not just TANF

## Command Updates

### review-pr
- Added **Step 6: Regulatory Review** using program-reviewer
- Reviews now include: Domain, Reference, Implementation, Test Coverage, Documentation, **Regulatory**

## Skills Updates

### policyengine-parameter-patterns-skill
- Add bracket-style age eligibility pattern (single file vs separate min/max)
- Clarify PDF reference format: `#page=XX` is FILE position (not printed page)
- Add examples for MBTA and SNAP age eligibility

### policyengine-implementation-patterns-skill
- Add "Legal Code is the Source of Truth" principle
- Add `adds` vs `add()` rules with explicit examples
- Add reference format: tuple `()` not list `[]`, no `documentation` field

### policyengine-code-style-skill
- Add pattern for breaking out complex expressions in `where()`, `max_()`
- Add `add() > 0` pattern instead of `spm_unit.any()`

## Agent Updates

### rules-engineer
- Add "Legal Code is the Source of Truth" as first principle
- Add explicit `adds`/`add()` decision tree with wrong/correct examples
- Add person vs group entity level verification
- Add reference format rules

### naming-coordinator
- Restructure to load skills first as source of truth
- Add state-specific program naming table (TEA, OWF, CalWORKs, etc.)
- Add state-specific terminology rules (need standard vs payment standard)

### implementation-validator
- Added aggregation-skill and code-style-skill
- Reordered phases: Parameters → Variables → Tests
- Added rule: variables with `formula` need tests; `adds` variables don't
- Updated report format to output structured fixes for ci-fixer

### ci-fixer
- Added STEP 0: Implement pattern fixes from validator
- Runs tests LOCALLY (not GitHub CI)
- Critical rule: Don't create wrapper variables when test inputs don't match - fix test inputs instead

### program-reviewer (renamed from tanf-program-reviewer)
- Research regulations FIRST before looking at code (prevents confirmation bias)
- Generalized for any government program

## Key Rules Added

| Rule | Description |
|------|-------------|
| Legal code is source of truth | Law comes first, patterns are tools |
| `adds` vs `add()` | `adds=[]` for pure sums, `add()` for sum+ops, never `a+b` |
| `add() > 0` pattern | Instead of `spm_unit.members` + `spm_unit.any()` |
| Reference format | Tuple `()` not list `[]`, no `documentation` field |
| PDF page numbers | FILE position in `#page=XX` (not printed page) |
| Entity verification | Check per-person or per-group (SPMUnit/TaxUnit/Household) |
| State naming | TEA (AR), OWF (OH), CalWORKs (CA) - use official names |
| Test coverage | Variables with `formula` need tests; `adds` don't |
| Test input mismatch | Fix inputs to match federal baseline, don't create wrappers |

## Files Changed

```
.claude-plugin/marketplace.json          (version bump)
CHANGELOG.md                             (3.2.4 entry)
agents/README.md                         (program-reviewer rename)
agents/country-models/ci-fixer.md        (local tests, pattern fixes)
agents/country-models/document-collector.md (PDF handling)
agents/country-models/implementation-validator.md (reordered, new rules)
agents/country-models/issue-manager.md   (hybrid approach)
agents/country-models/program-reviewer.md (renamed from tanf-program-reviewer)
agents/reference-validator.md            (program-reviewer reference)
commands/encode-policy.md                (phase restructuring)
commands/review-pr.md                    (added program-reviewer step)
```

## Test Plan

- [ ] Review encode-policy phase changes
- [ ] Review ci-fixer local test execution
- [ ] Review implementation-validator check order
- [ ] Verify program-reviewer rename across all files
- [ ] Test review-pr includes regulatory review step

prs.title: Add scheduled weekly uv.lock update workflow
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a GitHub Actions workflow that automatically creates PRs to update `uv.lock` on a weekly schedule.

Related to #7000 (standing tracking issue - kept open for recurring PRs)

## Implementation

New file: `.github/workflows/weekly-uv-lock.yaml`

**Schedule:** Every Wednesday at 5 PM EST (10 PM UTC)

**Workflow steps:**
1. Checkout master branch
2. Install uv
3. Run `uv lock --upgrade`
4. If changes detected, create a PR to master using `peter-evans/create-pull-request`

**Features:**
- Never directly modifies master - all changes go through PR review
- Manual trigger available via `workflow_dispatch` for testing
- Auto-deletes the bot branch when PR is closed/merged
- Only runs on the main PolicyEngine repo (not forks)

## Why This Approach

- **Safe**: Master is never directly modified
- **Controllable**: You can close unwanted PRs with no impact
- **Traceable**: All dependency updates go through normal review process
- **Recurring**: Issue #7000 stays open as a tracking issue; weekly PRs reference it but don't close it

prs.title: Early Childhood Prevention Initiative (PI)
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #6778

Implements the Illinois Prevention Initiative (PI) program, administered by the Illinois State Board of Education (ISBE). PI provides early, continuous, and comprehensive child development and family support services to expectant parents and families with children birth to age 3.

## Regulatory Authority

- [ISBE Prevention Initiative Overview](https://www.isbe.net/Pages/Birth-to-Age-3-Years.aspx)
- [ISBE Prevention Initiative Eligibility Form (Weighted Criteria)](https://www.isbe.net/Documents/Prevention-Initiative-Eligibility-Form.pdf)
- [ISBE Prevention Initiative Manual](https://www.isbe.net/Documents/prevention-initiative-manual.pdf)
- [Gov. Pritzker Smart Start FY2024 Press Release](https://www.illinois.gov/news/press-release.29519.html)
- [Gov. Pritzker Smart Start FY2025 Press Release](https://gov-pritzker-newsroom.prezly.com/gov-pritzker-announces-5150-new-preschool-seats-through-smart-start-initiative)

## Program Overview

| Aspect | Prevention Initiative (PI) |
|--------|---------------------------|
| **Target** | Expectant parents & families with children birth to age 3 |
| **Services** | Home visiting, developmental screenings, family support |
| **Funding/Child (FY2024)** | $13,383 (center-based) |
| **Funding/Child (FY2025)** | $13,379 (center-based) |
| **Minimum Score** | 50 points |

## Eligibility Model

Based on the [ISBE Prevention Initiative Eligibility Form](https://www.isbe.net/Documents/Prevention-Initiative-Eligibility-Form.pdf), PI uses a weighted point system:

### Basic Eligibility
- Child under 3 years OR pregnant woman
- Family income ≤ 400% FPL

### Weighted Priority Score

PI assigns points based on risk factors. **Minimum score to be enrolled is 50 points.**

#### Highest Priority Factors (50 points each)

| Factor # | Factor | Modeled | Variable |
|----------|--------|---------|----------|
| 1 | Homeless (McKinney-Vento) | ✅ | `is_homeless` |
| 2 | Youth in Care (foster care) | ✅ | `is_in_foster_care` |
| 3 | Early Intervention (EI) or developmental delay | ✅ | `has_developmental_delay` |
| 4 | Income ≤ 50% FPL and/or TANF | ✅ | `il_pi_is_deep_poverty` |
| 5 | Non-English speaking home | ✅ | `is_non_english_speaking_home` |

> **Note on Factor 3:** The form specifies "Child enrolled in Early Intervention (EI) or the child has been identified through implementation of a research-based child developmental screening tool as having a potential developmental delay." We use `has_developmental_delay` as a proxy since EI enrollment data is not available.

#### Other Priority Factors (25 points each)

| Factor # | Factor | Modeled | Variable |
|----------|--------|---------|----------|
| 6 | Income ≤ 100% FPL | ✅ | `il_pi_is_low_income` |
| 7 | Parent didn't complete high school | ✅ | `parent_has_less_than_high_school_education` |
| 8 | Child/parent born outside US | ✅ | `is_born_outside_us` |
| 9 | Siblings in EI or Special Education | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 10 | Active Duty Military family | ✅ | `military_basic_pay > 0` |
| 11 | Parent currently age 21 or younger | ✅ | `il_pi_is_young_parent_family` |
| 12 | History of low student achievement | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 13 | History of child abuse or neglect | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 14 | History of domestic violence | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 15 | Substance abuse history/needs treatment | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 16 | Tobacco use in home | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 17 | Chronic or terminal illness | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 18 | Household has developmental delay/disability | ✅ | `il_pi_has_developmental_delay` |
| 19 | Mental illness/depression/PTSD | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 20 | Death in immediate family | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 21 | Non-parent caregiver raising child | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 22 | Low birth weight/NICU stay | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 23 | Parent incarcerated/history of incarceration | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 24 | High mobility/transience | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 25 | Child experienced trauma | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 26 | Prenatal diagnosis detected | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 27 | High lead levels | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 28 | Geriatric pregnancy (age 40+) | ✅ | `il_pi_has_geriatric_pregnancy` |
| 29-30 | Program specific | N/A | Community-defined factors |

#### Lower Priority Factors (10 points each)

| Factor # | Factor | Modeled | Variable |
|----------|--------|---------|----------|
| 31 | Receiving services from another agency | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 32 | Socially or geographically isolated | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 33 | Teen parent at birth of first child | ✅ | `il_isbe_was_teen_parent_at_first_birth` |
| 34 | One delay on screening tool | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 35 | Single parent | ✅ | Derived from `is_tax_unit_head_or_spouse` |
| 36 | Poverty (≤ 200% FPL) | ✅ | `il_pi_is_poverty` |
| 37 | Other health issue | ❌ | Requires new input variable |
| 38-39 | Program specific | N/A | Community-defined factors |

### Summary of Modeled Factors

| Category | Total Factors | Modeled | Coverage |
|----------|---------------|---------|----------|
| Highest Priority (50 pts) | 5 | 5 | 100% |
| Other Priority (25 pts) | 25 | 8 | 32% |
| Lower Priority (10 pts) | 9 | 4 | 44% |
| **Total** | **39** | **17** | **44%** |

> **Note:** Public benefits (SNAP, WIC, Medicaid, CCAP) are listed on the eligibility form for **income verification purposes only** - they do not award points. Only TANF receipt awards points as part of Factor 4.

### Eligibility Formula

```
PI Eligible = Demographic Eligible AND Income Eligible AND Risk Eligible

Where:
  Demographic Eligible = Child under 3 OR Pregnant
  Income Eligible = Family income ≤ 400% FPL
  Risk Eligible = Priority Score ≥ 50 points
```

## Income Definition

Shared with PFA/PFAE via `il_isbe_countable_income`. Per ISBE guidelines, countable income includes:
- Earnings from work (gross, before deductions)
- Child support, alimony
- Pensions, retirement, Social Security
- Workers' comp, unemployment, SSI, VA benefits, disability

**Excluded**: SNAP, FDPIR, WIC, TANF, federal education benefits, foster payments

## Benefit Amounts

| Program | FY2024 | FY2025 | Source |
|---------|--------|--------|--------|
| PI (center-based) | $13,383 | $13,379 | Smart Start Press Releases |

Calculations:
- FY2024: $9.39M ÷ 702 children = $13,383
- FY2025: $6.85M ÷ 512 children = $13,379

## New/Updated Variables

### PI-Specific Variables
| Variable | Entity | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `il_pi` | Person | PI benefit amount |
| `il_pi_eligible` | Person | Full PI eligibility |
| `il_pi_demographic_eligible` | Person | Child under 3 or pregnant |
| `il_pi_basic_eligible` | Person | Demographic + income eligible |
| `il_pi_risk_eligible` | Person | Priority score ≥ 50 |
| `il_pi_priority_score` | Person | Total weighted priority score |
| `il_pi_highest_priority_score` | Person | Score from 50-pt factors |
| `il_pi_other_priority_score` | Person | Score from 25-pt factors |
| `il_pi_lower_priority_score` | Person | Score from 10-pt factors |
| `il_pi_is_deep_poverty` | Person | Income ≤ 50% FPL or receives TANF |
| `il_pi_is_low_income` | Person | Income ≤ 100% FPL |
| `il_pi_is_poverty` | Person | Income ≤ 200% FPL |
| `il_pi_is_young_parent_family` | SPMUnit | Any parent ≤ 21 in household |
| `il_pi_has_developmental_delay` | SPMUnit | Household has disability/developmental delay |
| `il_pi_has_geriatric_pregnancy` | SPMUnit | Pregnant woman age 40+ |

### Shared ISBE Variables
| Variable | Entity | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `il_isbe_income_eligible` | Person | Income ≤ 400% FPL (shared with PFA/PFAE) |
| `il_isbe_countable_income` | SPMUnit | Countable income for ISBE programs |
| `il_isbe_was_teen_parent_at_first_birth` | SPMUnit | Was teen at first child's birth |

### New Demographic Input Variables
| Variable | Entity | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `is_non_english_speaking_home` | Household | Primary language not English |
| `has_developmental_delay` | Person | Has a developmental delay |
| `parent_has_less_than_high_school_education` | Household | Parent didn't complete HS |
| `is_born_outside_us` | Person | Born outside the US |
| `has_no_prior_formal_early_learning` | Person | No prior formal early learning |

### Parameters
| Parameter | Value | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.benefit.amount` | $13,383 (2024), $13,379 (2025) | Per-child funding (center-based) |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.eligibility.age_threshold.child` | 3 | Max age for child eligibility |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.eligibility.age_threshold.young_parent` | 21 | Max age for young parent factor |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.eligibility.risk_factors.minimum_score` | 50 | Minimum score for enrollment |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.eligibility.priority.geriatric_pregnancy_age` | 40 | Age threshold for geriatric pregnancy |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.eligibility.income.deep_poverty_rate` | 0.5 | 50% FPL threshold |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.eligibility.income.low_income_rate` | 1.0 | 100% FPL threshold |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.pi.eligibility.income.poverty_rate` | 2.0 | 200% FPL threshold |

## Test Coverage

- Unit tests for each variable with formula
- Integration tests with realistic family scenarios
- Priority score calculation tests with multiple factor combinations
- Boundary tests including 45-point ineligible case and age 21 threshold
- **57 total test cases**

prs.title: Illinois Preschool For All (PFA) & Expansion (PFAE)
prs.body:
## Summary

Fixes #6776 (PFA)
Fixes #6777 (PFAE)

Implements the Illinois Preschool For All (PFA) and Preschool For All Expansion (PFAE) programs, administered by the Illinois State Board of Education (ISBE).

## Regulatory Authority

- [ISBE Preschool For All Overview](https://www.isbe.net/pages/preschool-for-all.aspx)
- [ISBE PDG Enrollment Form (Weighted Eligibility)](https://www.isbe.net/Documents/pdg-eg-grant-enrollment-form.pdf#page=2)
- [ISBE Household and Income Form (69-72)](https://www.isbe.net/Documents/69-72_hshld_income.pdf)
- [23 IAC § 235.10 - Definitions](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/illinois/Ill-Admin-Code-tit-23-SS-235.10)
- [105 ILCS 5/2-3.71(a)(4.5) - Preschool for All Children (4x poverty guidelines)](https://law.onecle.com/illinois/105ilcs5/2-3.71.html)
- [105 ILCS 5/10-20.12 - Kindergarten enrollment age (age 5 by Sept 1)](https://law.onecle.com/illinois/105ilcs5/10-20.12.html)
- [Gov. Pritzker Smart Start FY2024 Press Release](https://www.illinois.gov/news/press-release.29519.html)
- [Gov. Pritzker Smart Start FY2025 Press Release](https://gov-pritzker-newsroom.prezly.com/gov-pritzker-announces-5150-new-preschool-seats-through-smart-start-initiative)

## Program Overview

| Aspect | PFA | PFAE |
|--------|-----|------|
| **Hours** | Part-day: 2.5 hrs/day | Full-day: 5+ hrs/day |
| **Meals** | Snack only | Breakfast + Lunch + Snack |
| **Funding/Child (FY2024)** | $3,900 | $8,500 |
| **Funding/Child (FY2025)** | $3,900 | $8,500 |
| **Services** | Basic preschool | Comprehensive + family support |

**Note:** PFA and PFAE share identical eligibility criteria. A child receives one or the other based on local program availability, not both simultaneously.

## PFAE Eligibility Model

Based on the [ISBE PDG Enrollment Form](https://www.isbe.net/Documents/pdg-eg-grant-enrollment-form.pdf#page=2), PFAE uses a weighted point system:

### Basic Eligibility
- Age 3-5 years (before kindergarten per 105 ILCS 5/10-20.12)
- Family income ≤ 400% FPL (per 105 ILCS 5/2-3.71(a)(4.5))

### Highest Priority Factors (50 points each)
*If a child has any one of these factors, they are directly enrolled in PFAE:*

| # | Factor | Variable |
|---|--------|----------|
| 1 | Homeless (McKinney-Vento) | `is_homeless` |
| 2 | Child welfare involvement (foster care) | `is_in_foster_care` |
| 3 | Has IEP or referred for special education | `has_individualized_education_program` |
| 4 | Family income ≤ 50% FPL and/or receiving TANF | `il_pfae_is_deep_poverty` or `il_tanf > 0` |

### Secondary Priority Factors (25 points each)
*Children with 2+ of these factors qualify for PFAE:*

| # | Factor | Variable |
|---|--------|----------|
| 5 | Family income ≤ 100% FPL | `il_pfae_is_low_income` |
| 6 | Parent didn't complete high school | `parent_has_less_than_high_school_education` (Household) |
| 7 | Teen parent at birth of first child (under 20) | `il_isbe_was_teen_parent_at_first_birth` (SPMUnit) |
| 8 | Child/parent born outside US | `is_born_outside_us` |
| 9 | Non-English speaking home | `is_non_english_speaking_home` (Household) |
| 10 | Active Duty Military family | `military_basic_pay > 0` |
| 11 | Developmental delays (without IEP) | `has_developmental_delay` |
| 12 | Never attended formal early learning | `has_no_prior_formal_early_learning` |

### Eligibility Formula

```
PFAE Eligible = Basic Eligible AND (any highest priority factor OR 2+ secondary priority factors)

Where:
  Basic Eligible = Age 3-5 AND Income ≤ 400% FPL
```

## Income Definition

Per [ISBE Form 69-72](https://www.isbe.net/Documents/69-72_hshld_income.pdf), countable income includes:
- Earnings from work (gross, before deductions)
- Child support, alimony
- Pensions, retirement, Social Security
- Workers' comp, unemployment, SSI, VA benefits, disability

**Excluded**: SNAP, FDPIR, WIC, TANF, federal education benefits, foster payments

## Benefit Amounts

| Program | FY2024 | FY2025 | Source |
|---------|--------|--------|--------|
| PFA | $3,900 | $3,900 | Smart Start Press Releases |
| PFAE | $8,500 | $8,500 | Smart Start Press Releases |

Calculations:
- **PFA FY2024**: $20.99M ÷ 5,383 children = $3,900
- **PFA FY2025**: $15.63M ÷ 4,008 children = $3,900
- **PFAE FY2024**: $4.28M ÷ 503 children = $8,500
- **PFAE FY2025**: $9.70M ÷ 1,142 children = $8,500

## New Variables

### IL ISBE Shared Variables
| Variable | Entity | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `il_isbe_countable_income` | SPMUnit | ISBE countable income for eligibility |
| `il_isbe_income_eligible` | Person | Income ≤ 400% FPL eligibility |
| `il_isbe_was_teen_parent_at_first_birth` | SPMUnit | Parent was under 20 at birth of first child |

### Demographic Input Variables
| Variable | Entity | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `is_born_outside_us` | Person | Person was born outside the United States |
| `has_no_prior_formal_early_learning` | Person | Child has NOT attended formal early learning program |
| `has_individualized_education_program` | Person | Has Individualized Education Program (IEP) |
| `has_developmental_delay` | Person | Has screening-indicated developmental delay |
| `is_non_english_speaking_home` | Household | Household primary language is not English |
| `parent_has_less_than_high_school_education` | Household | Parent didn't complete high school |

### PFA Variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `il_pfa` | PFA benefit amount |
| `il_pfa_eligible` | PFA eligibility (mirrors PFAE) |

### PFAE Eligibility Variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `il_pfae_eligible` | Main PFAE eligibility determination |
| `il_pfae_basic_eligible` | Age and income eligibility combined |
| `il_pfae_age_eligible_child` | Age 3-5 eligibility |

### PFAE Priority Variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `il_pfae_has_highest_priority_factor` | Has any 50-point factor |
| `il_pfae_secondary_priority_factor_count` | Count of 25-point factors |
| `il_pfae_is_deep_poverty` | Income ≤ 50% FPL |
| `il_pfae_is_low_income` | Income ≤ 100% FPL |

### PFAE Benefit Variables
| Variable | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `il_pfae` | PFAE benefit amount |

## Parameters

| Parameter Path | Value | Description |
|----------------|-------|-------------|
| `gov.states.il.isbe.income.income_limit_rate` | 4.0 | 400% FPL max income |
| `gov.states.il.isbe.income.countable_sources` | list | Income sources for ISBE programs |

prs.title: Add Arkansas Transitional Employment Assistance (TEA)
prs.body:
## Summary

Implements Arkansas Transitional Employment Assistance (TEA) program.

Closes #6970

---

## Arkansas TEA Income Rules

### Regulatory Authority
- **TEA Policy Manual** (effective 01/01/2023): https://humanservices.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/TEA_MANUAL-10.1.24.pdf
- **208.00.13 Ark. Code R. Section 001** (TEA Program State Plan)
- **016.20.98-041 Ark. Code R.** (TEA Policy 2352-2362, Work Expense/Incentive Deductions)

---

### 1. INCOME ELIGIBILITY TEST

#### Net Income Test (Section 2101, 2353.1)
- **Limit:** $513/month (applies to ALL family sizes, effective 01/01/2023)
- Countable income (after deductions) must be at or below $513

Source: [TEA Manual Section 2101, page 13](https://humanservices.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/TEA_MANUAL-10.1.24.pdf#page=13)

---

### 2. INCOME DEDUCTIONS & EXEMPTIONS (Section 2352)

#### A. Work Expense Deduction (Initial & Ongoing)

| Deduction | Rate |
|-----------|------|
| Work-related expense | 20% of gross earned income |

#### B. Work Incentive Deduction (Ongoing Recipients Only)

| Deduction | Rate |
|-----------|------|
| Work incentive | 60% of remaining earned income after work expense |

**Note:** Initial applicants receive only the 20% work expense deduction. Ongoing recipients receive both 20% work expense + 60% work incentive.

Source: [TEA Manual Section 2352, page 89](https://humanservices.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/TEA_MANUAL-10.1.24.pdf#page=89)

---

### 3. PAYMENT STANDARDS BY FAMILY SIZE (Section 2361)

| Family Size | Payment Standard |
|-------------|-----------------|
| 1 | $81 |
| 2 | $162 |
| 3 | $204 |
| 4 | $247 |
| 5 | $286 |
| 6 | $331 |
| 7 | $373 |
| 8 | $415 |
| 9+ | $457 |

Source: [TEA Manual Section 2361, page 92](https://humanservices.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/TEA_MANUAL-10.1.24.pdf#page=92)

---

### 4. RESOURCE LIMIT

| Limit | Amount |
|-------|--------|
| Maximum countable resources | $3,000 |

**Exempt resources:** Homestead, one operable motor vehicle, household and personal goods, income-producing property, IDA/escrow accounts.

Source: [TEA Manual Section 2101, page 13](https://humanservices.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/TEA_MANUAL-10.1.24.pdf#page=13)

---

### 5. BENEFIT CALCULATION (Section 2362)

#### Countable Income Calculation:
- **Initial applicants:** `(Gross Earned × 0.80) + Gross Unearned`
- **Ongoing recipients:** `(Gross Earned × 0.80 × 0.40) + Gross Unearned`

#### Benefit Formula:
- **If gross income < $1,026:** `Benefit = max(Payment Standard − Countable Income, 0)`
- **If gross income ≥ $1,026:** `Benefit = Payment Standard × 0.5` (no subtraction)

The $1,026 trigger (effective 01/01/2023) causes a 50% reduction when gross income exceeds this threshold.

Source: [TEA Manual Section 2362, page 93](https://humanservices.arkansas.gov/wp-content/uploads/TEA_MANUAL-10.1.24.pdf#page=93)

---

### 6. OTHER REQUIREMENTS

- **Immigration status:** Must have at least one U.S. citizen or qualified immigrant in the household
- **Time limits:** 12 months (state), 60 months (federal) - effective 04/01/2024

---

prs.title: Experiment: Faster CI timing
prs.body:
Fixes #6962

## Summary

Optimizes CI test job distribution to reduce total CI runtime by rebalancing workloads across parallel jobs.

## Changes

### Job restructuring
- Move NY state tests from States → Baseline job (NY was a major bottleneck)
- Move Python tests from Structural → States job
- **Split contrib/states into per-state batches** to prevent memory accumulation (RI alone uses 5.2 GB)
- Rename jobs to reflect actual content:
  - States (excl NY) & Python
  - Baseline (incl NY) & Reform
  - Structural (States) — each state runs in own subprocess
  - Structural (Other) — 7 memory-balanced batches including congress

### Results

| Job | Before | After | Delta |
|-----|--------|-------|-------|
| States (excl NY) & Python | 23m 59s | ~8m 10s | **-15m 49s** |
| Baseline (incl NY) & Reform | 9m 22s | ~12m 43s | +3m 21s |
| Structural (States) | 15m 17s | ~15m | ~same |
| Structural (Other) | 20m 4s | ~13m | **-7m** |

**Total CI time (slowest job): ~24m → ~15m = ~9 min faster**

---

## CI Job Breakdown

### 1. States (excl NY) & Python

| Batch | Path | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **1** | `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/` | `--exclude ny` (46 states + tax/) |
| **2** | `pytest policyengine_us/tests/` | All Python tests |

**States included:** `al, ar, az, ca, co, ct, dc, de, ga, hi, ia, id, il, in, ks, ky, la, ma, md, me, mi, mn, mo, ms, mt, nc, nd, ne, nh, nj, nm, oh, ok, or, pa, ri, sc, tx, ut, va, vt, wa, wi, wv` + `tax/`

---

### 2. Baseline (incl NY) & Reform

| Batch | Path | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **1** | `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ny/` | NY only |
| **2** | `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/` | `--exclude states` |
| **3** | `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/household/` | |
| **4** | `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/contrib/` | |
| **5** | `policyengine_us/tests/policy/reform/` | `ctc_expansion.yaml`, `winship.yaml` |

---

### 3. Structural (States) — Per-State Batches

Each state folder runs in its own subprocess with garbage collection between them. This prevents memory accumulation that was causing CI failures when adding new state folders.

| 1 | `dc` | 1.7 GB |

**New state folders are automatically picked up as separate batches.**

### 4. Structural (Other) — 7 Memory-Balanced Batches

| **1** | `federal`, `harris`, `treasury` | ~9.0 GB |

reviews.title: Add Emergency Medicaid for undocumented immigrants
reviews.body:
## Summary

Implements Emergency Medicaid eligibility for individuals who are ineligible for regular Medicaid due to immigration status but meet all other Medicaid eligibility requirements and have an emergency medical condition.

Closes #7003

## Regulatory Authority

This implementation is based on:

- **42 USC 1396b(v)(2)** - Exception for emergency services for aliens
  - (v)(2)(A): Person is not otherwise eligible due to immigration status
  - (v)(2)(B): Person meets all applicable Medicaid eligibility requirements except immigration status
  - (v)(2)(C): Organ transplant procedures are excluded
- **42 USC 1396b(v)(3)** - Definition of emergency medical condition
- **8 USC 1611(b)(1)(A)** - Exception for emergency medical care from public benefits restrictions
- **42 CFR 440.255** - Federal regulations on emergency services
- **42 CFR 435.406** - Citizenship and noncitizen eligibility

## Eligibility Requirements

Per the statute, Emergency Medicaid eligibility requires **all three** conditions:

1. **Immigration Status**: Person is NOT eligible for regular Medicaid due to immigration status (uses existing `is_medicaid_immigration_status_eligible` variable)
2. **Medicaid Requirements**: Person meets all other Medicaid eligibility requirements including income and categorical eligibility (uses existing `medicaid_category` variable)
3. **Emergency Condition**: Person has an emergency medical condition as defined in 42 USC 1396b(v)(3)

## Files Added

### Parameters (5 files)
```
policyengine_us/parameters/gov/hhs/medicaid/emergency_medicaid/
├── index.yaml                        # Metadata (economy: false, household: false)
├── enabled.yaml                      # Program enabled from 1987
├── emergency_condition_definition.yaml  # Statutory definition criteria
├── organ_transplant_exclusion.yaml   # Organ transplant exclusion per (v)(2)(C)
└── uses_medicaid_income_thresholds.yaml  # Income threshold requirement
```

### Variables (2 files)
```
policyengine_us/variables/gov/hhs/medicaid/emergency_medicaid/
├── has_emergency_medical_condition.py   # Input variable (boolean)
└── is_emergency_medicaid_eligible.py    # Eligibility calculation
```

### Tests (3 files, 57 test cases)
```
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/hhs/medicaid/emergency_medicaid/
├── has_emergency_medical_condition.yaml  # 3 unit tests
├── is_emergency_medicaid_eligible.yaml   # 34 unit tests
└── integration.yaml                      # 20 integration tests
```

## Test Coverage (57 tests)

| Test Category | Count | Description |
|--------------|-------|-------------|
| Unit tests - eligible cases | 12 | All immigration statuses and Medicaid categories |
| Unit tests - ineligible (regular Medicaid) | 8 | Citizens, LPRs, refugees, asylees |
| Unit tests - no emergency | 2 | Missing emergency condition |
| Unit tests - no Medicaid category | 3 | Income too high |
| Unit tests - edge cases | 9 | Pre-1987, condition combinations |
| Integration tests | 20 | Full pipeline with household structures |
| Input variable tests | 3 | has_emergency_medical_condition |

## Example Calculation

**Scenario**: Undocumented adult (age 35) with emergency medical condition and $18,000 income

1. `is_medicaid_immigration_status_eligible`: false (undocumented)
2. `medicaid_category`: ADULT (income < 138% FPL in expansion state)
3. `has_emergency_medical_condition`: true

**Result**: `is_emergency_medicaid_eligible` = true

Formula: `enabled & has_emergency & (medicaid_category != NONE) & ~immigration_eligible`

## Implementation Notes

- Uses existing `medicaid_category` variable which handles all income/categorical eligibility checks
- Uses existing `is_medicaid_immigration_status_eligible` variable for immigration status
- `has_emergency_medical_condition` is an input variable (boolean) since emergency conditions are determined by medical providers, not calculated
- Program enabled starting 1987 (OBRA '86 created Emergency Medicaid)
- Parameters marked with `economy: false` and `household: false` since this is person-level eligibility

## References

- [42 USC 1396b(v)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396b#v) - Emergency services exception
- [8 USC 1611(b)(1)(A)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/8/1611#b_1_A) - Emergency medical care exception
- [42 CFR 440.255](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/440.255) - Emergency services regulations
- [42 CFR 435.406](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/435.406) - Noncitizen eligibility

reviews.title: Medicare savings program
reviews.body:
Fixes #6893

## Summary

This PR corrects the Medicare Savings Program (MSP) implementation to align with federal statutory requirements. Key fixes:

1. **FPL Unit Size**: Uses individual/couple FPL instead of SPM unit size
2. **Income Methodology**: Applies SSI income exclusions per statutory requirement
3. **Parameter Updates**: Adds historical values and proper legal citations

---

## FPL Unit Size Fix

**Legal References**:
- [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - Income "determined under section 1382a" (SSI methodology)
- [SSA POMS SI 01715.010](https://secure.ssa.gov/apps10/poms.nsf/lnx/0501715010) - Specifies "individual" and "couple" resource limits

**Rationale**: MSP follows SSI methodology, which uses individual or eligible couple as the unit. SSI does not include children or other household members in the income/resource unit. Medicare.gov also publishes limits only for "Individual" and "Married couple" categories.

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `spm_unit_fpg` which calculated FPL based on the full SPM unit size (could be 3, 4, 5+ people).

**Fix**: Created `msp_fpg` variable that returns:
- Individual FPL (1 person) if unmarried
- Couple FPL (2 persons) if married

---

## Income Methodology Fix

**Legal Reference**: [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)(B)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) - "income (determined under section 1382a of this title)"

Section 1382a is the SSI income determination methodology ([42 U.S.C. § 1382a](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1382a)), which requires:
1. $20 general income exclusion (from unearned first)
2. $65 earned income exclusion
3. 50% of remaining earned income excluded

**Issue**: The previous implementation used `adjusted_gross_income_person` without any exclusions.

**Fix**: Updated `msp_countable_income` to use SSI income variables and apply the `_apply_ssi_exclusions()` function.

---

## Published Limits vs Our Approach

Medicare.gov publishes income limits that are approximately $20/month higher than raw FPL thresholds. This is because they include the $20 general exclusion in the threshold.

Our implementation applies the $20 exclusion to income instead:
- **Our approach**: `(income - $20) <= FPL`
- **Published approach**: `income <= (FPL + $20)`

These are mathematically equivalent.

---

## Income Limit Legal Citations

| Category | FPL % | Legal Reference |
|----------|-------|-----------------|
| QMB | 100% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(i)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_i), [42 U.S.C. § 1396d(p)(1)-(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396d#p) |
| SLMB | 120% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iii)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iii) |
| QI | 135% | [42 U.S.C. § 1396a(a)(10)(E)(iv)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/42/1396a#a_10_E_iv) |

---

## Test Plan

- [x] All 19 MSP tests pass
- [x] Unit tests for `msp_fpg`, `msp_category`, `msp_eligible`, `msp_benefit_value`
- [x] Integration tests for complete eligibility pipeline
- [x] Tests document calculation methodology with inline comments
