Adds the Illinois HFS Family Planning Program, a Medicaid-funded program providing reproductive health services to eligible Illinois residents.

**Key eligibility rules implemented:**
- Income limit: 213% FPL (208% + 5% disregard)
- Fixed household size of 2 for FPL calculation (Illinois uses the federal option under 42 CFR § 435.603(k) to count individual + 1)
- Only the applicant's individual income is counted (not household income)
- Must NOT be pregnant
- Must NOT be enrolled in full Medicaid
- Must meet immigration/citizenship requirements (ongoing program only)

**Files added:**
- Parameters: `household_size.yaml`, `income_limit.yaml`
- Variables: `il_fpp_income_level.py`, `il_fpp_income_eligible.py`, `il_fpp_eligible.py`
- Tests: 11 tests (unit + integration)

**References:**
- [DHS MR #22.28 Family Planning](https://www.dhs.state.il.us/page.aspx?item=146077)
- [HFS Family Planning Program](https://hfs.illinois.gov/medicalclients/familyplanning.html)
- [42 CFR § 435.603(k)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/435.603#k) - Federal authority for fixed household size

**Note:** The 213% FPL income limit is documented in administrative guidance (DHS MR #22.28) rather than statute. The parameter file includes a comment noting this.

reviews.body:
## Summary

Implements Michigan Family Independence Program (FIP), the state's TANF cash assistance program.

Closes #7013

---

## Michigan FIP Income Rules

### Regulatory Authority
- **Michigan DHHS BEM 518** - FIP/RCA/SDA Income Budgeting
- **Michigan DHHS BEM 520** - Computing the FIP/RCA/SDA Budget
- **Michigan DHHS BEM 400** - Assets
- **Michigan TANF State Plan 2023/2025**

---

### 1. INCOME ELIGIBILITY TESTS

#### Qualifying Deficit Test (New Applicants)
- **Applies to:** New applicants only
- **Deduction rate:** 20% of remaining earned income after flat $200 deduction
- **Test:** Countable income < Payment Standard

Source: [BEM 520 Section C (p.3)](https://mdhhs-pres-prod.michigan.gov/olmweb/EX/BP/Public/BEM/520.pdf#page=3)

#### Issuance Deficit Test (Enrolled Recipients)
- **Applies to:** Currently enrolled recipients
- **Deduction rate:** 50% of remaining earned income after flat $200 deduction
- **Test:** Countable income < Payment Standard

Source: [BEM 520 Section D (p.4)](https://mdhhs-pres-prod.michigan.gov/olmweb/EX/BP/Public/BEM/520.pdf#page=4)

---

### 2. INCOME DEDUCTIONS & EXEMPTIONS

#### A. Earned Income Flat Deduction

| Deduction Type | Amount |
|----------------|--------|
| Flat (per working person) | $200 |

**Critical:** Deduction applies **per person** - each worker in the household receives their own $200 deduction.

Source: [BEM 518 (p.5)](https://mdhhs-pres-prod.michigan.gov/olmweb/ex/BP/Public/BEM/518.pdf#page=5)

#### B. Earned Income Percentage Deduction

| Purpose | Percentage | Effective Date |
|---------|------------|----------------|
| Initial eligibility (qualifying) | 20% | 2008-10-01 |
| Benefit calculation (issuance) | 50% | 2011-01-01 |

**Applied to:** Remaining earned income after $200 flat deduction

Source: [BEM 518 (p.5)](https://mdhhs-pres-prod.michigan.gov/olmweb/ex/BP/Public/BEM/518.pdf#page=5)

---

### 3. INCOME STANDARDS BY FAMILY SIZE

| Family Size | Payment Standard (2017) | Payment Standard (2024) |
|-------------|------------------------|------------------------|
| 1 | $306 | $363 |
| 2 | $403 | $478 |
| 3 | $492 | $583 |
| 4 | $597 | $707 |
| 5 | $694 | $822 |
| 6 | $828 | $981 |
| 7 | $905 | $1,072 |
| 8+ | +$80/person | +$95/person |

Source: [Michigan TANF State Plan 2017 (p.7)](https://www.michigan.gov/-/media/Project/Websites/mdhhs/Folder1/Folder33/TANF_State_Plan_2017.pdf#page=7), [Reference Table 210](https://mdhhs-pres-prod.michigan.gov/olmweb/ex/RF/Public/RFT/210.pdf#page=1)

---

### 4. BENEFIT CALCULATION

#### Formula:
```
Benefit = Payment Standard − Countable Income
```

Where **Countable Income** (per person) =
```
max(Gross Earned − $200 − 50% of Remainder, 0) + Gross Unearned
```

#### Calculation Steps (Per Person):
1. Determine gross earned income for each working person
2. Subtract $200 flat deduction from each person's earnings
3. Subtract 50% of remaining earned income (for benefit calculation)
4. Result cannot go below $0
5. Sum all persons' countable earned income
6. Add gross unearned income = **Total Countable Income**
7. Benefit = Payment Standard − Countable Income

#### Example: Two-Earner Household (Family of 4)
```
Parent 1: $800 earned
  Step 1: $800 - $200 = $600 remainder
  Step 2: $600 × 50% = $300 deduction
  Step 3: $600 - $300 = $300 countable

Parent 2: $400 earned
  Step 1: $400 - $200 = $200 remainder
  Step 2: $200 × 50% = $100 deduction
  Step 3: $200 - $100 = $100 countable

Total Countable = $300 + $100 = $400
Payment Standard (size 4, 2024) = $707
Benefit = $707 - $400 = $307/month
```

Source: [BEM 520 Section F](https://mdhhs-pres-prod.michigan.gov/olmweb/EX/BP/Public/BEM/520.pdf)

---

### 5. RESOURCE LIMITS

| Period | Resource Limit |
|--------|----------------|
| 2008-10-01 | $3,000 |
| 2019-01-01 | $15,000 |

Source: [BEM 400 (p.1)](https://mdhhs-pres-prod.michigan.gov/olmweb/EX/BP/Public/BEM/400.pdf#page=1)

---

## Variables Implemented

- `mi_fip` - Main benefit amount
- `mi_fip_eligible` - Overall eligibility
- `mi_fip_income_eligible` - Income eligibility (dual-test)
- `mi_fip_resources_eligible` - Resource eligibility
- `mi_fip_payment_standard` - Payment standard by family size
- `mi_fip_countable_income_for_eligibility` - Countable income (20% rate)
- `mi_fip_countable_income_for_benefit` - Countable income (50% rate)
- `mi_fip_countable_earned_income_for_eligibility` - Earned income after 20% deduction
- `mi_fip_countable_earned_income_for_benefit` - Earned income after 50% deduction
- `mi_fip_earned_income_after_deductions_for_eligibility_person` - Per-person 20% deduction
- `mi_fip_earned_income_after_deductions_for_benefit_person` - Per-person 50% deduction

## Test Coverage

- 66 unit and integration tests covering all variables

---

reviews.body:
## Summary

Implements Georgia Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) cash assistance program.

Closes #6790

---

## Georgia TANF Income Rules

### Regulatory Authority
- **Georgia Administrative Code 290-2-28** - TANF Regulations
- **PAMMS TANF Policy Manual** - Sections 1525, 1605, 1615

---

### 1. INCOME ELIGIBILITY TESTS

#### Gross Income Test
- **Limit:** 185% of Standard of Need (SON)
- **Definition:** Total gross earned + unearned income, prior to deductions
- **Consequence:** When gross income > limit, application is denied

Source: [Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 290-2-28-.02(j)](https://rules.sos.ga.gov/gac/290-2-28-.02), [PAMMS 1605 Step 6](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/tanf/1605/)

#### Net Income Test
After passing the gross income test, countable income (after deductions) must be below the Standard of Need (SON)

Source: [PAMMS 1605 Step 11](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/tanf/1605/)

---

### 2. INCOME DEDUCTIONS & EXEMPTIONS

#### A. Work Expense Deduction

| Deduction Type | Amount |
|----------------|--------|
| Standard work expense (per employed individual) | $250 |

**Critical:** Deduction applies **per person** - each employed individual receives their own $250 deduction.

Source: [PAMMS 1615](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/tanf/1615/)

#### B. Childcare Deduction

| Child Age | Maximum Deduction |
|-----------|-------------------|
| Under age 2 | $200/month per child |
| Age 2 and older | $175/month per child |

- Applies to dependent children (`is_tax_unit_dependent`)
- Capped at actual `childcare_expenses`
- Applied to earned income only (after work expense)

Source: [PAMMS 1615](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/tanf/1615/)

#### C. Unearned Income
- **No deductions allowed** to unearned income
- Full amount counts toward countable income

Source: [PAMMS 1605](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/tanf/1605/)

---

### 3. INCOME STANDARDS BY FAMILY SIZE

| Family Size | Standard of Need (SON) | Gross Income Ceiling (185%) | Family Maximum |
|-------------|------------------------|----------------------------|----------------|
| 1 | $235 | $435 | $155 |
| 2 | $356 | $659 | $235 |
| 3 | $424 | $784 | $280 |
| 4 | $500 | $925 | $330 |
| 5 | $573 | $1,060 | $378 |
| 6 | $621 | $1,149 | $410 |
| 7 | $672 | $1,243 | $444 |
| 8 | $713 | $1,319 | $470 |
| 9 | $751 | $1,389 | $496 |
| 10 | $804 | $1,487 | $530 |
| 11+ | +$24/person | +$44/person | +$17/person |

> **Note:** These values have not changed since 1997 (frozen since AFDC era).

Source: [PAMMS Appendix A](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/tanf/appendix-a/), [1997 Green Book Table 7-8](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GPO-CPRT-105WPRT37945/html/GPO-CPRT-105WPRT37945-2-7.htm)

---

### 4. BENEFIT CALCULATION

#### Formula:
```
Benefit = min(Standard of Need − Countable Income, Family Maximum)
```

Where **Countable Income** =
```
max(Sum of each person's (Gross Earned − $250), 0) − Childcare Deduction + Gross Unearned
```

#### Calculation Steps (Per PAMMS 1605):
1. Determine gross earned income for each employed person
2. Subtract $250 work expense from each person's earnings
3. Sum all persons' net earned income
4. Subtract childcare deduction (earned income only)
5. Result cannot go below $0
6. Add gross unearned income = **Countable Income**
7. Calculate deficit: SON − Countable Income
8. Benefit = min(Deficit, Family Maximum)

#### Example: Working Single Parent with 2 Children
```
Income: $500 earned + $100 unearned

Step 1: Gross Income Test
  GIC = $424 × 1.85 = $784
  Gross = $600 < $784 ✅ PASSES

Step 2: Calculate Countable Income
  Earned after work expense: $500 - $250 = $250
  No childcare deduction (assume no expenses)
  Unearned: $100
  Countable = $250 + $100 = $350

Step 3: Net Income Test
  SON (size 3) = $424
  $350 < $424 ✅ PASSES

Step 4: Benefit Calculation
  Deficit = $424 - $350 = $74
  Family Maximum (size 3) = $280
  Benefit = min($74, $280) = $74/month
```

Source: [PAMMS 1605](https://pamms.dhs.ga.gov/dfcs/tanf/1605/)

---

### 5. RESOURCE LIMITS

| Resource Type | Limit |
|---------------|-------|
| Countable resources (cash assets) | $1,000 |

Source: [Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 290-2-28-.13](https://rules.sos.ga.gov/gac/290-2-28-.13)

---

## Variables Implemented

- `ga_tanf` - Main benefit amount
- `ga_tanf_eligible` - Overall eligibility
- `ga_tanf_income_eligible` - Income eligibility (gross and net tests)
- `ga_tanf_resources_eligible` - Resource eligibility
- `ga_tanf_standard_of_need` - Standard of Need by family size
- `ga_tanf_family_maximum` - Family Maximum by family size
- `ga_tanf_gross_income_ceiling` - 185% × SON
- `ga_tanf_countable_income` - Net countable income
- `ga_tanf_earned_income_after_disregard` - Per-person earned income after $250 deduction
- `ga_tanf_childcare_deduction` - Childcare deduction by age

## Test Coverage

- 49 unit and integration tests covering all variables

---

reviews.body:
## Summary

Implements Montana Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) program.

Closes #6397

---

## Montana TANF Income Rules

### Regulatory Authority
- **MT DPHHS TANF Manual** (Chapters 001-705)
- **Montana Administrative Rules** (ARM 37.78.xxx)
- **TANF State Plan** ([Income Standards, p.10](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/TANF/TANFStatePlan.pdf#page=10))

---

### 1. Income Eligibility Tests

#### Gross Monthly Income (GMI) Test
- **Limit:** Net Income Standard x 1.85
- **Definition:** Total gross earned + unearned income of all assistance unit members

Source: [TANF 001 Monthly Income Standards](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/TANF001.pdf)

#### Benefit Standard Test
- **Limit:** 30% of FPG for the assistance unit size
- **Definition:** Countable income (after all disregards/deductions) must be below the benefit standard

Source: [TANF State Plan - Income Standards, p.10](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/TANF/TANFStatePlan.pdf#page=10)

#### Payment Standard Test
- **Limit:** 35% of FPG for the assistance unit size
- **Definition:** Countable income must be below the payment standard

Source: [TANF State Plan - Income Standards, p.10](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/TANF/TANFStatePlan.pdf#page=10)

---

### 2. Income Deductions & Exemptions

#### A. Work-Related Expense Deduction
- **Amount:** $200/month flat deduction from gross earned income per person

Source: [TANF 602-1 Income Disregards](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/tanf602-1jan012018.pdf), [ARM 37.78.406(2)(a)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.406)

#### B. Earned Income Disregard
- **Amount:** 25% of remaining earned income (after work expense deduction)

Source: [TANF 602-1 Income Disregards](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/tanf602-1jan012018.pdf), [ARM 37.78.406(2)(b)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.406)

#### C. Dependent Care Deduction
- **Amount:** Up to $200/month per eligible dependent child or incapacitated adult

Source: [TANF 602-1 Income Disregards](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/tanf602-1jan012018.pdf), [ARM 37.78.406(2)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.406)

#### D. Child Support Obligation Deduction
- **Amount:** Legally-binding child support paid to non-household members is subtracted from countable income

Source: [TANF 602-1 Income Disregards (step d)](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/tanf602-1jan012018.pdf)

---

### 3. Income Standards (FPG-Based)

All standards are derived from the Federal Poverty Guidelines for the assistance unit size:

| Standard | Formula |
|----------|---------|
| Payment Standard | FPG x 0.35 |
| Benefit Standard | FPG x 0.30 |
| Net Income Standard | Benefit Standard / 0.785 |
| Gross Income Standard | Net Income Standard x 1.85 |

Source: [TANF State Plan - Income Standards, p.10](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/TANF/TANFStatePlan.pdf#page=10), [TANF 001 Monthly Income Standards](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/TANF001.pdf)

---

### 4. Benefit Calculation

#### Formula:
```
Benefit = Payment Standard - Countable Income
```

Where **Countable Income** =
```
max(Countable Earned Income + Gross Unearned Income - Dependent Care Deduction - Child Support Expense, 0)
```

And **Countable Earned Income** (per person) =
```
(Gross Earned Income - $200 work expense) - 25% of remainder
```

#### Calculation Steps:
1. Determine gross earned income per person
2. Subtract $200 work-related expense deduction
3. Subtract 25% earned income disregard from remainder
4. Sum across assistance unit members = Countable Earned Income
5. Add gross unearned income
6. Subtract dependent care deduction
7. Subtract child support obligation
8. Subtract countable income from Payment Standard = **Benefit**

Source: [ARM 37.78.420](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.420), [TANF 602-1 Income Disregards](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/tanf602-1jan012018.pdf)

---

### 5. Additional Program Rules

#### Work Requirements

| Household Type | Required Hours/Week |
|----------------|-------------------|
| Single parent, youngest child < 6 | 27 |
| Single parent, youngest child >= 6 | 33 |
| Two-parent household (each able parent) | 33 |

- Incapacitated parents are excluded from the two-parent determination (treated as single-parent for hours)
- Disabled persons and eligible children are exempt from work requirements

Source: [TANF 705-1 Participation Hours](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/TANF705.1.pdf)

#### Resource Limit
- **Limit:** $3,000

Source: [ARM 37.78.401](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.401), [TANF 402-1 Countable and Excluded Resources](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/TANF4021May012021.pdf)

#### Assistance Unit Exclusions
- Persons receiving SSI are excluded ([ARM 37.78.220](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.220))
- Persons in foster care are excluded ([ARM 37.78.208](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.206))

#### Immigration Status
- Qualified noncitizen statuses accepted: Refugee, Asylee, Deportation Withheld, Paroled 1+ Year, Conditional Entrant, Legal Permanent Resident, Cuban/Haitian Entrant

Source: [ARM 37.78.220](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/montana/Mont-Admin-r-37.78.220)

---

### 6. Known Limitation: FPG Year Not Pinned

The income standards in this implementation are derived from the **current period's FPG**. However, Montana's [TANF 001 manual](https://dphhs.mt.gov/assets/hcsd/tanfmanual/TANF001.pdf) (effective July 2025) shows all cash assistance standards are still based on the **2023 FPL** — they have not updated to 2024 or 2025 FPL. This means the implementation will overstate standards for simulation periods after 2023 (e.g., payment standard of ~$439 for AU=1 in 2024 vs actual $425).

Pinning the FPG lookup to the 2023 year will be addressed in a follow-up PR. See [#6824](https://github.com/PolicyEngine/policyengine-us/issues/6824) for full details and historical timeline.

issues.title: Mississippi TANF: Implement 6-month and 3-month earned income disregards
issues.body:
## Summary

The Mississippi TANF implementation (PR #7011) does not currently model the time-limited earned income disregards due to PolicyEngine's single-period simulation architecture.

## What's Missing

Mississippi TANF provides two earned income disregard options that are not implemented:

### 6-Month Total Earned Income Disregard
- **Amount**: 100% of earned income disregarded
- **Requirements**:
  - Full-time employment (35+ hours/week)
  - At or above federal minimum wage
  - Must find job within 30 days of TANF approval OR within 30 days of starting job readiness activities
- **Limit**: One-time only per case

### 3-Month Total Earned Income Disregard
- **Amount**: 100% of earned income disregarded
- **Requirements**:
  - Case would otherwise close due to increased earnings
  - Employed at least 25 hours/week at minimum wage
- **Limits**:
  - Cannot combine with 6-month disregard
  - Can use again after 12-month break in assistance

## Source

[Miss. Code. tit. 18, pt. 19 - TANF State Plan](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/mississippi/Miss-Code-tit-18-pt-19)

## Why Not Implemented

These disregards require tracking temporal state that PolicyEngine's single-period simulation cannot model:
- How long has the person been on TANF?
- When did they start employment?
- Have they used the disregard before?
- How many months remain in their disregard period?

## Possible Future Solutions

1. Add multi-period simulation support to PolicyEngine Core
2. Create input variables allowing users to specify disregard eligibility manually
3. Model a simplified "average case" assumption

issues.title: Kansas TANF: Implement additional county groups and living situations
issues.body:
### Summary

The current Kansas TANF implementation uses only **Group III (High Population Counties)** payment standards for **Non-Shared Living** arrangements. Kansas actually has three county groups and two living situation types, each with different payment standards.

### What's Missing

#### 1. County Groups Not Implemented
Kansas divides counties into three groups with different shelter allowances:
- **Group I** (Rural): $91 shelter allowance
- **Group II** (Semi-Urban): $100 shelter allowance  
- **Group III** (High Population): $109 shelter allowance ← *Currently implemented*

#### 2. Living Situations Not Implemented
- **Non-Shared Living**: Higher payment standard ← *Currently implemented*
- **Shared Living**: Lower payment standard (no shelter allowance)

### Regulatory References

| Source | Link |
|--------|------|
| Kansas TANF State Plan FFY 2024-2026 | [DCF Report](https://www.dcf.ks.gov/services/ees/Documents/Reports/TANF%20State%20Plan%20FFY%202024%20-%202026.pdf#page=29) |
| K.A.R. 30-4-100 (Payment Standards) | [Law Cornell](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-100) |
| K.A.R. 30-4-101 (Basic Standards) | [Law Cornell](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/kansas/K-A-R-30-4-101) |

### Current Simplification

The implementation assumes all Kansas households:
1. Live in High Population Counties (Group III)
2. Have Non-Shared Living arrangements

This provides the **highest** payment standard, which may overestimate benefits for rural households or those in shared living situations.

### To Fully Implement

Would require:
1. County-to-group mapping (which Kansas counties are in which group)
2. Living situation variable (shared vs non-shared)
3. Parameter structure with all 6 combinations (3 groups × 2 living types)

Add an option (or prompt) to ask users before posting to GitHub:

```
Would you like to:
1. Post findings to GitHub (default)
2. Show findings locally only (no GitHub post)
```

### Implementation Options

**Option A: Prompt during execution**
- After generating the review/summary, ask the user before posting
- Use `AskUserQuestion` tool to get confirmation

**Option B: Command argument**
- Add `--local` or `--no-post` flag to skip GitHub posting
- Example: `/review-pr 6390 --local`

**Option C: Both**
- Support the flag for scripting
- Default to prompting when flag not provided

## Files to Update

issues.title: Refactor medicaid_group to use state-level override pattern for state-funded Medicaid programs
issues.body:
## Problem

PR #7005 (Illinois HBI) adds state-specific logic directly into the federal `medicaid_group` variable. This approach doesn't scale well - if other states add similar programs (like California FFYP), the federal file will become cluttered with state-specific code.

Current implementation in `medicaid_group.py`:
```python
# Illinois HBI-specific mapping (for those who fail immigration check
# but are eligible via state-funded HBI program)
il_hbi_eligible = person("il_hbi_eligible", period)
age = person("age", period)
p_hbi = parameters(period).gov.states.il.hfs.hbi.eligibility
il_hbi_child = il_hbi_eligible & (age <= p_hbi.child.max_age)
# ... more Illinois-specific logic
```

## Proposed Solution

Create a generic state override pattern:

1. **New file**: `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/il/hfs/hbi/il_hbi_medicaid_group.py`
   - Returns appropriate `MedicaidGroup` for HBI-eligible people
   - Returns `NONE` for everyone else

2. **New file**: `policyengine_us/variables/gov/hhs/medicaid/costs/state_medicaid_group_override.py`
   - Aggregates all state-level Medicaid group overrides
   - Future state programs just add their variable to this file

3. **Edit**: `policyengine_us/variables/gov/hhs/medicaid/costs/medicaid_group.py`
   - Remove state-specific logic
   - Add generic check for state override at the end:
   ```python
   state_override = person("state_medicaid_group_override", period)
   has_override = state_override != MedicaidGroup.NONE
   return where(has_override, state_override, federal_group)
   ```

## Benefits

- Keeps federal variables clean of state-specific logic
- Scales to multiple states without modifying federal files
- State logic stays in state folders (`gov/states/il/...`)
- Follows existing patterns (similar to how `is_medicaid_eligible` handles state programs)

## Related

- #7005 - Illinois Medicaid for undocumented immigrants

issues.title: Add Tennessee Families First Differential Grant Payment Amount (DGPA)
issues.body:
## Summary

The Tennessee Families First implementation currently only provides the Standard Payment Amount (SPA). Certain assistance groups are eligible for the higher Differential Grant Payment Amount (DGPA), which is not yet implemented.

## Regulatory Authority

[Tennessee Administrative Code § 1240-01-50-.20 (2021)](https://publications.tnsosfiles.com/rules/1240/1240-01/1240-01-50.20210701.pdf#page=26)

## DGPA Eligibility

Assistance groups qualify for DGPA when the caretaker meets one of these exemptions:
- Age 60 or older
- Disabled
- Caring for a disabled household member
- No eligible adult in the assistance group (child-only cases)

## DGPA Calculation

Per the regulation:
- **Family sizes 1-5:** DGPA = SPA + $100
- **Family sizes 6+:** DGPA = SPA (same as standard payment)

For family size 3, DGPA represents 31.4% of the Consolidated Need Standard.

## Current Status

- Parameters exist in `parameters/gov/states/tn/dhs/ff/payment/dgpa/` but are not used
- Code includes a comment noting DGPA is not modeled:
  ```python
  # NOTE: Tennessee has a Differential Grant Payment Amount (DGPA) for
  # caretakers who are age 60+, disabled, or provide care for disabled.
  # This is not currently modeled; we only return the Standard Payment Amount (SPA).
  ```

## Implementation Notes

Would require:
1. New eligibility variable for DGPA qualification
2. Modify benefit calculation to use DGPA when eligible
3. Add tests for DGPA scenarios

issues.title: Childcare subsidy programs should use *_before_lsr income variables to avoid LSR circular dependency
issues.body:
## Summary

Childcare subsidy programs flow into `household_net_income` via `household_state_benefits`. When Labor Supply Response (LSR) is enabled in microsimulation, programs that use LSR-affected income variables (like `employment_income`) can create circular dependencies or incorrect results.

This blocks SNAP from using `childcare_expenses` (the policy-correct net amount after subsidies) instead of `pre_subsidy_childcare_expenses`.

## The Cycle

```
employment_income (includes LSR behavioral response)
    │
    ▼
Childcare subsidy eligibility/calculation
    │
    ▼
Subsidy amount → household_state_benefits → household_net_income
    │
    ▼
relative_income_change (compares baseline vs reform)
    │
    ▼
income_elasticity_lsr → employment_income_behavioral_response
    │
    ▼
employment_income ← CYCLE
```

## Current State Audit

| Program | Income Variable Used | Status |
|---------|---------------------|--------|
| MA CCFA | `employment_income_before_lsr`, `self_employment_income_before_lsr` | ✅ Correct |
| CA CalWORKs Child Care | `earned_income` | ❌ Needs fix |
| CO CCAP | `snap_earned_income` (uses `employment_income`) | ❌ Needs fix |
| NE Child Care Subsidy | `spm_unit_net_income` | ❌ Needs fix |
| NC SCCA | `employment_income`, `self_employment_income` | ❌ Needs fix |
| DC CCSP | `employment_income`, `self_employment_income` | ❌ Needs fix |
| IL CCAP | `employment_income`, `self_employment_income` | ❌ Needs fix |
| TX CCS | `employment_income`, `self_employment_income` | ❌ Needs fix |

## Proposed Fix

### 1. Update parameter files to use `*_before_lsr` versions

For NC, DC, IL, TX - update their income source parameter files:
```yaml
# Change FROM:
- employment_income
- self_employment_income

# Change TO:
- employment_income_before_lsr
- self_employment_income_before_lsr
```

### 2. Create `earned_income_before_lsr` variable

For CA CalWORKs which uses `earned_income`:
```python
class earned_income_before_lsr(Variable):
    value_type = float
    entity = Person
    label = "Earned income (before labor supply response)"
    unit = USD
    definition_period = YEAR
    adds = ["employment_income_before_lsr", "self_employment_income_before_lsr"]
```

### 3. Fix CO CCAP

Either create `snap_earned_income_before_lsr` or change the parameter to use base income sources.

### 4. Fix NE Child Care Subsidy

Replace `spm_unit_net_income` with appropriate income components that don't include benefits.

### 5. Add NC to `childcare_expenses.py`

NC SCCA is in `household_state_benefits` but missing from the childcare subsidy list:
```python
STATES_WITH_CHILD_CARE_SUBSIDIES = ["CA", "CO", "NE", "MA"]  # Add "NC"
```

### 6. Update SNAP to use `childcare_expenses`

Once childcare subsidies are fixed, SNAP can use the policy-correct net childcare expenses.

## Broader Context

This same pattern applies to **all benefit programs** in `household_net_income`. Any benefit that:
1. Is included in `household_benefits` or `household_state_benefits`
2. Uses LSR-affected income variables (`employment_income`, `self_employment_income`, `earned_income`, `spm_unit_net_income`)

...should be updated to use `*_before_lsr` versions to ensure correct microsimulation results when LSR is enabled.

## Files Affected

- `policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/nc/ncdhhs/scca/income/sources.yaml`
- `policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/dc/dhs/ccsp/income/countable_income/sources.yaml`
- `policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/il/dhs/ccap/income/countable_income/sources.yaml`
- `policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/tx/twc/ccs/income/sources.yaml`
- `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ca/cdss/tanf/child_care/eligibility/ca_calworks_child_care_meets_work_requirement.py`
- `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/co/ccap/co_ccap_countable_income.py`
- `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/ne/dhhs/child_care_subsidy/ne_child_care_subsidy.py`
- `policyengine_us/variables/household/expense/childcare/childcare_expenses.py`

- [Miss. Code. tit. 18, pt. 19](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/mississippi/Miss-Code-tit-18-pt-19) - TANF State Plan
- [Mississippi Department of Human Services - TANF](https://www.mdhs.ms.gov/help/tanf/)

## Program Rules

### Income Eligibility (185% of Need Standard)

| Family Size | Need Standard | Gross Income Limit (185%) |
|-------------|---------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | $339 | $627 |
| 2 | $460 | $851 |
| 3 | $581 | $1,075 |
| 4 | $702 | $1,299 |
| 5 | $823 | $1,523 |
| 6 | $944 | $1,746 |
| 7 | $1,065 | $1,970 |
| 8 | $1,186 | $2,194 |
| 9 | $1,307 | $2,418 |
| 10 | $1,428 | $2,642 |

### Payment Standards (MS Code 43-17-5)

| Family Size | Calculation | Amount |
|-------------|-------------|--------|
| 1 | $200 | $200 |
| 2 | $200 + $36 | $236 |
| 3 | $200 + $36 + $24 | $260 |
| 4 | $200 + $36 + $24 x 2 | $284 |
| 5 | $200 + $36 + $24 x 3 | $308 |

### Resource Limit

- **$2,000** for all households (effective July 1, 2019 - Hope Act)
- **Exclusions**: Primary residence, personal vehicle

### Benefit Formula

```
Benefit = Maximum Payment Standard - Countable Income
If Benefit < 0, Benefit = $0
```

## Implementation Status

- [x] Need standard parameters (10 household sizes)
- [x] Gross income limit rate (185%)
- [x] Payment standard parameters (first person, second person, additional person)
- [x] Resource limit ($2,000)
- [x] Income eligibility variable
- [x] Resources eligibility variable
- [x] Overall eligibility variable (demographic + immigration + income + resources)
- [x] Maximum benefit calculation
- [x] Countable income calculation
- [x] Final benefit calculation
- [x] Unit tests for all variables
- [x] Integration tests with realistic scenarios

## Files Added

### Parameters (7 files)

```

├── income/
│   └── gross_income_limit_rate.yaml
├── need_standard/
│   ├── amount.yaml

├── payment_standard/

│   ├── first_person.yaml

└── resources/
    └── limit.yaml

### Variables (6 files)

├── eligibility/
│   ├── ms_tanf_eligible.py
│   ├── ms_tanf_income_eligible.py
│   └── ms_tanf_resources_eligible.py
├── ms_tanf.py
├── ms_tanf_countable_income.py
└── ms_tanf_maximum_benefit.py
```

### Tests (6 files, 55 tests)

```
policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/ms/dhs/tanf/
├── integration.yaml (7 tests)
├── ms_tanf.yaml (11 tests)
├── ms_tanf_eligible.yaml (8 tests)
├── ms_tanf_income_eligible.yaml (12 tests)
├── ms_tanf_maximum_benefit.yaml (10 tests)
└── ms_tanf_resources_eligible.yaml (7 tests)
```

## Test Coverage

| Component | Tests | Coverage |
|-----------|-------|----------|
| Benefit calculation | 11 | Zero income, reduced benefits, edge cases |
| Income eligibility | 12 | All family sizes 1-4, boundary conditions |
| Resources eligibility | 7 | Zero to over limit, boundary at $2,000 |
| Maximum benefit | 10 | Family sizes 1-10 |
| Overall eligibility | 8 | All eligibility combinations |
| Integration | 7 | End-to-end realistic scenarios |

## Example Calculations

### Example 1: Single Parent with One Child, No Income
- Household size: 2
- Gross income: $0
- Need standard (size 2): $460
- Income limit (185%): $851
- Income eligible: $0 <= $851 = Yes
- Resources: $500 <= $2,000 = Yes
- Payment standard: $200 + $36 = $236
- **Benefit: $236/month**

### Example 2: Family of 3 with Low Income
- Household size: 3
- Monthly gross income: $500
- Need standard (size 3): $581
- Income limit (185%): $1,074.85
- Income eligible: $500 <= $1,074.85 = Yes
- Payment standard: $200 + $36 + $24 = $260
- Countable income: $500
- **Benefit: $260 - $500 = $0** (income exceeds payment standard)

### Example 3: Family of 4, No Income
- Household size: 4
- Gross income: $0
- Need standard (size 4): $702
- Income limit (185%): $1,298.70
- Income eligible: $0 <= $1,298.70 = Yes
- Resources: $2,000 <= $2,000 = Yes
- Payment standard: $200 + $36 + $24 + $24 = $284
- **Benefit: $284/month**

## Implementation Notes

- **Simplified income calculation**: Uses federal TANF gross income baseline without Mississippi-specific deductions
- **Time-limited disregards not implemented**: Mississippi's 6-month and 3-month total earned income disregards cannot be tracked in PolicyEngine's single-period simulation architecture
- **Federal eligibility baselines used**: Demographic eligibility (age, child presence) and immigration eligibility use federal TANF baseline rules

uv.lock not updated when version number changes on merge
issues.body:
## Problem

When a PR is merged to `master`, the version number gets bumped (e.g., `v1.458.0 -> v1.458.1`), but `uv.lock` is not updated to reflect this change.

As a result, after running `git pull upstream master`, contributors still need to run `uv lock --upgrade` to sync the lock file with the new version - even though that version change was already included in the pull.

## Expected Behavior

`git pull upstream master` should include an up-to-date `uv.lock` that matches the current version number.

## Suggested Solution

Update `uv.lock` as part of the version bump / merge process so the lock file stays in sync with the version number.

## Summary

Fixes #6894

Per form instructions, the previous implementation incorrectly floored ALL income sources at 0 if negative. This PR updates the logic to only floor the specific income sources that the form explicitly says "If negative, enter 0":

**Lines that require flooring:**
- **Net business income**: `farm_income`, `self_employment_income`, `partnership_s_corp_income`

## Summary

Fixes #6984 - Maine Dependent Exemption Credit now correctly includes dependents age 17+ who qualify for the federal Credit for Other Dependents (ODC).

## Changes

Changed the `defined_for` condition in `me_dependent_exemption_credit_amount_person.py` from `ctc_qualifying_child` to `is_tax_unit_dependent` to correctly include all dependents eligible under IRC Section 24.

**Before:** Only included children under age 17 (CTC-qualifying)  
**After:** Includes all tax unit dependents (both CTC and ODC-qualifying)

## Legal Basis

**Maine Statute 36 M.R.S. §5219-SS** states taxpayers qualify if they "were eligible to claim the federal child tax credit **pursuant to the Code, Section 24**"

**IRC Section 24(h)(4) - Credit for Other Dependents** explicitly includes dependents age 17+ as part of Section 24, so they satisfy Maine's eligibility requirement.

**ME Form 1040ME Instructions (Line 13a)** confirms: "Enter the number of qualifying children and dependents for whom you are eligible to claim the **federal child tax credit or the credit for other dependents**"

## Testing

Added comprehensive integration tests in `integration.yaml` that verify:
- Age 17 dependents qualify for the credit
- Age 18+ dependents qualify for the credit  
- Mixed households with both CTC and ODC-qualifying dependents work correctly

reviews.title: Fix AZ property tax credit income definition (exclude exemptions)
reviews.body:
## Summary
Fixes #6956 by implementing Option 3: creating a new `az_property_tax_credit_agi` variable that correctly calculates income for property tax credit purposes.

## Changes
- **Created new variable**: `az_property_tax_credit_agi.py` that calculates AGI per ARS 43-1072(H)(6) and Arizona Admin Code R15-2C-502
  - Uses Federal AGI + Arizona additions - Arizona subtractions
  - **Does NOT subtract Arizona exemptions** (aged, blind, etc.) unlike `az_agi`
- **Updated parameter**: Modified `income_sources.yaml` to use `az_property_tax_credit_agi` instead of `az_agi`
- **Added test**: Created test case demonstrating the fix for the issue scenario (75-year-old with $3,766.08 AGI)

## Why This Fix is Correct
Per ARS 43-1072(H)(6) and Arizona Admin Code R15-2C-502, the property tax credit uses a custom definition of "adjusted gross income" that:
- Starts with Federal AGI
- Adds certain Arizona-specific items
- Subtracts certain Arizona-specific items
- **Does NOT subtract Arizona exemptions** (the $2,100 aged exemption, blind exemption, etc.)

The previous implementation incorrectly used `az_agi`, which subtracts exemptions as part of the regular Arizona income tax calculation.

## Test Results
- ✅ New test for issue scenario passes (AGI of $3,766.08 correctly calculated, not $1,666.08)
- ✅ All existing property tax credit tests pass

## References
- [ARS 43-1072](https://www.azleg.gov/viewdocument/?docName=https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01072.htm)
- [Arizona Admin Code R15-2C-502](https://apps.azsos.gov/public_services/Title_15/15-02.pdf)

reviews.title: Fix flat Social Security taxation for parametric reforms
reviews.body:
## Summary
- Separated Social Security taxation parameters to match each statutory percentage in IRC Section 86 independently
- Refactored Social Security taxation formula to use properly separated parameters
- This enables parametric reforms to achieve flat 85% taxation with just 3 parameter changes

## Changes
- Created 5 new parameter files to separate each occurrence of percentages in the statute:
  - `tier1_benefit_cap.yaml` - 50% cap on benefits for tier 1 (§86(a)(1)(A))
  - `tier1_excess.yaml` - 50% rate on excess for tier 1 (§86(a)(1)(B))  
  - `tier1_bracket.yaml` - 50% rate for bracket calculation (§86(a)(2)(A)(ii))
  - `tier2_excess.yaml` - 85% rate on excess for tier 2 (§86(a)(2)(A)(i))
  - `tier2_benefit_cap.yaml` - 85% cap on benefits for tier 2 (§86(a)(2)(B))
- Refactored the formula to use the `p = parameters...` pattern
- Used default parameter in select() instead of True

## Minimal Reform for Flat 85% Taxation
With the separated parameters, a flat 85% tax on Social Security benefits can now be achieved with just 3 parameter changes:
1. `gov.irs.social_security.taxability.combined_income_ss_fraction`: 0.5 → 1.0
2. `gov.irs.social_security.taxability.threshold.base[SINGLE]`: 25000 → 0
3. `gov.irs.social_security.taxability.threshold.adjusted_base[SINGLE]`: 34000 → 0

This works because with fraction=1.0 and thresholds=0, the excess equals 100% of SS benefits, so tier2_taxable = min(0.85 × SS, 0.85 × SS) = 0.85 × SS

Fixes #6540

reviews.title: Fix `ny_ctc_pre_2024.py` formula
reviews.body:
Fixes #6510

  **What was broken:**
  Families with investment income (like interest or dividends) were only getting $100 NY Child Tax Credit when they should get $330.

  **Why it was broken:**
  The formula was checking if families had wages/earned income. If they didn't have wages, it gave them $0 federal CTC, even though they could claim the credit using their tax liability from investment income.

  **What I fixed:**
  Removed the earned income restriction for the non-refundable portion of the federal CTC. The credit now properly considers tax liability from all income sources, not just wages.

  **The fix:**
  ```python
  # Before: Incorrectly required earned income
  federal_ctc = min_(max_federal_ctc, ctc_phase_in)  # Wrong - zeros out if no wages

  # After: Correctly uses tax liability
  non_refundable_ctc = min_(max_federal_ctc, limiting_tax)  # Uses actual tax liability
  refundable_ctc = ...  # Still requires earned income
  federal_ctc = non_refundable_ctc + refundable_ctc

  Test results:
  - ✅ Family with $48k interest income: Now gets $330 (was incorrectly $100)
  - ✅ Family with $0 income: Still gets $100 minimum (working correctly)

  Who this helps:

#### Income Subtractions (ip25.pdf page 12)

### 3. Food Sales Tax Credit - SUNSET After 2024

The food sales tax credit sunsets after tax year 2024 per [HB 2106](https://www.kslegislature.gov/li_2024/b2023_24/measures/documents/summary_sb_169_2023) (state food sales tax reduced to 0% on 1/1/2025).

### 4. New Programs to Model

#### A. Pregnancy Resource Act Credit (K-94) - Priority: High
**New for tax years 2024+** - [K.S.A. 79-32,309](https://www.ksrevenue.gov/prtaxcredits-pregnancy.html)

- **Credit**: 70% of contributions to eligible charitable organizations
- **Caps**: $5M per organization, $10M statewide annually

**Files to create:**

**New for tax years 2024-2028** - [K.S.A. 74-32,286](https://www.ksrevenue.gov/prtaxcredits-workforce.html)

#### C. Additional AGI Subtractions - Priority: Medium

- **First-Time Home Buyer Savings Subtraction**: Up to $6,000 (MFJ) or $3,000 (others) - K.S.A. 79-32,117(c)(xxv)
- **KPERS/Teacher Retirement Subtraction**: Full exclusion - K.S.A. 79-32,117(c)(iii)

#### D. Additional Exemptions - Priority: Medium

### 5. Tests to Add

## Implementation Checklist

issues.body:
## Summary

Update the Oklahoma individual income tax implementation for tax year 2025. This includes adding 2025 references to all parameters, updating any changed values, and identifying new programs that could be modeled.

## Reference Document

**Primary Source**: [2025 Oklahoma Individual Income Tax Forms and Instructions for Nonresidents and Part-Year Residents (Form 511-NR-Pkt)](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/individuals/current/511-NR-Pkt.pdf)

**Additional 2025 Forms**:
- [2025 Form 511-Pkt (Resident Instructions)](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/individuals/current/511-Pkt.pdf)
- [2025 Form 538-H (Property Tax Credit)](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/individuals/current/538-H.pdf)
- [2025 Form 538-S (Sales Tax Credit)](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/individuals/current/538-S.pdf)
- [2025 Form 511-EIC (Earned Income Credit Worksheet)](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/individuals/current/511-EIC.pdf)
- [2025 Form 511-CR (Other Credits)](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/tax-credits/511-CR.pdf)

---

## Part 1: Parameter Value Updates

### 1.1 Pension Subtraction Limit (CRITICAL UPDATE)
**File**: `policyengine_us/parameters/gov/states/ok/tax/income/agi/subtractions/pension_limit.yaml`

**Current value**: $10,000 (since 2021)
**New value for 2024+**: $20,000

**Reference**: [HB 2020](https://www.okhouse.gov/posts/news-20230324_4) increased the Oklahoma income tax exemption for retirement benefits from $10,000 to $20,000 beginning in tax year 2024.

**Action**: Add new entry `2024-01-01: 20_000` and add 2025 Form 511-Pkt reference (page 17)

---

## Part 2: Add 2025 References to All Parameters

All parameters below require adding a 2025 reference entry. Even if values are unchanged, we must document the 2025 source with page numbers.

### 2.1 Tax Rate Files (5 files)
Each rate file needs 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt reference (page 38 for tax tables):

| File | Reference to Add |
|------|------------------|
| `rates/single.yaml` | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=38 |
| `rates/joint.yaml` | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=38 |
| `rates/head_of_household.yaml` | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=38 |
| `rates/separate.yaml` | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=38 |
| `rates/surviving_spouse.yaml` | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=38 |

**2025 Tax Rates** (unchanged from 2024):
- Brackets: 0.25%, 0.75%, 1.75%, 2.75%, 3.75%, 4.75%
- Top rate (4.75%) begins at $7,200 (single) / $14,400 (joint)

### 2.2 Deduction Files (2 files)

| File | Current Value | 2025 Reference |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| `deductions/standard/amount.yaml` | Single: $6,350, Joint: $12,700, HoH: $9,350 | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=10 |
| `deductions/itemized/limit.yaml` | $17,000 | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=10 |

### 2.3 Exemption Files (3 files)

| File | Current Value | 2025 Reference |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| `exemptions/amount.yaml` | $1,000 | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=10 |

| `exemptions/special_agi_limit.yaml` | Varies by filing status | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=9 |

### 2.4 AGI Subtraction Files (4 files)

**Note**: Oklahoma EITC is 5% of federal EITC calculated using 2020 federal requirements, refundable since 2022.

### 2.6 Child/CDCC Credit Files (3 files)

| File | Current Value | 2025 Reference |
|------|---------------|----------------|
| `credits/child/agi_limit.yaml` | $100,000 | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=11 |

| `credits/child/cdcc_fraction.yaml` | 20% | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=11 |

### 2.7 Property Tax Credit Files (4 files)
Use 2025 Form 538-H for all:

| File | Current Value | 2025 Reference |
|------|---------------|----------------|

### 2.8 Sales Tax Credit Files (4 files)

| `credits/sales_tax/age_minimum.yaml` | 65 | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=15 |

### 2.9 Credit List Files (2 files)

| File | 2025 Reference |
|------|----------------|
| `credits/refundable.yaml` | 2025 Form 511-EIC, 538-H, 538-S |
| `credits/nonrefundable.yaml` | 2025 Form 511-NR-Pkt#page=11 |

---

## Part 3: New Programs to Implement

The following Oklahoma tax credits could be modeled using existing PolicyEngine variables:

### 3.1 Scholarship-Granting Organization Credit (Form 511-CR)
**Description**: Credit for contributions to eligible scholarship-granting organizations
- **Amount**: 50% of contribution (75% if committed for additional year)
- **Maximum**: $1,000 individual / $2,000 joint / $100,000 business
- **Carryover**: 3 years
- **Reference**: [2025 Form 511-CR](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/tax-credits/511-CR.pdf)

**Implementation complexity**: Medium - requires new input variable for contributions

### 3.2 Parental Choice Tax Credit for Homeschool Expenses (Form 591-D)
**Description**: Credit for qualified homeschool expenses
- **Amount**: Qualified expenses
- **Maximum**: $1,000 per eligible student per year
- **Statewide cap**: $5 million annually (starting 2024)
- **Reference**: [Oklahoma Parental Choice Tax Credit Act](https://www.edchoice.org/school-choice/programs/oklahoma-parental-choice-tax-credit-act/)

**Implementation complexity**: Medium - requires new input variables for homeschool status and expenses

### 3.3 Electric Vehicle Credit
**Description**: One-time income tax credit for new alternative fuel vehicles
- **Amount**: Up to $5,500 (vehicles at or under 6,000 lbs GVWR)
- **Amount**: Up to $9,000 (vehicles 6,000-10,000 lbs GVWR)
- **Reference**: [Alternative Fuels Data Center](https://afdc.energy.gov/laws/all?state=OK)

**Implementation complexity**: Medium - requires new input variables for vehicle type/weight

### 3.4 Zero-Emission Facility Credit (Form 511-CR)
**Description**: Credit for production and sale of electricity from zero-emission facilities
- **Reference**: [2025 Form 511-CR](https://oklahoma.gov/content/dam/ok/en/tax/documents/forms/tax-credits/511-CR.pdf)

**Implementation complexity**: Low priority - not applicable to most individual filers

---

## Part 4: New Tests for 2025

### 4.1 Update Existing Test Files
Add 2025 test cases to all existing Oklahoma test files:
- `ok_income_tax_before_credits.yaml` - Test 2025 tax calculation
- `ok_standard_deduction.yaml` - Verify 2025 deduction amounts
- `ok_exemptions.yaml` - Verify 2025 exemption amounts
- `ok_pension_subtraction.yaml` - **Critical**: Test new $20,000 limit for 2024+
- `ok_military_retirement_exclusion.yaml` - Verify 100% exclusion continues
- `ok_ptc.yaml` - Test 2025 property tax credit
- `ok_stc.yaml` - Test 2025 sales tax credit

### 4.2 Critical Test: Pension Subtraction Increase
```yaml
- name: Oklahoma pension subtraction 2025 - increased limit
  period: 2025
  input:
    people:
      person:
        taxable_pension_income: 25_000
    tax_units:
      tax_unit:
        members: [person]
  output:
    ok_pension_subtraction: 20_000  # New $20,000 limit (was $10,000)
```

### 4.3 Integration Test
Add comprehensive 2025 integration test to `ok_integration.yaml` that tests full tax calculation pipeline.

---

## Part 5: Future Considerations (2026)

The implementation already includes 2026 rate changes from [HB 2764](https://www.oklegislature.gov/cf_pdf/2025-26%20ENR/hB/HB2764%20ENR.PDF):
- Top rate reduced from 4.75% to 4.5%
- Six brackets consolidated to three brackets
- Rate structure: 0%, 2.5%, 3.5%, 4.5%

These are already implemented in the rate files. Verify accuracy when 2026 approaches.

---

## Checklist

### Parameter Updates
- [ ] Update `pension_limit.yaml` with $20,000 for 2024+
- [ ] Add 2025 references to all 29 parameter files

### Documentation
- [ ] Verify all page numbers match 2025 forms
- [ ] Update any changed values

### Tests
- [ ] Add 2025 test cases for pension subtraction
- [ ] Add 2025 integration test
- [ ] Run full test suite

### New Programs (Optional)
- [ ] Evaluate priority of new credit implementations
- [ ] Create issues for high-priority credits

## Summary

This includes adding 2025 references (with page numbers) to all parameters, updating parameter values where they have changed, adding new 2025 integration tests, and implementing new programs that can be modeled with existing variables.

**Primary Source:** [2025 Virginia Form 760 Instructions](https://www.tax.virginia.gov/sites/default/files/vatax-pdf/2025-760-instructions.pdf)

---

## 1. Parameter Reference Updates (All Parameters Need 2025 References)

All parameters below require adding a reference to the 2025 Form 760 Instructions with the appropriate page number, regardless of whether the value changed.

### Tax Rates (`rates.yaml`)
- **Current values**: 2%/3%/5%/5.75% on $0/$3,000/$5,000/$17,000

  - Add 2025-01-01 entry: $0
  - Add reference: https://www.tax.virginia.gov/rebate

---

## 4. New Programs to Implement (Can Model with Existing Variables)

### High Priority (Commonly Claimed)

#### Credit for Taxes Paid to Another State
- **Type**: Non-refundable
- **Calculation**: Lesser of tax paid to other state or (VA tax x other state income / VA taxable income)
- **Variables needed**: `state_income_tax` (exists), `state_taxable_income` (exists)
- **Reference**: Form 760, Schedule OSC (page ~30)

### Medium Priority (Specific Populations)

#### Food Donation Tax Credit
- **Type**: Non-refundable
- **Amount**: 30% of fair market value of crops donated to nonprofit food bank
- **Cap**: $5,000 per year
- **Eligibility**: Farmers who donate crops they grow
- **Reference**: Code of Virginia 58.1-439.12:12

#### Firearm Safety Device Credit (Expanded for 2025)
- **Type**: Non-refundable
- **Amount**: Credit for purchase of firearm safety devices
- **2025 Change**: Now covers purchases from commercial retailers (previously only from federally licensed dealers)
- **Reference**: Code of Virginia 58.1-339.11

#### Livable Home Tax Credit
- **Type**: Non-refundable
- **Amount**: Up to $5,000 for accessibility improvements
- **Eligibility**: Homeowners making accessibility modifications
- **Reference**: Code of Virginia 58.1-339.7

---

## 5. New Tests for 2025

### Unit Tests to Create/Update

1. **Standard Deduction Tests** (`deductions/va_standard_deduction.yaml`)
   - Test single filer with $8,750 deduction
   - Test joint filer with $17,500 deduction

2. **EITC Tests** (`credits/eitc/va_refundable_eitc_if_claimed.yaml`)
   - Test 20% refundable match calculation
   - Test with various federal EITC amounts

3. **Military Benefit Subtraction Tests** (`subtractions/va_military_benefit_subtraction.yaml`)

issues.title: Create reform to separate dependent children from Virginia personal exemption
issues.body:
## Current Implementation

Virginia's personal exemption (`va_personal_exemption`) currently applies the same exemption amount to all persons in the tax unit - filers, spouses, and dependents alike:

- `va_personal_exemption_person.py` returns the flat exemption amount for each person
- `va_personal_exemption.py` sums all person-level exemptions

## Requested Reform

Create a reform similar to the Delaware dependent credit reform (PR #6889) that:

1. Separates dependent children exemption from the base personal exemption
2. Allows configurable parameters for the dependent children portion:
   - Exemption amount (can differ from filer exemption)
   - Age limit (optional)
   - Income phaseout (optional)
3. Modifies `va_personal_exemption` to calculate:
   - Base exemption (filer + spouse + older dependents)
   - Plus dependent children exemption (with separate parameters)

## Implementation Pattern

Follow the Delaware reform pattern in `policyengine_us/reforms/states/de/dependent_credit/de_dependent_credit_reform.py`:

1. Create parameters under `gov/contrib/states/va/dependent_exemption/`:
   - `amount.yaml` - exemption amount per dependent child
   - `age_limit/in_effect.yaml` - whether age limit applies
   - `age_limit/threshold.yaml` - age threshold
   - `in_effect.yaml` - whether reform is active

2. Create reform file at `policyengine_us/reforms/states/va/dependent_exemption/va_dependent_exemption_reform.py`:
   - `va_eligible_dependents_count` - count of eligible dependent children
   - `va_dependent_exemption` - exemption for dependent children
   - `va_older_dependents_count` - dependents not eligible for dependent exemption
   - Override `va_personal_exemption` to separate filer exemption from dependent exemption

3. Register reform in `reforms/reforms.py`

4. Add tests under `tests/policy/contrib/states/va/`

## References

- Delaware dependent credit reform: #6889
- Rhode Island exemption reform (similar work mentioned)
- Virginia exemption statute: https://law.lis.virginia.gov/vacodefull/title58.1/chapter3/article2/

issues.title: Fix Arizona Family Tax Credit income calculation per ARS 43-1073
issues.body:
## Summary

The Arizona Family Tax Credit eligibility uses the wrong income measure. Per ARS 43-1073, the income threshold should be:

> "Arizona adjusted gross income, **plus the amount subtracted for exemptions** under section 43-1023"

This means the Family Tax Credit should use `az_agi + az_exemptions`, not just `az_agi`.

## Current Implementation

**File:** `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/tax/income/credits/family_tax_credit/az_family_tax_credit_eligible.py`

```python
def formula(tax_unit, period, parameters):
    p = parameters(period).gov.states.az.tax.income.credits.family_tax_credits
    income = tax_unit("az_agi", period)  # <-- WRONG: should add back exemptions
    ...
    return income <= income_limit
```

## Correct Implementation

Per ARS 43-1073, the income for Family Tax Credit eligibility should be:
- Arizona AGI (which per ARS 43-1022 includes exemptions as subtractions)
- PLUS the amount subtracted for exemptions

So the correct income measure is: `az_agi + az_exemptions`

## Why This Matters

The current implementation understates income for Family Tax Credit purposes, potentially making people eligible who shouldn't be. For example:

- Person with Federal AGI of $22,000
- Arizona exemptions of $2,100 (aged)
- `az_agi` = ~$19,900 (after exemptions subtracted)
- **Current:** Uses $19,900 for eligibility
- **Correct:** Should use $22,000 ($19,900 + $2,100) for eligibility

## Suggested Fix

Update `az_family_tax_credit_eligible.py`:

```python
def formula(tax_unit, period, parameters):
    p = parameters(period).gov.states.az.tax.income.credits.family_tax_credits
    az_agi = tax_unit("az_agi", period)
    # Per ARS 43-1073: "Arizona adjusted gross income, plus the amount 
    # subtracted for exemptions under section 43-1023"
    exemptions = tax_unit("az_exemptions", period)
    income = az_agi + exemptions
    ...
    return income <= income_limit
```

## Files to Modify

- `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/tax/income/credits/family_tax_credit/az_family_tax_credit_eligible.py`
- Tests in `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/az/tax/income/credits/az_family_tax_credit_eligible.yaml`

## References

- [ARS 43-1073 - Family Income Tax Credit](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01073.htm)
- [ARS 43-1022 - Subtractions from Arizona gross income](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01022.htm) (confirms exemptions are part of AGI calculation)
- [ARS 43-1023 - Exemptions](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01023.htm)

## Instructions for Bot

To fix this issue:

1. Update `az_family_tax_credit_eligible.py` to add exemptions back to az_agi:
   ```python
   az_agi = tax_unit("az_agi", period)
   exemptions = tax_unit("az_exemptions", period)
   income = az_agi + exemptions
   ```

2. Add documentation/reference to ARS 43-1073 explaining why exemptions are added back

3. Update tests in `az_family_tax_credit_eligible.yaml` to verify the correct income is used

4. Run all Arizona tests:
   ```bash
   policyengine-core test policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/az/ -c policyengine_us
   ```

5. Add changelog entry describing the fix

issues.title: Fix Arizona AGI calculation - exemptions should not be included in AGI
issues.body:
## Summary

The current `az_agi` variable incorrectly subtracts Arizona exemptions (aged, blind, etc.) as part of AGI. Per Arizona Form 140 and tax statutes, exemptions are subtracted **after** AGI is calculated, not as part of AGI itself.

This causes issues for any calculation that uses `az_agi` expecting it to be true Arizona AGI.

## Current Implementation

**File:** `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/tax/income/az_agi.py`

```python
def formula(tax_unit, period, parameters):
    adjusted_gross_income = tax_unit("adjusted_gross_income", period)
    additions = tax_unit("az_additions", period)
    subtractions = tax_unit("az_subtractions", period)
    exemptions = tax_unit("az_exemptions", period)  # <-- WRONG

    return max_(
        0, adjusted_gross_income + additions - subtractions - exemptions  # <-- WRONG
    )
```

## What Arizona Form 140 Shows

| Line | Description | Formula |
|------|-------------|---------|
| 12 | Federal AGI | - |
| 13-36 | Additions and Subtractions | - |
| **37** | **Arizona AGI** | Fed AGI + additions - subtractions |
| 38-42 | Exemptions | - |
| 43 | AZ AGI minus exemptions | Line 37 - exemptions |
| 44 | Deductions | - |
| 45 | **Taxable Income** | Line 43 - deductions |

## Impact

### 1. Family Tax Credit (ARS 43-1073)
The statute says eligibility is based on:
> "Arizona adjusted gross income, **plus the amount subtracted for exemptions**"

This means the Family Tax Credit should use true Arizona AGI (before exemptions). But currently it uses `az_agi` which already has exemptions subtracted, resulting in **incorrect eligibility calculations**.

**File:** `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/tax/income/credits/family_tax_credit/az_family_tax_credit_eligible.py`

### 2. Any other variable using `az_agi`
Any variable expecting true Arizona AGI will get the wrong value.

## Suggested Fix

### Option 1: Rename and create new variable (Recommended)
1. Rename `az_agi` to `az_agi_less_exemptions` (or similar)
2. Create new `az_agi` that equals `Fed AGI + additions - subtractions` (no exemptions)
3. Update `az_taxable_income` to use `az_agi_less_exemptions`
4. Update `az_family_tax_credit_eligible` to use the new true `az_agi`

### Option 2: Fix in place
1. Remove exemptions from `az_agi` calculation
2. Create `az_agi_less_exemptions` for use in `az_taxable_income`
3. Update downstream variables accordingly

## Files to Modify

- `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/tax/income/az_agi.py`
- `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/tax/income/az_taxable_income.py`
- `policyengine_us/variables/gov/states/az/tax/income/credits/family_tax_credit/az_family_tax_credit_eligible.py`
- Tests in `policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/az/tax/income/`

## References

- [Arizona Form 140 Instructions](https://azdor.gov/forms/individual)
- [ARS 43-1073 - Family Income Tax Credit](https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01073.htm)
- Related PR: #6957 (Property Tax Credit fix)

## Instructions for Bot

To fix this issue:

1. Create a new variable `az_agi_less_exemptions` that equals `az_agi - az_exemptions` (using the corrected az_agi)

2. Update `az_agi.py` to NOT subtract exemptions:
   ```python
   return max_(0, adjusted_gross_income + additions - subtractions)
   ```

3. Update `az_taxable_income.py` to use the new flow:
   ```python
   az_agi = tax_unit("az_agi", period)
   exemptions = tax_unit("az_exemptions", period)
   deductions = tax_unit("az_deductions", period)
   return max_(0, az_agi - exemptions - deductions)
   ```

4. Update `az_family_tax_credit_eligible.py` - it should now work correctly with the fixed `az_agi`

5. Update tests in `az_agi.yaml` to reflect the new calculation (without exemptions)

6. Run all Arizona tests to ensure nothing breaks:
   ```bash
   policyengine-core test policyengine_us/tests/policy/baseline/gov/states/az/ -c policyengine_us
   ```

7. Add changelog entry describing the fix

prs.title: Restructure codebase into separate website and calculator apps
prs.body:
## Summary

Restructures the PolicyEngine app into a proper Turborepo monorepo with separate apps and shared packages.

### New Structure

```
policyengine-app-v2/
├── apps/
│   ├── website/           # policyengine.org (port 3000)
│   └── calculator/        # app.policyengine.org (port 3001)
├── packages/
│   ├── design-system/     # Shared UI components and design tokens
│   └── shared/            # Common utilities, hooks, routing
└── app/                   # DELETED - old monolithic app
```

### Key Changes

**Apps separation:**
- `apps/website/` - Static website with NO Redux, NO React Query (lightweight)
- `apps/calculator/` - Interactive calculator with full Redux + React Query stack

**Shared packages:**
- `@policyengine/design-system` - Design tokens, HomeHeader component, chart utilities
- `@policyengine/shared` - Country config, `useCurrentCountry` hook, geolocation routing, URL utilities

**Code consolidation:**
- Country labels consolidated to single source of truth in shared package
- HomeHeader refactored to "dumb" component accepting props (moved to design-system)
- Each app has thin wrapper components for app-specific navigation logic

**New utilities:**
- `replaceCountryInPath()` - Clean URL manipulation for country switching
- `COUNTRIES` / `WEBSITE_COUNTRIES` arrays for dropdowns
- `countryLabels` record for display names

**Testing:**
- Added organizations validation test (ensures all orgs have country IDs)
- Updated vitest.setup.ts with browser API mocks for Mantine components

### Before Merging

1. **Rebase after PR #540** - That PR adds dynamic port discovery which resolves the dev mode cross-app URL issue.

2. **Vercel Dashboard** - Configure Root Directory for each project:
   - `policyengine-website` → `apps/website`
   - `policyengine-calculator` → `apps/calculator`

### Documentation

See `repo-code-split-summary.md` for detailed breakdown of all changes.

## Test Plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` passes
- [x] `npm run packages:build` succeeds
- [x] Website tests pass (`npm test` in apps/website)
- [x] Website dev server runs on :3000
- [x] Calculator dev server runs on :3001

prs.title: Add fallback logic to correctly filter region for society-wide calculations
prs.body:
## Problem

  Economy-wide reports for US states incorrectly calculated using national data instead of region-specific data.

  Example: Montana CTC reform showed $13B (entire US) instead of $48M (Montana only).

 ## Root Cause

  In CalcOrchestrator.ts:319, the region parameter had incomplete fallback logic:

  // BEFORE (BUG):
  region = geography?.geographyId || config.countryId;

  Issue: During report calculation, if geography?.geographyId is undefined or empty (due to race conditions during async data loading or when the geography object isn't passed in config), it falls back directly to config.countryId ("us"), causing the API to calculate for the entire country instead of the specific region.

  API call: /us/economy/{reform}/over/{baseline}?region=us (should be ?region=mt)

 ## Solution

  Add sim1.populationId as fallback before config.countryId:

  // AFTER (FIX):
  region = geography?.geographyId || sim1.populationId || config.countryId;

  The simulation object always contains the correct populationId from the database, making it a reliable fallback when the geography object is unavailable or incomplete.

prs.title: Crash in policy creation
prs.body:
Fixes #383 

Thorough verification required.

RCA (Root Cause Analysis)

  Crash: TypeError: (char || "").match is not a function

  Location: ValueSetter.tsx - in the ValueInputBox component when rendering NumberInput (which uses react-number-format's NumericFormat component internally)

  Root Cause:
  Some parameters (specifically HMRC IncomeTax parameters) have non-numeric values (likely objects, arrays, or other complex types) in their metadata. When a user clicks on
  these parameters in the policy parameter selector, the ValueInputBox component tries to pass these non-numeric values directly to Mantine's NumberInput component.

  The NumberInput uses react-number-format's NumericFormat internally, which expects string or number values. When it receives a non-numeric value, it attempts to call
  .match() on it (for parsing/formatting), which fails because .match() only exists on strings.

  Trigger:
  Clicking on specific parameter leaves in the policy parameter selector tree (HMRC IncomeTax and a few other params) during isolated policy creation flow.

  Fix:
  Added type guard in ValueSetter.tsx line 536-538 to ensure the value passed to NumberInput is always a number:
  const numericValue = typeof value === 'number' ? value : 0;
  const displayValue = isPercentage ? numericValue * 100 : numericValue;

  This prevents non-numeric values from reaching the NumberInput/NumericFormat component.

prs.title: Store household calculation outputs in Simulation records instead of Report
prs.body:
Fixes #226 

  Problem

  Household calculation outputs were incorrectly stored in Report.output due to economy calculation limitations being applied to household calculations. Ideally, each Simulation should store its own output.

___

Solution Overview

  Implemented a callback-based flow where the Handler manages per-simulation execution and the Manager orchestrates storage via callbacks. 

___

  Architecture Changes

  **Added simulationIds to CalculationMeta**

  Why: The handler needs to know which simulations to run calculations for. Critical for the waterfall pattern (direct URL navigation/page refresh) where metadata must be reconstructed from the report.

  **Handler Executes Multiple Simulations**

  Why: Each simulation needs its own calculation with its own policy (baseline vs reform).

  - Unique tracking keys: Uses ${reportId}-sim-${simulationId} to avoid handler collisions
  - Positional mapping: simulationIds[0] → baseline, simulationIds[1] → reform (matches report structure)
  - Synthetic progress: Aggregates progress across all simulations for a report
  - Callback coordination: Wraps onSimulationComplete callback to detect when all simulations are done and trigger onComplete

  **Manager Provides Storage Callbacks**

  Why: Separation of concerns - Handler handles calculation logic, Manager handles storage/side effects (dependency inversion).

  - Dependency injection via callbacks: Standard pattern (used in React, Express, event emitters)
  - Progressive updates: Each simulation output stored immediately via onSimulationComplete
  - Report completion: Final report status updated via onComplete after all simulations finish

___

  Related Backend Changes (policyengine-api)

  - Service: Added update_simulation_output() to SimulationService
  - Routes: Added PATCH /{country}/simulation endpoint (ID in payload, not URL)
  - Database: Updated initialise.sql and initialise_local.sql with output_json column

___

  **The Complete Flow**

  1. Manager calls Service's executeCalculation() with callbacks
  2. Service routes to Handler based on calculation type
  3. Handler loops through meta.simulationIds
  4. For each simulation:
    - Handler executes calculation → calls onSimulationComplete → Manager stores in Simulation
  5. After all simulations complete:
    - Handler calls onComplete → Manager stores Report with output={}

prs.title: Add vercel.json for SPA routing configuration
prs.body:
##  Problem

  Direct navigation to routes (e.g., /us, /us/policies) was returning 404 errors on Vercel deployment, despite working locally. Only the root path / was accessible.

##  Root Cause

  Vercel serves our built files as static assets. When you navigate directly to /us, Vercel looks for a file at /us/index.html which doesn't exist (we only have /index.html). The browser never loads our React app, so React Router never gets a chance to handle the routing.

 ## Solution Attempted: React Router Framework Mode

  We initially tried using the @vercel/react-router preset, which Vercel recommends for React Router apps. However, this preset requires React Router to be used in framework mode, which is fundamentally different from how our app is structured:

  Our App (Data Mode):
  - Uses createBrowserRouter for client-side routing
  - Routes defined programmatically in Router.tsx
  - Standard React SPA architecture
  - Vite handles the build process directly

  Framework Mode Requirements:
  - File-based routing (app/routes/*.tsx)
  - Special app/root.tsx entry point
  - Routes configuration in app/routes.ts
  - React Router controls the entire build pipeline
  - Designed for SSR/SSG, not traditional SPAs

##  Final Solution: vercel.json

  Added a simple vercel.json configuration that tells Vercel to serve index.html for all routes:

  ```
{
    "rewrites": [{ "source": "/(.*)", "destination": "/" }]
  }
```

## Testing

  - Build passes locally
  - Routes work in local development
  - Direct navigation works on Vercel preview URL
  - All major routes: /us, /uk, /us/policies, /us/populations, etc. work

##  Note for Future

  If we ever want to adopt React Router's framework mode (for SSR, better code splitting, etc.), we would need to restructure the entire app. For now, the vercel.json approach seems to be the best solution for our SPA architecture.

prs.title: IP-based Country Detection for Auto-redirect
prs.body:
Implements automatic country detection and redirect at root path (`/`) using IP geolocation.

  ### Implementation
  - **Primary provider:** ipapi.co (30k free requests/month, no API key required)
  - **Fallback:** Browser language detection
  - **Cache:** 4-hour localStorage TTL for traveling users
  - **Note:** ipinfo.io provider tested but not active (50k free tier available if needed)

  ### Performance Testing
  Tested detection timing from initial page load:
  - IP detection: ~333ms
  - Total time to redirect: ~4.8s (mostly React app initialization)

  ### Architecture
  - Chain of responsibility pattern for provider fallbacks
  - Geolocation service under `/routing` since it's routing-specific
  - Clean separation: providers handle detection, service orchestrates, component handles UI

  ### Why ipapi.co
  - Larger free tier than alternatives
  - Simple country-only endpoint (2 bytes vs full JSON)
  - No API key complexity for development
  - Reliable ~300ms response times

reviews.title: feat: Allow multiple instances of the dev server to run simultaneously
reviews.body:
## Summary

- Adds automatic port discovery for dev servers, allowing multiple instances to run simultaneously
- Creates a launcher script (`scripts/dev-server.mjs`) that finds available ports starting from 3000
- Ports are automatically passed to Vite via environment variables
- Each instance gets its own consecutive port pair (e.g., 3000/3001, 3002/3003)

## How it works

When running `make dev`:
1. The launcher script checks ports starting from 3000
2. It detects occupied ports by attempting TCP connections on both IPv4 and IPv6
3. Once two consecutive available ports are found, it passes them to the Vite dev servers
4. The vite config reads `WEBSITE_PORT` and `CALCULATOR_PORT` and configures servers accordingly
5. Cross-app URLs are derived from these ports automatically

## Usage

```bash
# Terminal 1
make dev
# → "Dev servers: Website :3000, Calculator :3001"

# Terminal 2 (while first is running)
make dev
# → "Dev servers: Website :3002, Calculator :3003"
```

## Test plan

- [x] Run `make dev` in one terminal - verify website on :3000, calculator on :3001
- [x] Run `make dev` in second terminal - verify it auto-discovers :3002/:3003
- [x] Verify cross-app navigation works correctly (website links to its paired calculator)

reviews.title: Add monorepo structure with design system and app split
reviews.body:
## Summary

This PR implements a monorepo architecture that splits the PolicyEngine app into two separate deployable applications:

- **Website** (`policyengine.org`) - Homepage, blog/research, team, donate pages
- **Calculator** (`app.policyengine.org`) - Interactive policy simulator, household builder, reports

### Key Changes

#### Architecture
- **Separate entry points**: `main.website.tsx` and `main.calculator.tsx`
- **Separate routers**: `WebsiteRouter.tsx` and `CalculatorRouter.tsx`
- **Separate HTML files**: `website.html` and `calculator.html`
- **Build-time app selection**: `VITE_APP_MODE` env var controls which app is built

#### Cross-App Navigation
- Added `WEBSITE_URL` and `CALCULATOR_URL` constants in `src/constants/index.ts`
- Environment-aware URLs (relative in dev, absolute in prod)
- Updated `HeaderLogo` to navigate from calculator → website homepage

#### Vercel Configuration
- Root `vercel.json` for website (`VITE_APP_MODE=website`)
- `calculator/vercel.json` for calculator app (`VITE_APP_MODE=calculator`)
- Proper rewrites to serve SPA from correct HTML entry point

### Files Changed

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `calculator/vercel.json` | Vercel config for calculator project |
| `vercel.json` | Vercel config for website project |
| `app/vite.config.mjs` | Build config with app mode selection |
| `app/src/main.website.tsx` | Website entry point |
| `app/src/main.calculator.tsx` | Calculator entry point |
| `app/src/WebsiteApp.tsx` | Website app component |
| `app/src/CalculatorApp.tsx` | Calculator app component |
| `app/src/WebsiteRouter.tsx` | Website routes |
| `app/src/CalculatorRouter.tsx` | Calculator routes |
| `app/src/constants/index.ts` | Cross-app URL constants |
| `app/src/components/homeHeader/HeaderLogo.tsx` | Fixed to use anchor for cross-app nav |

## Pre-Merge Checklist

- [x] Preview deployments tested for both apps
- [x] Cross-app navigation works (website → calculator, calculator → website)
- [x] HeaderLogo tests updated and passing
- [x] `policyengine-calculator` Vercel project Root Directory set to `calculator`

## Post-Merge Steps

1. Verify both Vercel projects trigger production deployments
2. Test production URLs:
   - `https://policyengine.org/us` loads website homepage
   - `https://app.policyengine.org/us` loads calculator dashboard
3. Test cross-app navigation in production

## Expected Outcome

After merge:
- `policyengine.org` serves the Website app (homepage, research, team, etc.)
- `app.policyengine.org` serves the Calculator app (dashboard, reports, simulations, etc.)
- Logo click in calculator navigates to website homepage
- "Calculate my taxes" buttons in website navigate to calculator

## Architecture Diagram

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Monorepo Root                             │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                    │                           │
        ┌───────────┴───────────┐   ┌───────────┴───────────┐
        ▼                       │   ▼                       │
┌───────────────────┐           │   ┌───────────────────┐   │
│  policyengine.org │           │   │app.policyengine.org│  │
│  (Website)        │           │   │  (Calculator)      │  │
├───────────────────┤           │   ├───────────────────┤   │
│ vercel.json       │           │   │ calculator/       │   │
│ VITE_APP_MODE=    │           │   │   vercel.json     │   │
│   website         │           │   │ VITE_APP_MODE=    │   │
└───────────────────┘           │   │   calculator      │   │
        │                       │   └───────────────────┘   │
        ▼                       │           │               │
┌───────────────────┐           │           ▼               │
│ website.html      │           │   ┌───────────────────┐   │
│ main.website.tsx  │           │   │ calculator.html   │   │
│ WebsiteApp        │           │   │ main.calculator   │   │
│ WebsiteRouter     │           │   │ CalculatorApp     │   │
└───────────────────┘           │   │ CalculatorRouter  │   │
                                │   └───────────────────┘   │
```

## Test Plan

- [x] `npm run vitest` - HeaderLogo tests pass
- [x] `npm run lint` - No errors
- [x] `npm run typecheck` - No errors
- [x] Preview deployment for website works
- [x] Preview deployment for calculator works
- [x] Cross-app links resolve correctly

reviews.title: IP-based Country Detection for Auto-redirect
reviews.body:
Implements automatic country detection and redirect at root path (`/`) using IP geolocation.

  ### Implementation
  - **Primary provider:** ipapi.co (30k free requests/month, no API key required)
  - **Fallback:** Browser language detection
  - **Cache:** 4-hour localStorage TTL for traveling users
  - **Note:** ipinfo.io provider tested but not active (50k free tier available if needed)

  ### Performance Testing
  Tested detection timing from initial page load:
  - IP detection: ~333ms
  - Total time to redirect: ~4.8s (mostly React app initialization)

  ### Architecture
  - Chain of responsibility pattern for provider fallbacks
  - Geolocation service under `/routing` since it's routing-specific
  - Clean separation: providers handle detection, service orchestrates, component handles UI

  ### Why ipapi.co
  - Larger free tier than alternatives
  - Simple country-only endpoint (2 bytes vs full JSON)
  - No API key complexity for development
  - Reliable ~300ms response times
